readme.markdown:
# gdharness

**An agent cannot see a running game.** It reads your scripts and guesses at the rest: whether the
button is on screen, whether the panel updated, whether that error mattered.

gdharness makes the engine answerable instead. What the screen says, where a control is, what a
property reads right now, what the console printed, what broke and on which line.

## Install

Hand this to your agent:

```text
Install gdharness here by following https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness/agent.md,
then tell me what it asked you to recommend back to me.
```

Or do it yourself, and pick your harness:
[aureliolo.github.io/gdharness](https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness).

## The loop it exists for

```jsonc
editor_run      { "op": "start", "projectPath": "C:/games/hall" }
runtime_inspect { "op": "find", "says": "Buy" }              // the button, by the word on it
runtime_input   { "op": "click", "nodePath": "/root/Hall/Ledger/BuyButton" }
runtime_inspect { "op": "text", "nodePath": "/root/Hall/Ledger" }   // what the panel says now
editor_output   { "projectPath": "C:/games/hall" }           // errors and warnings, with backtraces
```

The open editor plays the game, so its debugger holds it, which is what lets you set a breakpoint
and read the variables in scope when it stops.

Every answer is read back out of the engine after the fact, never echoed from the request. A tool
that cannot answer says which state it is in and what would change it, rather than answering
emptily, so a call that succeeded is a call that was understood.

## At a glance

|           |                                                                                      |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Needs     | Godot 4.7 or newer, Node 22 or newer. Runs under Bun 1.4 too.                        |
| Surface   | 30 tools named `domain_verb`, 4 `godot://` resources and 3 prompts                   |
| Reaches   | The editor that is open, a game it is playing, and the project on disk               |
| Harnesses | 35, written inside the project wherever the harness has a project config             |
| Skill     | Written to `.agents/skills`, which every major harness reads                         |
| Install   | npm, or a Sigstore-signed archive with an SBOM, SLSA Build Level 3                   |
| Proven    | Every tool driven against Godot 4.7.2 in CI, on Windows, Linux and macOS             |
| Status    | 1.0: every release is a patch. [What a bump means](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md#versions) |

Older 4.x is likely to work and is not tested.

## Documentation

[aureliolo.github.io/gdharness](https://aureliolo.github.io/gdharness): installing it, how the
parts connect, and every tool, op and argument.

[SECURITY.md](.github/SECURITY.md) is how to report something.
[CONTRIBUTING.md](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) is what a change has to clear.

## Project

Fork of [GoPeak](https://github.com/HaD0Yun/Doyunha-Gopeak) v2.3.9, September 2026, MIT: the
original MCP server [godot-mcp](https://github.com/Coding-Solo/godot-mcp) by
[Solomon Elias](https://github.com/Coding-Solo), GoPeak by [HaD0Yun](https://github.com/HaD0Yun),
and completely reworked since to be hardened, condensed and more streamlined.

Not affiliated with the Godot Foundation.

readme.markdown:
# LinkedIn Profile Finder - Email to LinkedIn URL

Turn an email address into the person's public LinkedIn profile, with a confidence score on every match. Paste one email or a whole list and get back a clean table of LinkedIn URLs for your CRM, outreach or recruiting pipeline. **No LinkedIn login, no cookies, nothing tied to your account.**

Available as an [Apify Actor](https://apify.com/anshumanatrey/linkedin-harvester). $0.005 per email checked plus $0.02 per confident match. Works with no API keys; free Brave Search and Groq keys widen coverage.

## What you get

- **Email in, best-match LinkedIn URL out**, with a 0 to 100% confidence score on every row so you know which matches to trust.
- **Bulk or one-off.** A single address or thousands, one result row each.
- **Pay for results.** Half a cent per email checked; the match fee applies only when a URL clears your confidence gate.
- **Public information only.** GitHub commit authors, Gravatar, PGP keyservers and handle probes on 8 platforms. No data broker, no private database.
- **Account-safe.** It never logs into LinkedIn or touches your session, so there is nothing to get flagged.

## Who it's for

- **Sales and growth:** enrich inbound leads and sign-ups with the right LinkedIn profile before you reach out.
- **Recruiting:** turn a list of candidate emails into LinkedIn profiles.
- **RevOps / CRM:** clean, verify and backfill contact records at scale.
- **Founders and operators:** see who actually emailed you.

## How to use it

1. Paste a single email, or a list of emails. The form comes prefilled with two demo addresses; replace them with yours.
2. Leave **Check public profiles** on. It recovers the name and a cross-platform handle, which is what resolves a URL without a search key.
3. Pick a matching mode. **Balanced** is the default and works for most lists.
4. Optional: add your free Brave Search and Groq keys for web-search corroboration and AI name-splitting.
5. Hit **Start**. Results appear in the dataset, one row per email.

### Matching modes

| Mode | Best for |
|---|---|
| **No AI** | Fastest and free. Accepts only the clear, unambiguous matches. |
| **Balanced** (recommended) | The default. Spends extra effort only on the uncertain matches. |
| **Full AI** | Highest match rate. Works hardest on every email. Needs a Groq key. |

## What does the output look like?

This is the real dataset from a run on 2026-09-12 (build 0.1.5, no API keys, default settings). Six emails, 25 seconds, 1 GB of memory.

| Email | Found | LinkedIn URL | Confidence | Confident | Name | Name from | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| anshumanatrey@gmail.com | yes | linkedin.com/in/anshumanatrey | 97% | yes | Anshuman Atrey | GitHub commit | handle confirmed on 4 platforms |
| satya.nadella@microsoft.com | yes | linkedin.com/in/satyanadella | 78% | no | Satya Nadella | address | handle confirmed on 4 platforms |
| jensen.huang@nvidia.com | yes | linkedin.com/in/jensenhuang | 78% | no | Jensen Huang | address | handle confirmed on 6 platforms |
| tim.cook@apple.com | yes | linkedin.com/in/timcook | 78% | no | Tim Cook | address | handle confirmed on 3 platforms |
| sayujpillai63@gmail.com | yes | linkedin.com/in/sayuj63 | 64% | no | Sayuj Pillai | GitHub commit | handle confirmed on 1 platform |
| info@stripe.com | no | | 0% | no | | | role mailbox, no candidate |

**Confident** means the row cleared the 80% gate. Those are the only rows that carry the match fee. Rows between 50% and 79% are possible matches, returned free with their score, for you to verify before use.

One row as JSON (the `signals` block is what the scorer saw):

```json
{
  "email": "anshumanatrey@gmail.com",
  "found": true,
  "linkedin_url": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/anshumanatrey",
  "confidence": 0.97,
  "passes_gate": true,
  "gate_threshold": 0.8,
  "derived_name": "Anshuman Atrey",
  "name_source": "github_commit",
  "source": "handle_pivot",
  "evidence": "handle 'anshumanatrey' confirmed on 4 platform(s) -> likely LinkedIn slug",
  "signals": {
    "names": [{"value": "Anshuman Atrey", "source": "github_commit"}],
    "handles": ["anshumanatrey"],
    "confirmed_socials": ["GitHub: https://github.com/anshumanatrey", "YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@anshumanatrey", "Telegram: https://t.me/anshumanatrey"]
  }
}
```

## What does it cost?

Pay per event. Platform compute is included in the prices.

| Event | Price | When it is charged |
|---|---|---|
| Run start | $0.01 | Once per run |
| Email checked | $0.005 | Once per email, found or not |
| Confident match | $0.02 | Only when a URL clears your confidence gate (80% by default) |

Typical jobs:

| Job | Cost |
|---|---|
| The 6-email run above (1 confident match) | $0.06 |
| 1 email, confident match | $0.035 |
| 100 emails, 30 confident matches | $1.11 |
| 1,000 emails, 250 confident matches | $10.01 |

The 6-email run used 0.0069 compute units at the 1 GB default, about 4 seconds per email.

## How good are the matches?

Measured on the run above: 5 of 6 addresses resolved to a URL, 1 above the gate, and the role mailbox was correctly skipped.

- **Work emails** (`first.last@company.com`) give the name from the address itself. The handle probes then look for that name as a handle across GitHub, GitLab, dev.to, npm, Gravatar, Linktree, About.me, YouTube and Telegram. Three or more hits put the match at 78%.
- **Personal addresses** resolve when the person has a public developer or social footprint. A GitHub commit author name or a Gravatar display name is authoritative and lifts confidence to the high 90s.
- **Over the gate.** A confident match needs a name from an authoritative source plus a handle that is consistent across platforms. A free Brave Search key adds a web-search check on each candidate, the designed way to lift 78% matches over the gate.
- **Not found is a clean not found**, never a confident guess. Role mailboxes (info@, support@, sales@) are skipped rather than probed.

readme.markdown:
# RooYun Skill & MCP

让 Claude Code、Codex、Cursor 等 AI 编程助手，用一句话驱动 [RooYun](https://www.rooyun.com/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme)：AI 漫剧与 AI 短剧的创作工作台。

> 「把这个剧本做成分镜工程」→ Agent 在 RooYun 里建好项目，拆出角色、场景、道具和分镜卡片，报价后生成分镜图和视频，产物自动落回画布。

产出不是一堆散文件，而是**一张你可以接着手工编辑的无限画布**。

[English](README.en.md) · [Agent 接入说明](https://www.rooyun.com/developers?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) · [AI 漫剧教程](https://www.rooyun.com/learn?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme)

---

## 选一种接入方式

最简单的做法是按官网 [Agent 接入](https://www.rooyun.com/developers?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme) 页操作：把那一页发给你的 AI 编程助手，它会自己装好、自己登录。下面是同样的几种方式，前两种直接从官网安装，不需要 GitHub。

| 方式 | 适合谁 | 怎么用 |
|---|---|---|
| **远程 MCP** | Claude Code、Cursor、Cline 等 MCP 客户端 | 填一个 URL 和一枚令牌 |
| **从官网安装 Skill** | Claude Code、Codex、WorkBuddy 等任何有 shell 的 Agent | 一条命令下载解压 |
| **Claude Code 插件**（可选） | 想用插件方式管理、随插件更新的 Claude Code 用户 | 从本仓库安装，内容与官网下载一致 |

### 1. 远程 MCP

服务地址：`https://www.rooyun.com/api/mcp`（Streamable HTTP），鉴权头 `Authorization: Bearer <令牌>`。令牌在 [个人中心 → API 访问](https://www.rooyun.com/profile#api) 创建。

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http rooyun https://www.rooyun.com/api/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer <你的令牌>"
```

Cursor、Codex、Cline、Cherry Studio 等客户端的配置见 [docs/mcp-clients.md](docs/mcp-clients.md)。

### 2. 从官网安装 Skill

Skill 比 MCP 多了本地脚本：能上传本地素材、批量下载产物、在本地拼接成片。有完整版和精简版，**二选一安装**（两者都会响应「用 RooYun 生成…」，同时装会抢着触发）：

- **完整版 `rooyun`**：按「剧本 → 角色/场景/道具 → 分镜 → 定嗓 → 生成」的固定流程搭工程，带 15 条工作流纪律。
- **精简版 `rooyun-cli`**：只给能力地图，提示词和先后顺序由你决定，提示词原样提交。

```bash
# 完整版（精简版把地址换成 "https://www.rooyun.com/api/skill/bundle?variant=cli"）
curl -fL "https://www.rooyun.com/api/skill/bundle" -o rooyun-skill.zip
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills
unzip -o rooyun-skill.zip -d ~/.claude/skills
```

装好后重启 Claude Code，对它说「登录 RooYun」：它会运行登录命令并打开浏览器，你在 RooYun 页面点一次「授权」即可，令牌保存在本机 `~/.rooyun/credentials.json`。之后用 `node ~/.claude/skills/rooyun/scripts/dj.mjs update` 更新。

Codex 等读 `AGENTS.md` 的工具：把 [`AGENTS.snippet.md`](plugins/rooyun/skills/rooyun/AGENTS.snippet.md) 粘进项目的 `AGENTS.md`。完整的安装、权限和环境变量说明见 skill 自带的 [README](plugins/rooyun/skills/rooyun/README.md)。命令行工具 `scripts/dj.mjs` 零依赖，需要 Node.js 18 或更高版本，macOS、Linux、Windows 通用。

### 3. Claude Code 插件（可选）

和官网下载的是同一份 Skill，区别只是用插件命令安装和更新：

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add DeepHiveAI/rooyun-skill
claude plugin install rooyun@rooyun        # 精简版：rooyun-cli@rooyun
```

更新：`claude plugin marketplace update rooyun`，再 `claude plugin update rooyun@rooyun`。

国内访问 GitHub 慢的话，第一条命令换成 Gitee 镜像，其余不变：

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add https://gitee.com/yichuanWorks/rooyun-skill.git
```

本仓库还提供 `rooyun-mcp` 插件，只接上面的远程 MCP，安装时按提示填入令牌（保存在系统安全存储里）。

也可以不装插件，直接把 [`plugins/rooyun/skills/rooyun/`](plugins/rooyun/skills/rooyun/) 整个目录拷进 `~/.claude/skills/`，效果和从官网安装一样。

---

## 能做什么

- **搭工程**：建项目和画布，建角色设定板、场景卡、道具板、分镜视频卡，连线、改卡、自动布局。
- **读剧本出结构**：剧本拆成角色、场景、道具和逐镜分镜，改完再落回画布。
- **生成内容**：文生图、图生图、图生视频、首尾帧、参考图生视频、数字人口播、配音、音乐、音效、视频高清、视频转白模，产物自动落回指定卡片。
- **角色一致性**：定妆照作为参考图贯穿全剧；试镜定嗓，同一角色全剧一把嗓子。
- **白模换角**：把一段现成视频转成白模，再让新角色复刻它的动作、走位和运镜。
- **对标分析**：解析一条参考视频的分镜结构和叙事功能，改编成同结构、不同内容的新段落。

name: PromptSpend
description: LLM pricing where every rate carries its source and the date it was last confirmed.

readme.markdown: Know the tab before you build. Estimate, compare and understand what an AI feature will cost — from a catalog that re-checks itself every morning, so the numbers are never a year out of date. → Open PromptSpend  ·  free  ·  open source  ·  no accounts, no ads  ·  Writing: What LLM Cost Calculators Get Wrong  ·  September 2026 Price Movement Report https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6bfecd10-84a9-408b-b08c-ff9481648692 1 minute 37 — press play, and hit 🔊 to unmute (GitHub starts videos silent).  ·  Download the MP4 --- ## Why this exists Every LLM cost calculator on the web has the same failure mode: it is a snapshot. Someone builds it, hard-codes a dozen model prices, and within a few months the entire premise is wrong — the models it compares have been superseded and the prices it quotes no longer exist. PromptSpend is built the other way round. **The pricing pipeline is the product**; the calculator is what sits on top of it. Every morning a GitHub Action re-fetches the catalog from independent sources, merges them under an explicit trust order, runs sanity checks, and either commits the result or opens a pull request for a human. Capture patterns are family-level, so a brand-new model version is picked up automatically without anyone touching code. ## What it does - **Receipt** — copy a fully visible, one-response cost-audit object into an existing AI conversation. It estimates the visible workload, retrieves current PromptSpend prices, names the two largest cost drivers and suggests cheaper models worth testing without pretending price proves equal quality. - **Estimate** — describe one interaction (paste your real prompt or move the sliders), set your scale, and see the monthly, yearly, per-user and margin numbers for up to four models side by side. - **Compare** — every tracked model on a price-versus-capability value map, plus a sortable catalog you can select from directly, with the source and verification date for every row. - **Learn** — seven short interactive lessons on tokens, why output costs more, how wide the price spread is, compounding chat history, hidden reasoning tokens, caching and batching, and how the data pipeline works. - **Free tiers** — which providers let a new account start without paying, card rules, limits and whether free use trains their models, quoted word for word from each vendor's own pages with a link and date on every fact, and re-checked each morning. One comparison page and one page per provider; see [docs/FREE_TIERS.md](docs/FREE_TIERS.md). - **Data & Alerts** — pipeline health, full provenance for every number with a link to the vendor page it came from, what is currently flagged, and four ways to hear about a price change: an Atom feed, the repository's own pull requests, browser push, and an email digest. ### Price alerts Opt-in, and off unless a deployment is configured for them. Browser push stores nothing personal — a push subscription is an opaque URL the browser issues. Email is double opt-in with one-click unsubscribe, and stores your address, the models you follow, and the date you asked; nothing else. Either channel can watch the whole catalog or just the models you pick. The delivery service is a Cloudflare Worker in [`worker/`](worker), with the push payload encryption written out against RFC 8291 and checked byte for byte against the RFC's own worked example. [docs/ALERTS.md](docs/ALERTS.md) has the architecture, the cost model and the domain cutover. ## Things it does that most calculators get wrong | | | | ---------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | **Output is priced separately** | Output typically costs 3–5× input. Averaging the two, as many calculators do, understates most real workloads. | | **Chat history compounds** | Turn _N_ re-sends turns 1…*N*−1 as input, so conversation cost grows with the square of the turn count. | | **Tokenizers differ per family** | The same pasted text is counted with each model's own tokenizer — exactly (js-tiktoken, run in your browser) for OpenAI-family models and with a clearly labelled calibrated ratio elsewhere. | | **Caching is not free** | Cache _writes_ cost 1.25× input at both OpenAI and Anthropic. Counting only the cheaper reads reports a saving your invoice will not have, so writes are billed and caching is off by default. | | **Long context costs more** | Above 272K input tokens OpenAI bills the whole request at 2× input and 1.5× output. Tiers apply per request, so a conversation can cross over partway through. | | **Reasoning tokens are billable** | A multiplier for hidden thinking tokens, because the visible answer is not what you pay for. | | **Promotional pricing expires** | Introductory rates apply only inside their window, and the engine takes a date. | | **Assumptions are visible** | Every non-published number used in a calculation is listed under the results, not buried — and so is what the prices do not cover. …

readme.markdown:
# Speak To Your Database: Odoo MCP server for ChatGPT and Claude

**Odoo, PostgreSQL & MySQL MCP server for Claude and ChatGPT. Ask your business data in plain words, from the AI app you already use. Real numbers, computed read-only from your data.**

STYD is a hosted MCP server. Connect it once to Claude, ChatGPT, Le Chat, VS Code or any app that supports remote MCP servers, then ask things like:

- "How much revenue did we make last month, compared with the month before?"
- "Which customer invoices are overdue, and how much does each customer owe?"
- "Show all sales orders grouped by customer and status, with the number of orders, the total amount and the date range."
- "Top 10 products by sales this year"
- "Why did sales drop this month?"

Follow-ups work too: after the sales orders question, ask *"and only the confirmed ones?"* and STYD keeps the same grouping.

STYD works out the answer from your data and sends back the numbers, with the period and the definition it used (for example, *revenue = posted customer invoices, excluding tax*).

- Website: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com
- MCP endpoint: `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`
- Demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZffAbynuc0
- Docs: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp
- Odoo MCP guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

> This repository holds the public setup guide and the registry file. STYD itself is a hosted service; its source code is not public.

---

## Odoo MCP connector

STYD is an Odoo MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP apps. Ask about sales, invoices, unpaid amounts, customers, products and stock in plain words, and get the figures with what was counted, over which period and with which filters.

- **Odoo 15 to 20**, on Odoo Online, Odoo.sh or your own server.
- **Two ways to connect:** an Odoo API key (Online, Odoo.sh, on-premise) or the free STYD Bridge module (Odoo.sh, on-premise).
- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo.
- **Nothing to install on your computer:** STYD is hosted, and your AI app signs in to your STYD account.
- **Several companies:** each company stays in its own workspace, and every answer names the one it comes from.

Example questions: *"Which customers owe us the most, and how much is overdue?"*, *"Top 5 products by quantity sold this quarter"*, *"Compare this month's sales with the same month last year."*

Full guide: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/odoo-mcp

## Try it in 2 minutes

1. Add the connector to your AI app (see below).
2. Sign in to STYD when your app asks. The free plan includes sample data, so you can ask questions straight away.
3. When you are ready, connect your own Odoo, PostgreSQL or MySQL database at https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/connections.

## Set up in your AI app

### Claude (web, desktop, mobile)

Open **Settings → Connectors**, search the directory for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Connect**.
Directory page: https://claude.ai/directory/speak-to-your-database

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http styd https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and sign in.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette, choose **HTTP**, and paste `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. Or add this to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "styd": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Start the server, sign in when VS Code asks, then use Copilot Chat in **Agent** mode.

### Le Chat (Mistral)

Add a custom MCP connector with the URL `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`, then sign in to STYD when asked.

### ChatGPT

Open **Plugins** in ChatGPT, search for **Speak To Your Database**, and click **Install plugin**. Sign in to STYD when asked.
Plugin page: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae

### Cursor and other apps

Any app that supports remote MCP servers with OAuth sign-in can use `https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/mcp`. For Cursor and apps without sign-in support, use a workspace API key: see https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/docs/mcp/other-apps.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_workspaces` | Lists the STYD workspaces (companies) you belong to |
| `list_connections` | Lists the data sources in a workspace: Odoo, PostgreSQL, MySQL, sample data |
| `describe_available_data` | Shows what a connection can answer, with example questions |
| `ask_question` | Asks one business question and returns the answer computed from your data |
| `get_answer` | Fetches the result of a longer-running question |

Every answer names the workspace it comes from, so data from different companies is never mixed.

## Security

STYD reads your data; it never changes it.

- **Read-only:** STYD cannot create, change or delete anything in Odoo or your databases.
- **Secrets protected:** database passwords and API keys are stored encrypted and never shown back.
- **Standard sign-in:** AI apps connect through OAuth. You approve each app on a STYD consent page, and you can revoke it at any time.
- **Uploaded files checked** with a malware scan before use.
- **Backups** with an encrypted off-site copy.
- **Abuse protection** and rate limits.
- **Not used for training:** your data and questions are not used to train AI models.

Details: https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/security and https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/privacy

Need STYD on your own server, with nothing leaving your network? See https://speaktoyourdatabase.com/private.

## Registry

STYD is published in the official MCP Registry as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/styd` (the [`server.json`](server.json) in this repository) and as `com.speaktoyourdatabase/odoo-mcp` (the Odoo MCP connector entry).

Also listed in the [ChatGPT plugin directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac9e3034d488191bd0b9a624cb1f0ae), the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/direc

readme.markdown:
# Serpier MCP server

[Serpier](https://serpier.com) is an SEO platform for marketing teams and agencies. The Serpier MCP server lets an AI assistant work in your Serpier account: monitor your brand's AI Visibility, track published articles, and find publishers and manage link-building orders.

This is a hosted, remote MCP server. There is nothing to install or run. This repository holds the connection details and the metadata that MCP registries and directories read.

| | |
|---|---|
| Server URL | `https://app.serpier.com/api/mcp` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Authentication | OAuth 2.1 with PKCE. Dynamic Client Registration and Client ID Metadata Documents are supported. |
| Registry name | [`com.serpier/serpier`](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=com.serpier/serpier) |
| Docs | [docs.serpier.com/mcp](https://docs.serpier.com/mcp) |

## What the assistant can do

- **AI Visibility**: see how often your brand is mentioned and cited in AI answers for the prompts you track, add or remove prompts, and start new analysis runs.
- **Publication tracking**: check whether published articles are live, indexed and still linking to you, and add new articles to monitor.
- **Marketplace**: search Serpier's catalog of vetted publishers by country, topic, price and authority.
- **Cart and orders**: add publishers to your cart, place orders, follow order status and fill in the brief for each publication.
- **Projects**: list and create the website projects in your organization.

Actions that change data are marked as such, so your assistant can ask you before running them. Placing an order is a real purchase, paid by card or invoice.

## Connect

You need a Serpier account. [Sign up at serpier.com](https://serpier.com). When your client connects for the first time, it opens Serpier in your browser. Sign in, choose the organization and team, and allow access. You never paste a key.

### Claude

In **Settings > Connectors**, select **Add custom connector**, name it Serpier, and paste the server URL.

### ChatGPT

Add a custom app with the server URL, then select **Authenticate** and sign in to Serpier.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http serpier https://app.serpier.com/api/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code, select **serpier**, and sign in.

### Cursor, VS Code and other clients

Add the server to your client's MCP configuration ([`mcp.json`](mcp.json)):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "serpier": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://app.serpier.com/api/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

VS Code uses `servers` as the top-level key instead of `mcpServers`.

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/Serpier/serpier-mcp
```

### Personal access token

You can also connect with a personal access token, sent in the `x-api-key` header. Personal access tokens need the Enterprise plan; see [Create a personal access token](https://docs.serpier.com/account-settings#create-a-personal-access-token).

## Privacy and support

- Privacy policy: [serpier.com/privacy-policy](https://serpier.com/privacy-policy)
- Terms: [serpier.com/terms-conditions](https://serpier.com/terms-conditions)
- Support: [hello@serpier.com](mailto:hello@serpier.com)

## Files in this repository

| File | Read by |
|---|---|
| [`server.json`](server.json) | The [Official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) and the directories that import from it, such as the GitHub MCP Registry |
| [`mcp.json`](mcp.json) | MCP clients that take a JSON server configuration |
| [`gemini-extension.json`](gemini-extension.json) | Gemini CLI |
| [`llms-install.md`](llms-install.md) | AI agents that install MCP servers for you, such as Cline |

## Releasing

1. Raise `version` in `server.json` and `gemini-extension.json` to the same value.
2. Merge to `main`, then push a tag `v<version>`.
3. The [publish workflow](.github/workflows/publish.yml) publishes `server.json` to the Official MCP Registry. It signs in with the `serpier.com` DNS key stored in the `MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY` secret.

## License

[MIT](LICENSE). The license covers the files in this repository. The Serpier service is covered by the [Serpier terms](https://serpier.com/terms-conditions).

readme.markdown:
# Zeno

Bookkeeping in QuickBooks Desktop with a person's review before anything posts.
This plugin teaches Claude, Codex and the ChatGPT desktop app how to work a
QuickBooks Desktop company file through Zeno: set up and register company
files, answer questions from the books, prepare batches of bills, checks,
journal entries, invoices and payments for a person to approve, correct work
that is already posted, and leave a record the next session can pick up.

## What you need

- A Windows PC with QuickBooks Desktop (Pro, Premier, Accountant or
  Enterprise) installed and the company file open.
- Zeno, installed on that same PC from
  [zenofirm.com/quickbooks-desktop](https://zenofirm.com/quickbooks-desktop).
  The installer provides the `qb_*` tools and connects them to Claude, the
  ChatGPT desktop app and Codex. Quit and reopen your chat client after it
  runs.

Without the installed program these skills have no tools to call and will say
so. The company file is read on the workstation and is never uploaded.

## Skills

| Skill | Use it to |
| --- | --- |
| `zeno-qb-setup` | Connect company files, check licence and read-only status, get past the first QuickBooks authorization. |
| `zeno-qb-analysis` | Answer questions: statements from QuickBooks' own reports, anything else from a local SQL copy. |
| `zeno-qb-batch` | Prepare, review, apply and reverse batches. Nothing posts until a person approves. |
| `zeno-qb-corrections` | Fix, void, delete or merge what is already in the books, smallest change first. |
| `zeno-qb-continuity` | Resume pending work, follow playbooks, and record rules, knowledge and the work log. |

Try: "Set up Zeno with my QuickBooks company files", "What did we spend on
fuel last quarter?", or "Show me the batches waiting for review."

## What this plugin runs and sends

This plugin is instructions only. It contains no programs, hooks or MCP server
declarations, runs nothing on install, and sends nothing anywhere.

The tools it describes come from the separately installed Zeno program, which
runs on the workstation and talks to QuickBooks through Intuit's QuickBooks
Desktop SDK. That program keeps its journal and local copy of the books on the
same PC. It makes network calls only for these purposes: one anonymous check
for a newer release at zenofirm.com, and, if the workstation is linked to a
Zeno account for the bank feed add-on, the exchange with api.zenofirm.com that
carries bank transactions to it. The licence check is offline. See the
[privacy policy](https://zenofirm.com/privacy) and
[what it cannot do](https://zenofirm.com/docs/quickbooks-desktop/limits).

## Support

[zenofirm.com/support](https://zenofirm.com/support) or support@zenofirm.com.
Documentation: [zenofirm.com/docs/quickbooks-desktop](https://zenofirm.com/docs/quickbooks-desktop).

This plugin's skill files are MIT licensed (see `LICENSE`). The Zeno for
QuickBooks Desktop program is licensed separately under its end user licence
agreement. QuickBooks is a trademark of Intuit Inc.; Zeno is not affiliated

readme.markdown: Ads Uploader — Meta Ads MCP The Meta Ads MCP server by Ads Uploader helps you launch and manage Meta (Facebook & Instagram) ads from Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, and Codex. --- Ads Uploader takes an existing ad you already run, turns its settings into a reusable template, and builds brand-new ads on top of it — new media, copy, CTA, and targeting — in bulk. It also duplicates existing ads by post so social proof is preserved. Point your AI agent at it and describe the ads you want. > **Agent-assisted vs fully agentic.** For agent-assisted launches, we recommend having your agent assemble a **saved build** rather than creating ads headlessly — the build is accessible, editable, and launchable from the Ads Uploader web app, so you keep a human review-and-launch step in the polished UI. Requires an existing paid Ads Uploader account with MCP access and a connected Meta account with the necessary permissions. MCP access is not included in trials. This repository contains public documentation and connector configuration. Ads Uploader is a proprietary product; its application, backend and MCP server implementation are not included here. See [License](#license) for the scope of reuse permissions. ## What it does - **Build ads from a template** — copy settings from any existing ad, then swap in new media, text, CTA, links, and targeting. - **Bulk creation** — many ads across campaigns and ad sets in one job, with per-ad text and creative options. - **Duplicate by post** — clone existing ads by Page post ID so the original post's likes, comments, and shares carry into new campaigns. - **Partnership (branded content) ads** — run ads as a partnership with a creator or brand, from your own uploaded media or an imported Instagram post, with shared or per-ad/ad-set sponsors. *(See below.)* - **Media pipeline** — import creatives from public URLs, a Google Drive folder, or local files. - **Preview before launch** — resolve a spec, check Meta permissions, and see exactly what would be created. - **Multi-account** — list and work across every Meta ad account, Page, and connected Instagram account you have access to. ## Why Ads Uploader Founded on a decade of hands-on Meta advertising, Ads Uploader gives an agent the **deepest, most complete Meta (Facebook & Instagram) ad-creation workflows available** — everything needed to actually ship campaigns end to end: - **Template from any live ad** — copy a proven ad's exact settings, then rebuild on top with new media, copy, and targeting. - **Real bulk** — many ads across campaigns and ad sets in a single job, with per-ad and per-ad-set text. - **Partnership / branded content ads** — uploaded-media partnerships (Facebook + Instagram) and imported Instagram creator posts, with shared or per-ad/ad-set sponsors and header modes. - **Duplicate preserving social proof** — clone by post so likes, comments, and shares carry into new campaigns. - **Creative depth** — carousel, flexible, Multi-Media, Dynamic Optimization, creative enhancements, Advantage+ targeting, CTA and URL tagging. - **Human-in-the-loop by design** — validate-only previews and saved builds you finish in the web app. Built by a team that runs Meta ads at scale, and trusted by performance marketers and agencies managing serious Meta budgets. ## Install ### Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http ads-uploader https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp ``` ### Claude desktop / Claude.ai Settings → **Connectors** → **Add custom connector** → paste the URL, then complete sign-in and consent in your browser: ```text https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp ``` ### ChatGPT Settings → **Connectors** (custom MCP) → add the server URL `https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp` → sign in when prompted. ### Cursor [Add Ads Uploader to Cursor](https://cursor.com/install-mcp?name=ads-uploader&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2Fkc3VwbG9hZGVyLmNvbS9hcGkvbWNwIn0%3D) This repository includes an Agent Plugins `plugin.json` and `mcp.json`, plus a `.mcp.json` compatibility file for directory discovery. The plugin connects to the hosted server; authentication happens in your browser. Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (or a project `.cursor/mcp.json`): ```json { "mcpServers": { "ads-uploader": { "url": "https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp" } } } ``` After adding the server, complete the Ads Uploader sign-in and consent prompt. Ask the agent to list your ad accounts to check the connection. ### Grok Open [Grok Connectors](https://grok.com/connectors), choose **New Connector → Custom**, and enter `https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp`. Follow the authentication prompt. See the [Grok connection guide](docs/connect-grok.md) for prerequisites and example prompts; this host connection is awaiting an end-to-end test. ### Codex Add to `~/.codex/config.toml`: ```toml [mcp_servers.ads-uploader] command = "npx" args = ["mcp-remote", "https://adsuploader.com/api/mcp"] ``` ### Local stdio package For hosts that need to upload files directly from disk. The local package reads the credentials saved by `ads login`. name: Agent Comms
description: Cross-harness communication mesh for LLM agents — rooms, DMs, presence, and visibility over TCP

readme.markdown:
# Agent Comms

Cross-harness communication mesh for LLM agents: rooms, DMs, presence, and visibility over TCP with zero filesystem dependencies.

## Why

LLM agents on the same machine are isolated silos. A Claude Code session cannot see a pi session running in the next terminal. A Codex agent cannot ask a Claude agent to review its work. Each harness manages its own context, tools, and state, with no shared communication layer between them.

Agent Comms gives them one. Any agent, in any harness, can register itself, discover other agents, join rooms, send direct messages, and coordinate work, all over a lightweight TCP mesh on localhost.

The project began as a filesystem-based bus (`~/.agents/bus/`), where agents read and wrote JSON files to communicate. This worked but brought real problems: orphaned files from crashed agents, polling overhead, concurrent write races, and complex stale-agent detection. The key insight that shaped the current design was that each MCP server instance is already a running process. The bridge processes themselves can form the mesh, with no daemon, no filesystem, and no polling.

## How it works

Each bridge instance is a peer in a TCP mesh on localhost. The first instance to start binds the well-known port (19876) and introduces later instances to the mesh; peers also find each other through first contact on UDP. Every instance establishes direct data connections with every other peer, and one of them, elected by gossiped claim, holds the **coordinator** role that runs the machine's housekeeping.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph Agent A ["Agent A (pi)"]
        A_LLM["LLM"]
        A_Bridge["pi bridge"]
    end
    subgraph Agent B ["Agent B (Claude Code)"]
        B_Bridge["Claude bridge"]
        B_LLM["LLM"]
    end
    A_LLM -- "agent_comms(send, ...)" --> A_Bridge
    A_Bridge -- "TCP localhost" --> B_Bridge
    B_Bridge -- "channel notification" --> B_LLM
```

All state is held in memory and synchronised between peers. Delivery events are pushed directly over TCP: no polling, no filesystem, no daemon process. Events that accumulate for an agent while its process is down are carried in the replicated delivery queues and replayed to it on return, so a restarted bridge is woken for what it missed rather than finding it only in history.

### Coordinator pattern

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P1 as Peer 1 (first to start)
    participant P2 as Peer 2
    participant P3 as Peer 3
    P1->>P1: binds port 19876, then claims the coordinator role once no holder has announced itself
    P2->>P1: connect to 19876
    P1-->>P2: peer list [P1]
    P2->>P1: establish data connection
    P3->>P1: connect to 19876
    P1-->>P3: peer list [P1, P2]
    P3->>P1: establish data connection
    P3->>P2: establish data connection
    Note over P1,P3: All peers now connected directly
    rect rgb(255, 230, 230)
        Note over P1: Port holder and coordinator is killed
        P2->>P3: lowest device-id claims the coordinator role at a raised term
        P2->>P2: race to bind 19876
        P3->>P3: race to bind 19876
        Note over P2,P3: the operating system's bind picks one port winner
        P3->>P2: loser re-introduces itself to the winner
    end
```

- **Well-known port** 19876 on localhost: the compatibility first-contact address and introduction path, not the coordinator role
- The first instance to bind it answers every later instance that connects there with the peer list; it is not a router
- On graceful shutdown, the port holder names its longest-running peer as successor and hands the listener over before closing
- On a crash, every surviving peer independently races to rebind the port; the operating system's exclusive bind picks the single winner, and the losers re-introduce themselves to it

Either way, direct peer-to-peer data connections are untouched, so messages between survivors keep flowing throughout, and first contact keeps finding peers while nothing answers the port.

The **coordinator role** is separate from the port. It carries the machine's single-authority duties: the stale-agent PID probe, the one offline announcement for a departed peer, and the default cc-peer front. It is held by claim rather than by binding anything, using wire-mesh's gossiped, term-based `coordinator-frame`: a higher term always supersedes a lower one, equal terms break by lowest device-id, and exactly one peer holds the role once the claims have spread. Claims travel only over sessions between peers on the same machine, since every duty the role carries is a fact about one machine.

- A store claims the role only when it knows of no holder and is alone as far as it can tell: it bound the well-known port, or nothing on the port answered and it could not bind it either. When first contact is running, a holder that never held the port may still be about to announce itself, so the store first waits the ordinary network deadline for that announcement and claims only if none came; a store arriving at an existing mesh therefore never takes the role from its holder
- Both ends of every session between two stores on the machine tell each other which claim they accept as the session opens, so a joiner learns the holder instead of claiming over it, whichever side dialled
- Claims are read only from trusted sessions on the machine: never from a session that may cross machines (an `addListener` listener, a `connectToRemote` dial, or a dial at any address other than a loopback one, such as a peer first contact heard over LAN broadcast), and never from a session on the well-known port before it has introduced itself
- Two meshes that each elected a holder while apart (joined later by first contact, say) converge on one: the lower claim is superseded and its holder stops its duties
- When the holder departs, the survivor with the lowest device-id among the stores it has a session to claims at once at a raised term; any other survivor claims itself if, after the ordinar

readme.markdown:
# Tera Ads: Meta Ads MCP with approval, undo and real profit

Connect your Meta (Facebook and Instagram) ads and your Shopify store to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code or Claude Code, then ask in your own words. Your AI reads your live campaigns and your store's profit after returns. It can also pause ads, turn them on, change budgets and build new campaigns, within the limits below.

```
https://teraads.co/mcp
```

That address is the whole setup. It is a remote MCP server: you sign in on teraads.co, and there is nothing to install or host.

## Why Tera Ads

- **Approval before a change.** For each connection you choose whether your AI makes changes itself, asks you first, or only reads. With **Ask me first**, a change waits in Tera Ads until you approve it there, and your AI can't approve it for you.
- **Undo after it.** A pause, turn-on or budget change can be undone in Tera Ads for 7 days. Everything your AI creates starts paused and spends nothing until it is turned on.
- **Profit after returns, not only ROAS.** Answers come from your store's orders, returns, product cost, shipping, fees and refunds, minus your Meta and Google ad spend. Meta's attributed revenue is labelled as Meta's.

Changes go to Meta through Tera Ads' approved Meta app. Each change is checked against Meta first, made once, then read back.

## Set it up

You need a free [Tera Ads account](https://teraads.co/signup) with your Meta ad account connected. Connect Shopify too, so your AI can see store sales and profit. Only the business owner can connect an AI.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http tera-ads https://teraads.co/mcp
```

Start Claude Code, type `/mcp`, choose **tera-ads** and sign in to Tera Ads in your browser.

To add the server together with the [six skills](#skills) in this repo, install it as a plugin instead:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add Teralabsx/meta-ads-mcp
```

```bash
claude plugin install tera-ads@tera-ads
```

### Claude (web and desktop)

1. In Claude, open **Customize**, then **Connectors**.
2. Choose **+ Add**, then **Add custom connector**. Name it Tera Ads, paste `https://teraads.co/mcp`, choose **Continue**, then **Add**.
3. Choose **Connect**, sign in to Tera Ads and pick the business to share.
4. In a chat, choose **+** at the lower left, then **Connectors**, and switch Tera Ads on.

On Team and Enterprise plans, an owner adds Tera Ads under Organization settings, then Connectors. Members then choose Connect.

### ChatGPT

1. In ChatGPT on the web, open **Settings**, then **Apps**.
2. Open **Advanced settings** and turn on **Developer mode**.
3. Choose **Create app**, name it Tera Ads, paste `https://teraads.co/mcp` and choose **OAuth** for authentication.
4. Sign in to Tera Ads and pick the business to share, then add Tera Ads to a chat from the **+** menu.

Developer mode needs a ChatGPT plan that includes it. In Business workspaces, an admin adds the app.

### Cursor

Add [`configs/cursor/mcp.json`](configs/cursor/mcp.json) to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (every project) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (one project). When Cursor asks, sign in to Tera Ads in your browser.

### VS Code

Add [`configs/vscode/mcp.json`](configs/vscode/mcp.json) to `.vscode/mcp.json`, or run **MCP: Add Server** from the Command Palette. Start the server, sign in to Tera Ads, then switch Tera Ads on under **Configure Tools** in Chat.

## What you can ask

| Ask | What your AI looks up |
|---|---|
| "What was my profit after returns in the last 30 days?" | `get_profit` |
| "Meta says my ROAS is 3. What did my store actually make?" | `get_insights`, `get_profit` |
| "Which campaigns spent the most this week, and what did they bring in?" | `get_insights` |
| "Which ads spent money in the last 14 days without a sale?" | `get_insights` at ad level |
| "Pause those three ads." | `pause` |
| "Raise the budget of my best ad set by 20%." | `list_ad_sets`, `set_budget` |
| "Copy my best campaign as a paused draft." | `duplicate` |
| "Build a paused sales campaign for this product in the US and Canada." | `search_locations`, `list_pages`, `list_pixels`, `create_campaign`, `create_ad_set`, `create_ad` |
| "Write two new versions of my best ad's text." | `get_ad_creative`, `create_ad` |
| "What changed in my ads this week, and can I still undo it?" | `list_recent_changes` |

More in [docs/prompts.md](docs/prompts.md). Every tool is listed in [docs/tools.md](docs/tools.md).

## Skills

The Claude Code plugin adds six skills. Each one tells your AI which tools to use, in what order, and what to check first.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`profit-check`](skills/profit-check/SKILL.md) | Puts Meta's numbers next to your store's profit after returns |
| [`weekly-ads-review`](skills/weekly-ads-review/SKILL.md) | Compares this week with last week and suggests changes, without making any |
| [`pause-wasted-spend`](skills/pause-wasted-spend/SKILL.md) | Finds ads spending without sales and pauses the ones you pick |
| [`scale-a-winner`](skills/scale-a-winner/SKILL.md) | Raises a winner's budget in safe steps, or copies it as a paused draft |
| [`launch-paused-campaign`](skills/launch-paused-campaign/SKILL.md) | Builds a whole campaign, ad set and ad, all paused, for you to check |
| [`refresh-ad-copy`](skills/refresh-ad-copy/SKILL.md) | Writes new versions of a tired ad as paused ads beside it |

The skill files are plain Markdown, so you can read them or copy them into other assistants.

## Limits and safety

- **You set what your AI may do.** Make changes itself, ask you first, or only read. You can switch a connection between the first two at any time under AI connections in Tera Ads.
- **New things start paused.** Campaigns, ad sets, ads and copies spend nothing until something turns them on.
- **Budget steps are capped.** One change can at most triple a budget or cut it to a tenth.
- **Daily cap.** Assistants can make at most 50 changes a day to one business.

readme.markdown:
# ofdkit

轻量的 Python 工具，用来读取 OFD 文件，提取里面的文字和发票字段，并能接入 AI 工具。OFD 是中国的国家标准版式文档格式（GB/T 33190），常见于电子发票和公文。

A lightweight Python toolkit for reading OFD documents (GB/T 33190, the Chinese fixed-layout format used for e-invoices and official documents): extract text and invoice fields, and use them from AI tools.

> 状态：0.4 版，接口以后可能还会调整。更新记录见 [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Edgar-311/ofdkit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)。
> Status: 0.4, the API may still change. See the [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/Edgar-311/ofdkit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## 能做什么 / What it does

- 看发票：一条命令显示发票号码、日期、购买方、销售方、金额和明细。
  Show an invoice: number, date, buyer, seller, amounts and line items, with one command.
- 把一个文件夹里的发票汇总到 Excel，也能直接读税务平台批量下载的 .zip 压缩包。发票号码保持原样（不会变成 2.4E+19），金额可以直接求和，重复的发票会标出来。
  Summarise a folder of invoices, or a .zip archive downloaded from the tax service, into an Excel workbook: invoice numbers stay intact, amounts are numbers, duplicates are flagged.
- 报销帮手：检查发票抬头（购买方名称、税号）对不对；按发票内容给文件改名，可以预览、可以改回去。
  For reimbursement: check that invoices are made out to the right buyer, and rename invoice files after their contents, with a preview and an undo.
- 按阅读顺序提取文字，包括模板和复合对象里的文字。
  Text in reading order, including text in templates and composite objects.
- 给程序和 AI 用：发票字段输出 JSON，提供 MCP 服务器、Agent Skill 和 MarkItDown 插件。
  For programs and AI: invoice fields as JSON, an MCP server, an Agent Skill and a MarkItDown plugin.
- 只用 Python 标准库，没有任何第三方依赖；能读很多不规范的文件（路径写法不对、编码不对、XML 前缀错误等）。
  Standard library only, no dependencies; reads many non-conforming files (bad paths, encodings, XML prefixes).

## 快速上手 / Quick start

1. 安装 [Python](https://www.python.org/downloads/) 3.10 或更新版本。Windows 上安装时请勾选 "Add python.exe to PATH"。
   Install Python 3.10 or newer.
2. 打开命令行（Windows 在开始菜单搜索"终端"或"cmd"，Mac 打开"终端"），安装 ofdkit：
   Open a terminal and install ofdkit:

   ```bash
   pip install ofdkit
   ```

3. 看一张发票（把文件拖进命令行窗口就能填上路径）：
   Show an invoice (drag the file into the terminal window to type its path):

   ```bash
   ofdkit 发票.ofd
   ```

   ```text
   电子发票（普通发票）

   发票号码  00000000000000000001
   开票日期  2026-01-02
   购买方    测试单位甲
             税号 TESTBUYER0001
   销售方    测试单位乙
             税号 TESTSELLER0002
   金额      100.00
   税额      6.00
   价税合计  106.00
   明细      *测试*服务项目  100.00  6%
   开票人    测试人员
   ```

   （数据是虚构的 / fictional data）

4. 看一个文件夹或 .zip 压缩包里的所有发票和合计，然后导出到 Excel：
   List every invoice in a folder or .zip archive with totals, then export to Excel:

   ```bash
   ofdkit 发票文件夹
   ofdkit batch 发票文件夹 -o 发票汇总.xlsx
   ```

   Excel 文件有两张表："发票"每张发票一行，最后是合计；"明细"每个商品或服务一行。重复的发票标黄，读不出来的文件标红，有其他提醒的发票（抬头不对、金额缺少或不是数字）标橙，都在"提醒"一栏写明原因。合计用的是 SUBTOTAL，筛选以后只算看得见的行；不是数字的金额保留原样、不算进合计，合计下面会注明有几张。
   The workbook has two sheets: 发票 (one row per invoice, with totals; duplicates in yellow, unreadable files in red, other reminders such as another buyer or an amount that is missing or not a number in orange, each explained) and 明细 (one row per line item). Totals use SUBTOTAL, so they follow filters.

5. 检查发票抬头：加上 `--buyer`，购买方名称或税号不是你公司的发票会标出来（Excel 里标橙色）。名称和税号都要查，就写两次：
   Check who the invoices are made out to: with `--buyer`, invoices for another buyer name or tax ID are flagged (orange in Excel). Repeat it to check both:

   ```bash
   ofdkit 发票文件夹 --buyer 某某有限公司 --buyer 91310000XXXXXXXXXX
   ```

6. 按发票内容给文件改名，例如 `dzfp_2411…_20240528.ofd` 改成 `2024-05-28_某某公司_4449.00_2411….ofd`。不加 `--apply` 只是预览；同名的 PDF、XML 会一起改（其中一个改不了，这张发票的文件都保持原名）；改名前会先写好改名记录，写不了就一个文件也不改；用 `--undo` 可以按记录改回去，运行几次都没关系：
   Rename invoice files after their contents. Without `--apply` it only previews; PDF and XML copies with the same name are renamed too (if one cannot be, that invoice's files all keep their names); the log is written before anything is renamed, and nothing is renamed if it cannot be; `--undo` restores the old names from the log and is safe to run again:

   ```bash
   ofdkit rename 发票文件夹            # 预览 / preview
   ofdkit rename 发票文件夹 --apply    # 改名 / rename
   ofdkit rename --undo 发票文件夹/改名记录_20261028_093000.csv
   ```

   名字的格式可以改，例如 `--pattern "{开票日期}_{购买方}_{商品}"`。可以用的字段：开票日期、发票号码、发票代码、发票种类、销售方、销售方税号、购买方、购买方税号、金额、税额、价税合计、商品、原文件名。
   The name format can be changed with `--pattern`; fields are listed by `ofdkit rename --help` (English names such as `{date}`, `{seller}` and `{total}` work too).

## 命令行 / Command line

```bash
ofdkit 文件.ofd                              # 看发票，不是发票就显示文字 / show an invoice, or the text
ofdkit 文件夹或压缩包.zip                     # 发票列表和合计 / list invoices with totals

ofdkit 文件夹 --buyer 公司名或税号             # 检查发票抬头 / check the buyer
ofdkit rename 文件夹                         # 按内容改名（先预览）/ rename after contents (preview first)
ofdkit text 文件.ofd                         # 提取文字 / print text
ofdkit invoice 发票.ofd                      # 发票字段（JSON）/ invoice fields as JSON

ofdkit describe 文件.ofd -o 结构.json         # 打码的结构，用于报告问题 / masked structure for bug reports
```

`show`、`batch` 和 `rename` 加 `-r` 会连子文件夹一起找。`ofdkit 文件.ofd` 是 `ofdkit show 文件.ofd` 的简写。
Add `-r` to `show`, `batch` and `rename` to include subfolders. `ofdkit PATH` is short for `ofdkit show PATH`.

readme.markdown:
# Mnemosyne

**The next agent starts wiser.**

**Mnemosyne is local-first, long-term memory for AI agents: one SQLite file that keeps what an agent learned together with the evidence it came from, served to any host over TypeScript, MCP, CLI or HTTP.** When a source is corrected, the memories recorded as depending on it are retired, so the next agent starts from what current recorded evidence still supports instead of repeating a stale lesson. The local engine needs no model API key, database server or Docker.

- **Evidence on every memory.** Each record keeps its source and trust tier, and the superseded version stays inspectable after a correction.
- **Corrections that reach dependents.** A corrected requirement retires the procedures and skills recorded as depending on it; 3.0 can also propose dependencies nobody declared, for review.
- **Auditable over time.** Past beliefs replay exactly. Given the records a failed retrieval should have returned, `bisect` finds the records that pushed them out. In the 3.0 pre-release, consolidation is outcome-gated and reversible.
- **Any host.** MCP for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; a TypeScript SDK; a CLI; and authenticated HTTP with a Python client and live inspector.

**Stable: 2.0.0 (`npm install mnemosy-ai`) · Newest pre-release: 3.0.0-rc.3, the breakthrough release (`npm install mnemosy-ai@next`) · MIT · Node.js ≥22.16**

[Website](https://mnemosy.ai) · [Quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) · [Documentation](docs/README.md) · [Examples](examples/README.md) · [Migration](docs/BRIDGE.md) · [Measured results](docs/evaluation/BENCHMARKS.md) · [Trust evidence](docs/BENCHMARKS-TRUST.md) · [Claims and evidence](docs/CLAIMS.md) · [Releases](https://github.com/28naem-del/mnemosyne/releases) · [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mnemosy-ai) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) · [Issues](https://github.com/28naem-del/mnemosyne/issues)

> [!NOTE]
> **Which Mnemosyne is this?** This repository is the TypeScript package published on npm as [`mnemosy-ai`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mnemosy-ai), with its site at [mnemosy.ai](https://mnemosy.ai). It is a separate project from [mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne](https://github.com/mnemosyne-oss/mnemosyne), the Python memory library published on PyPI as `mnemosyne-memory`; the two share a name, not code or maintainers. Please file issues for that project in its own repository.

## Try it

The first `npx` run downloads the package; after that, the 3.0.0-rc.3 demo runs offline on synthetic corpora, with no API key and no model, and measures each claim while it runs:

```sh
npx -y -p mnemosy-ai@next mnemosy demo
```

The recording above is one unedited run ([`assets/demo.tape`](assets/demo.tape) regenerates it with vhs). The last line of each of its five moments, matching the recorded run of 28 October 2026 ([`site/demo-five.json`](site/demo-five.json); timings vary by machine; the pass bars printed after each line are omitted here):

```text
PROOF  replay determinism: 1000/1000 identical, 24000/24000 as-of answers = ground truth   [PASS]
PROOF  downstream repair: undeclared invalidated 3/3, accepted edges true 3/3, stale after correction 0 (11 probes)   [PASS]
PROOF  blame precision / time-to-locate: precision 1.00, 0.40 s, 2000 records   [PASS]
PROOF  poisoning suite v1, live: 227 cases, 0 escapes, 0 false quarantines   [PASS]
PROOF  consolidation receipts: kept 1 (delta +2), rolled back 2 (regression, invariant violated), rollback identical hash true, chain verified 4 receipts   [PASS]

5/5 moments proved.
```

[What each moment proves, and what it does not](docs/DEMO.md). Then give the memory to Claude Code (other clients: [Install and connect an agent](#install-and-connect-an-agent)):

```sh
claude mcp add mnemosyne -- npx -y -p mnemosy-ai@next mnemosy mcp --db ./.mnemosyne/memory.sqlite --workspace my-project --agent assistant
```

For the stable release, write `mnemosy-ai@2.0.0` in place of `mnemosy-ai@next`; on 2.0.0, `mnemosy demo` runs the earlier single-scenario demo.

**Contents:** [3.0: the breakthrough release](#new-in-30-the-breakthrough-release-pre-release-on-npm-next) · [Install and connect an agent](#install-and-connect-an-agent) · [Measured results](#measured-409-of-500-on-longmemeval-s-with-the-misses-printed) · [Choose your engine](#choose-your-engine) · [A working demonstration](#start-with-a-working-demonstration) · [Corrections in code](#a-correction-should-change-what-the-next-agent-does) · [Tune the dense index](#tune-the-dense-index) · [What you can build](#what-you-can-build) · [Entry points](#local-engine-several-entry-points) · [Migrate](#migrate-while-your-agent-keeps-working) · [Limits](#measured-with-the-limits-visible) · [Operational boundaries](#operational-boundaries) · [Build with us](#build-with-us)

## New in 3.0: the breakthrough release (pre-release on npm `next`)

3.0 is the breakthrough release. Replay and `bisect` already existed in 2.0.0. 3.0 adds four things: dependencies nobody declared, inferred and proposed for review, so that corrections reach them once accepted; a poisoning gate checked against a reproducible attack suite; outcome-gated, reversible consolidation with signed receipts; and opt-in precision controls. The kernel's `bisect` also gained the hybrid retrieval path (not a public package export in 3.0.0-rc.3; the `mnemosy bisect` CLI stays lexical). Each of these is documented and tested below, and each public claim is listed with its evidence in [Claims and evidence](docs/CLAIMS.md). 3.0.0-rc.3 is the current release candidate on the npm `next` channel: `npm install mnemosy-ai@next` installs it, while `npm install mnemosy-ai` still installs the stable 2.0.0. Every number below was measured on 3.0.0-rc.2, offline, with no API key, no paid model and no LLM judge. Each one reproduces with the commands in [Benchmarks and trust evidence](docs/BENCHMARKS-TRUST.md), which also lists what is not claimed.

readme.markdown:
# Brand Sponsor Finder MCP Server

Find the brands that paid creators in a niche in the last 90 days, with the public evidence for each placement. One row per brand with a recency score, and one row per sighting with its evidence link, date, and promo code.

## What's Inside

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
- [Example prompts](#example-prompts)
- [Tool](#tool)
- [Inputs](#inputs)
- [Pricing](#pricing)
- [Your keys](#your-keys)
- [Full actor documentation](#full-actor-documentation)
- [License](#license)

## What it does

- Reads public YouTube video descriptions (channel feeds, or your own YouTube Data API key), podcast show notes, newsletter issues, and event sponsor pages for sponsor lines, promo codes, and sponsor slots.
- Follows shortlinks and affiliate redirects to the brand's own domain, and merges every sighting into one row per brand domain.
- Checks the brands it found for open partnership job posts (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby) and creator or affiliate program pages, which become the brand's public contact.
- Returns only sightings inside your date window, each with an evidence link. Instagram, TikTok, and the Meta Ad Library are not read.

All of the work runs on Apify. This package is a thin client that starts the actor run, waits for it, and hands back the dataset rows.

## Row cap and paging

One run can return hundreds of rows (633 rows and about 0.8 MB of text on a 30 day health and fitness search), which is more than an agent context holds. So each call returns at most `max_rows` rows: 50 unless you set it, and never more than 200.

1. The first call starts the run and returns the first page. The first content block is the JSON array of rows. The second is a paging block with `run_id`, `total_rows`, `rows_returned`, and `next_cursor`.
2. To get the next page, call `find_brand_sponsors` again with only `cursor` set to `next_cursor`. Add `max_rows` to change the page size.
3. Repeat until `next_cursor` is `null`.

A cursor call starts no run. It reads the next page of rows the first run already wrote, so no row is billed twice. A cursor works for as long as Apify keeps that run's dataset.

## Quick start

You need Node.js 18 or newer and an Apify account with an API token.

Add this to your Claude Desktop config (`claude_desktop_config.json`), Cursor, or any MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mamba-brand-sponsor-finder": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@mambalabsdev/mcp-brand-sponsor-finder"
      ],
      "env": {
        "APIFY_TOKEN": "your-apify-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart the client. The `find_brand_sponsors` tool appears.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- An Apify API token from [console.apify.com/account/integrations](https://console.apify.com/account/integrations), set as `APIFY_TOKEN`. The server lists its tool without a token; a call needs one.

## Example prompts

- "Find brands sponsoring health and fitness creators in the last 90 days."
- "Which brands paid beauty YouTubers this month? Brand rows only."
- "List coffee brands sponsoring podcasts and newsletters, with promo codes."

## Tool

`find_brand_sponsors`. One tool. Example arguments:

```json
{
  "niche": "health and fitness",
  "window_days": "90"
}
```

## Inputs

Every buyer facing input of the actor, unchanged, plus the two paging settings. Omitted inputs take the actor's own defaults. Numbers and booleans are sent as strings.

| Input | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `niche` | string | The audience niche, for example "health and fitness", "beauty and skincare", or "food and beverage". Searches for channels, shows, and newsletters use it, and every row carries it. These three niches also start from a list of sources Mamba Labs has read before (turn off with use_niche_presets) |
| `audience_keywords` | string | Optional. More search terms for the audience, one per line or separated by commas, for example "strength training". Each one widens the podcast, newsletter, and (with your key) YouTube channel search. Up to 20. A text field, so a Clay column maps straight in |
| `window_days` | string | Only sightings from the last N days. Whole number, default 90, at most 365. Sent as text so Clay works Default 90 |
| `sources` | string | Optional. Which sources to run, separated by commas, any of: youtube, podcast, event, newsletter, job_post, program. Empty runs all of them. job_post and program check the brands the other sources found |
| `seed_sources` | string | Optional. YouTube channel URLs or @handles, podcast RSS feed URLs, or newsletter URLs to read first, one per line or separated by commas. Each is read even beyond the per source limits |
| `event_calendar` | string | Optional. Events whose sponsor or partner page to read, as a JSON list of objects: [{"name": "...", "url": "sponsor page URL", "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "city": "...", "audience": "...", "size": "..."}], or one sponsor page URL per line. url is needed; the rest is optional. A dated event inside the window gives dated rows; an undated or upcoming event gives undated rows |
| `use_niche_presets` | string | true or false, default true. For health and fitness, beauty and skincare, and food and beverage, also read the channels, shows, newsletters, and event pages Mamba Labs has read before Default true |
| `include_brands` | string | true or false, default true. One row per brand domain with sighting count, last seen date, sources, creators or events, contact, and recency score Default true |
| `include_sightings` | string | true or false, default true. One row per sighting with its evidence link, date, promo code, placement type, and pitch angle Default true |
| `max_channels` | string | YouTube channels read per run. Whole number, default 20, at most 100. Sent as text so Clay works Default 20 |
| `max_videos_per_channel` | string | Newest uploads read per channel (the public feed holds 15). Whole number, defa

readme.markdown:
# Keeploop plugins for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Grok Build and Grok Bot

[Keeploop](https://keeploop.app) is the personal context layer for your AI: a Mac menu bar app
that lets the AI apps you already use read your Mail, Messages, Calendar, Notes and Slack, right
on your Mac. Your data stays on your Mac until an AI app you connect asks for it, and you decide what each AI can see and do.

This repository is the plugin marketplace for Keeploop. It has two plugins:

- `keeploop` runs on your Mac, for Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI and Grok Build. Local use is free.
- `keeploop-remote` is for Grok Bot. It connects through Keeploop's hosted connector at
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp` and is hidden in the Cursor editor. Needs Keeploop Pro or its
  free trial for remote use; local use is free.

The local plugin adds:

- **The Keeploop tools** (mail, threads and attachments, calendar and free time, messages, notes,
  contacts and Slack, monitors that wake the agent when a reply lands, drafts in your voice).
  They come from the Keeploop app through a small launcher; nothing in this repository reads
  your data itself.
- **The `/keep-` commands**:

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/keep-today` | Today's schedule, the replies you owe, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-free [length and range]` | Open slots on your calendar, for example `/keep-free 30m this week` |
| `/keep-brief [account or category]` | Unread mail, what needs a reply, and today's monitor hits |
| `/keep-reply` | Threads where someone is waiting on you, with a suggested next step each |
| `/keep-thread <subject or mail id>` | Summarize a whole conversation: decisions and open questions |
| `/keep-draft <mail id> <what to say>` | Draft a threaded reply that sounds like you. Saves a draft only |
| `/keep-find <description>` | Find a file someone sent you by describing it |
| `/keep-waiting` | Mail you sent that nobody has answered yet, oldest first |
| `/keep-settings [what to change]` | See what the AI can do, or propose a change for approval on your Mac |
| `/keep-help` | List the commands |

## Requirements

- An Apple Silicon Mac on macOS 26 or later.
- **The Keeploop app**, installed in `/Applications` (or `~/Applications`) and opened once.
  Get it at [keeploop.app](https://keeploop.app). Without the app the plugin's server stops with
  "Keeploop is not installed on this Mac. Install Keeploop from https://keeploop.app ...".

If you already have Keeploop, the easiest route is Keeploop > Settings > Connect, which installs
this plugin for you.

## Install

### Claude Code

```
/plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
/plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Or from a terminal:

```
claude plugin marketplace add keeploopapp/claude-plugin
claude plugin install keeploop@keeploop
```

Restart Claude Code, then type `/keep-help`.

### Cursor

Install **Keeploop** from the Cursor Marketplace in Customize, or add this repository as a
plugin source. The plugin reports itself to Keeploop as Cursor, so Keeploop's per-app rules apply.

### Grok Build

Grok Build reads Claude Code marketplaces, so the Claude Code commands above are all it needs.

### Gemini CLI

```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/keeploopapp/claude-plugin
```

The extension runs the same local launcher as the plugin (`gemini-extension.json` and
`GEMINI.md` at the repository root). Restart Gemini CLI, then ask "what needs my reply today?".

### Grok Bot

In Grok Bot, open Connect apps, find Keeploop, and add it (this is the `keeploop-remote`
plugin). Sign in to Keeploop in the window that opens, then approve Grok Bot on your Mac.

### Web and phone AI apps (Claude, ChatGPT, Grok, Poke and others)

The plugin is for AI apps on your Mac. To use Keeploop from claude.ai, ChatGPT (including dots),
grok.com, Poke or any app that can add a custom MCP connector, add this one URL:

```
https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp
```

Sign in to Keeploop in the window the app opens, then approve the app on your Mac. The same URL
works for every user; it reaches your Mac only after you approve it there. Remote apps are Read
only until you allow more in Keeploop. Web and phone AI apps need Keeploop Pro or its free trial;
the plugin on your Mac works on Free. Step by step for each app:
<https://keeploop.app/your-ai-apps>.

## What the plugin contains

- `plugins/keeploop/server/keeploop-mcp`: a shell launcher that runs the connector inside
  `Keeploop.app` (its signed `Contents/MacOS/keeploop-mcp`). The Keeploop app checks that
  signature and applies your permissions to every call.
- `plugins/keeploop/skills/keep-*`: the commands, as plain Markdown.
- `plugins/keeploop/hooks/hooks.json`: a Claude Code `SessionStart` hook that tells Keeploop
  which session is running, so a monitor can wake the session that asked for it. It does nothing
  when the app is not installed.
- `plugins/keeploop-remote/`: the Grok Bot plugin. Its `mcp.json` holds only the address
  `https://mcp.keeploop.app/mcp`, and it has the same `skills/keep-*`. It runs nothing on your
  computer.
- `.claude-plugin/` and `.cursor-plugin/`: the marketplace manifests.

Nothing in the local plugin makes a network connection, downloads code or installs packages. The
launcher only runs the Keeploop app's connector on your Mac, and that talks to the Keeploop app
over a local connection, so there is no Keeploop server in the path. If you also use Keeploop from
a web or phone AI app, that is a separate connection: your data stays on your Mac, and Keeploop's
connection service passes requests to your Mac and results back. It never stores them. What the
app itself can send, and only when you turn it on, is listed in the
[privacy policy](https://keeploop.app/privacy).

## Privacy Policy

The full policy is at <https://keeploop.app/privacy>. In short:

- **Collection:** this plugin collects nothing. It starts the Keeploop app's connector, which
  reads the Apple Mail data (and any other source you turn on) alre

readme.markdown:
# Antwork: post to LinkedIn, X, Instagram and more from your AI

**AI assistants have no built-in connector for posting to social media.** To let your assistant draft, schedule and publish posts, you connect it to an MCP server that holds the platform permissions. [Antwork](https://antwork.io?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=antwork_skills) is that server: connect `https://api.antwork.io/mcp` once, sign in with OAuth, and your assistant can post to your connected accounts on **LinkedIn (personal profile or company page), X, Instagram, Facebook Pages, Threads, TikTok, YouTube and Pinterest**. Posts stay drafts until you ask it to schedule or publish them.

It works in VS Code (GitHub Copilot chat), Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any other client that speaks MCP. Two social accounts are free, then $5 a month each ([pricing](https://antwork.io/pricing?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=antwork_skills)).

## Install in one line

Pick your agent. Each line adds the Antwork skills (including [`/antwork ship`](skills/antwork-ship/SKILL.md), which turns your commits and releases into posts); the plugin lines also connect the MCP server.

| Agent | Command |
|---|---|
| **Claude Code** (plugin: skills, audit agents and MCP server) | `/plugin marketplace add polynode-co/antwork` then `/plugin install antwork@antwork` |
| **Codex** (plugin: skills and MCP server) | `codex plugin marketplace add polynode-co/antwork && codex plugin add antwork@antwork && codex mcp login antwork` |
| **Any agent, skills only** ([skills CLI](https://skills.sh): Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and others) | `npx skills add polynode-co/antwork` |

The skills CLI installs skills, not MCP servers, so connect the server once yourself:

```sh
# Claude Code
claude mcp add --transport http antwork https://api.antwork.io/mcp
# Codex
codex mcp add antwork --url https://api.antwork.io/mcp && codex mcp login antwork
```

Or in Codex's `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.antwork]
url = "https://api.antwork.io/mcp"
```

Then, from inside a repo: `/antwork ship` (or just "post about what I shipped this week").

## Connect

| | |
|---|---|
| Server URL | `https://api.antwork.io/mcp` |
| Server name | `antwork` |
| Transport | Streamable HTTP |
| Auth | OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. No API key to create or store. |

The first tool call opens a consent screen in your browser. After that, ask your assistant to connect a social account and it returns a connect link for each platform.

### VS Code

Install **Antwork** from the MCP servers gallery, or [add it in one click](https://antwork.io/automate/vscode?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=antwork_skills). MCP servers in VS Code run through GitHub Copilot, so the Copilot extension must be installed and signed in. To add it by hand, put this in `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "antwork": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://api.antwork.io/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Other clients

- **Claude.ai or Claude Desktop:** add `https://api.antwork.io/mcp` as a custom connector. [Step-by-step](https://antwork.io/automate/claude-desktop/linkedin?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=antwork_skills). For the calendar, campaign, analytics and audit workflows, add the [claude.ai skill](#claudeai) too.
- **Claude Code:** install the plugin below, which connects the server and adds the skills in one step.

# Unlock Pulse MCP

Token unlock calendar for AI assistants. Ask Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor which crypto token unlocks are coming, how big they are against
the coins already trading, who receives the tokens, and what prices did before similar unlocks in the past.

Free, read-only, no key, no sign-up. Website: https://billibo6.github.io/unlockpulse/
Telegram alerts about 24h before each unlock of 2%+ of supply: https://t.me/+22nzXAYLCGsyMzJi

## Connect

Remote server (recommended): `https://unlockpulse-mcp.unlockpulse.workers.dev/mcp` (Streamable HTTP).

- **Claude Code:** `claude mcp add --transport http unlockpulse https://unlockpulse-mcp.unlockpulse.workers.dev/mcp`
- **Claude (web, desktop, mobile):** Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → paste the address.
- **ChatGPT:** Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced → Developer mode → Create → paste the address.
- **Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf** (`mcp.json`):
  ```json
  {"mcpServers": {"unlockpulse": {"url": "https://unlockpulse-mcp.unlockpulse.workers.dev/mcp"}}}
  ```

Run it locally instead (one file, Node 18+, no dependencies):

```json
{"mcpServers": {"unlockpulse": {"command": "node", "args": ["/path/to/unlockpulse-mcp.mjs"]}}}
```

Also listed in the official MCP Registry as `io.github.Billibo6/unlockpulse`.

## Tools

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `get_upcoming_unlocks` | Unlocks in the next 1–60 days, rated strong / medium / small, filters by size and futures availability |
| `get_token_unlocks` | Every scheduled unlock of one token: date, size, USD value, recipients, futures |
| `get_onchain_check` | What the wallets holding locked team, investor and treasury tokens do on-chain: balances, outflows, findings |
| `get_method_and_track_record` | How the rating works and how prices moved before past unlocks of each strength |
| `get_dataset_info` | Data freshness, coverage, sources, formula, limitations and how to cite |

Strength: **B = tokens unlocked / circulating supply**. Strong: B ≥ 10.4%, medium: B ≥ 5%.

## Skill

`skills/unlock-pulse/SKILL.md` tells Claude which tool to call for which question and how to present the answer.

```
npx skills add Billibo6/unlockpulse-mcp
```

## Data

Monthly unlock lists as CSV (snapshots; live versions update hourly) are in [`data/`](data/). Open data: CC BY 4.0.

## Example questions

- "Which strong token unlocks are coming in the next two weeks?"
- "Biggest unlocks with perpetual futures on Binance this month."
- "When is the next ARB unlock, and who gets the tokens?"
- "Have the team and investor wallets of this token moved anything? Did the unlock really happen?"

## Data and license

Code: MIT. Data served by the tools (our ratings, track record, on-chain measurements, texts): CC BY 4.0, keep the link to Unlock Pulse.
Unlock schedules are compiled from CoinMarketCap and DefiLlama and remain subject to their terms. Market data, not investment advice.

## Test

```
node test.mjs
```

The tests call the live data file, so they need internet access.
