readme.markdown:
# Pitroom

### A free pit crew for your expensive coding agent

**Cheaper and faster: hand the reading, fixes, tests and reviews to workers that run in parallel. Keep the decisions.**

Model-agnostic · Verified answers · Receipts, not vibes · OpenCode / Codex / Claude Code / Gemini CLI / Qwen Code / Kilo Code / Antigravity workers

**[Quick start](#quick-start)** ·
[Dashboard](#dashboard) ·
[Benchmarks](#benchmarks) ·
[Workflow](#workflow) ·
[Skills](#skills) ·
[Commands](#commands) ·
[Workers](#workers) ·
[Responsibility](#responsibility) ·
[Write an adapter](docs/backends.md)

**Your agent decides · Cheap workers do the typing · A second model reviews**

<sub>`pitroom dash`, with sample data</sub>

---

## Why Pitroom?

Claude Code, Codex and friends spend premium tokens *reading*: grepping, opening files, scanning code they'll never quote.

Pitroom goes one step further:

> **Your agent stays in the driver's seat. A pit crew of cheap workers does the legwork in parallel, while your agent keeps going, and hands back only the answer, the exact diff and a receipt.**

### Your model, not ours

No model is hardcoded.

Pitroom uses your worker CLI's default model: a free tier, a local MLX/Ollama model or a cheap paid one. Switch there and Pitroom follows.

### Any worker CLI

OpenCode, Codex CLI, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, Kilo Code, Antigravity CLI and Cursor CLI (the last two beta on Linux and Windows).

One group can mix them, and a fallback chain can cross them ([how adapters work](docs/backends.md)).

### Verified answers

Every `path:line` a worker cites is checked on disk. A cite without its directory (`ipc.ts:218`, `src/main/ipc.ts:218`) is found in the project, and a call such as `Schema.parse:432` is not mistaken for a file.

Your agent trusts what checks out and skips re-reading it.

### Safe by construction

No commit, push, reset or bulk delete. A git guard stops the tricks.

In isolate mode nothing reaches your tree until you apply it.

### And more

<details>
<summary>12 more features</summary>

- **Receipts, not vibes.** Tokens the worker burned, tokens returned to your agent, compression ratio, and an estimate of what your primary model would have charged. `pitroom savings --card card.svg` makes a shareable card.
- **Self-healing worker chain.** Free models get rate-limited or retired. List fallback workers once (`fallback`) and a run that hits "model not found", 429 or quota errors moves to the next model automatically, also when a plan's usage limit stops a worker part way (the next one finishes the task). Still no model hardcoded: the chain is yours.
- **A crew, not just one worker.** `pitroom crew` starts several workers at once, `pitroom watch --json` streams one line per change so your agent follows them live, `pitroom wait -g` collects every answer, `pitroom apply -g` lands isolated patches in order. Up to 20 workers run at once by default (`maxParallel`, 30 at most), the rest queue, and the fallback chain absorbs free-tier rate limits; parallel writers are refused.
- **Faster, not only cheaper.** Workers run in the background and side by side (up to 20 at once) while your agent keeps working, so slow reading and review stop blocking it. In the [benchmark](#benchmarks), 470 s of worker time finished in 156 s of wall clock, about 3× faster than one question after another, and your agent's own context stayed small.
- **Free first, dearer only when needed.** Runs and plan tasks start on the `cheap` tier, OpenCode's free model; `standard` (Codex) and `capable` (Claude Code) are for tasks that need them, and an optional `review` tier names who reviews. Gemini CLI with a free Google AI Studio key is one more cheap worker (small daily quota per model). `pitroom models` shows what each worker offers, the effort levels (`low` … `xhigh`) each model accepts, what you say it costs (`costs`) and what it used; `--effort` sets the level per run. Details: [Models, costs and effort](#models-costs-and-effort).
- **Exact changes, even in a dirty tree.** Pitroom snapshots the working tree with a throwaway git index (your index, branches and stash are never touched), so it reports *only the worker's* edits and can undo exactly those: `pitroom revert <id>`.
- **Your agent sets the permissions.** It creates each worker with the permissions the task and your session allow (read-only, isolated copy, in-place edits, web), and a worker never widens its own. A fixed floor stays for every run: no git history changes, no `sudo`, no publishing, no secrets. A worker cannot land a deletion either: `pitroom apply` refuses a patch that deletes files unless your agent passes `--allow-delete`.
- **Real isolation.** `--isolate` runs the worker in a private copy of your **current** state (its own repository, sharing your objects read-only), uncommitted and untracked files included, then hands you a patch: `pitroom apply <id>` (checked, refuses on conflict) or `pitroom discard <id>`.
- **Zero repo pollution.** No `.pitroom/` folder, no `.gitignore` edits, no branches. Records live in `~/.local/state/pitroom`.
- **Works with any agent.** Fourteen [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io): the superpowers development workflow run by workers, plus delegation (`using-pitroom`, `pitroom-research`, `-crew`, `-implement`), a CLI, and a Claude Code / Codex plugin whose session-start hook loads the workflow. Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, or anything that can run a shell command.
- **A live dashboard and a searchable history.** `pitroom dash` opens a local page of every run (the task, what the worker did step by step, its result and diff) with history and statistics, for the agent apps that show neither hooks nor a status line; `pitroom history` searches everything Pitroom ever ran. See [Dashboard](#dashboard).
- **Small.** About 6,500 lines of TypeScript in the CLI, a ~210 KB CLI bundle (plus the ~1.9 MB of dashboard files it serves, with syntax highlighting for ten languages), zero runtime dependen

readme.markdown:
# SuprSend MCP Server

The official hosted **Model Context Protocol (MCP)** server for [SuprSend](https://www.suprsend.com). Connect an AI agent — Claude, ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, or any MCP client — to your SuprSend account and operate your notification stack in natural language.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (remote MCP server — nothing to install or host)
- **Auth:** OAuth 2.1 — you sign in with your SuprSend account

> This repository is the public description of the hosted server, for the MCP registries and Copilot surfaces. The server runs at the endpoint above.

## What it does

SuprSend is a notification infrastructure platform. The MCP server lets an agent operate your SuprSend workspaces:

- **Users & preferences** — look up users, their channels, subscriptions, and notification preferences, and update them.
- **Lists & objects** — manage subscriber lists and objects (teams, accounts) and their members.
- **Workflows** — read, draft, and publish notification workflows.
- **Templates** — read, edit, validate, and publish multi-channel templates (email, SMS, push, Inbox, WhatsApp, Slack, Teams).
- **Delivery data** — query delivery logs, workflow runs, and analytics with read-only SQL to answer questions like "why did user X not get Y?".
- **Events, schemas, translations, vendors, tenants, and broadcasts** — and more.

It also ships **skills** (packaged guidance for authoring workflows, templates, and SQL) and interactive **MCP Apps** (a chart view for query results and a message-content preview).

## Connect it

Add the remote MCP server URL in your client and sign in when prompted:

- **Claude (web, desktop, or Code):** add a custom connector with the URL `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp`.
- **ChatGPT and other MCP clients:** add `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp` as a remote (Streamable HTTP) MCP server.
- **Scope to one workspace:** connect to `https://mcp.suprsend.com/mcp/<workspace>` to pin a single workspace, or use `.../mcp` for all workspaces you can access.

You authenticate with your SuprSend login, and the agent gets only the access your role allows (admins get write tools; members get reads).

## Learn more

- SuprSend: https://www.suprsend.com
- Documentation: https://docs.suprsend.com

readme.markdown:
# VibeFix: an AI agent that finds what is breaking your live app and fixes it in your code

VibeFix is an AI agent. A free check signs up to your live, published app like a brand-new person, with a real inbox, on a phone and a computer, and confirms what is broken. A paid fix is available on vibe-fixer.com.

Every app gets one free check. This repository is the MCP connection for it: add the server to your AI tool, then ask it to check your live app.

- **Endpoint:** `https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP
- **Authentication:** two tools need no sign-in; five use OAuth sign-in to your VibeFix account (the client is prompted when you call one)
- **Website:** [vibe-fixer.com](https://vibe-fixer.com)
- **Server card:** [`/.well-known/mcp.json`](https://vibe-fixer.com/.well-known/mcp.json)
- **Registry name:** `com.vibe-fixer/vibefix`

## What it does

1. **Check.** `check_live_app` starts a check of your published app. It signs up as a brand-new person with a real inbox, follows the confirmation email, and uses the app on a phone and a computer. Every app gets one free check (one new app a day per account).
2. **Read.** `get_check_result` returns what it found, with evidence.
3. **Re-check.** `confirm_fix` re-checks those problems on your live app and marks each one fixed or not.

The free check never changes your app. A full check runs only when you confirm the app is yours; otherwise the check is look-only and does not sign up. Today the fix is for apps built with Lovable, or any app whose code is on GitHub.

## Free check, paid fix

The check is free: every app gets one free check. A paid fix is available on vibe-fixer.com.

Details: [vibe-fixer.com](https://vibe-fixer.com)

## Tools

| Tool | Sign-in | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `assess_broken_app` | none | Describe a symptom in plain words; get the likely cause, the evidence that would confirm it, and what a fix involves. Reads the description only: no code, no access to your app. |
| `get_fix_options` | none | Returns the link to a sign-up check of your live app and how it works. Read-only: starts nothing, charges nothing. |
| `list_projects` | OAuth | Lists the checks on your VibeFix account. Read-only. |
| `check_repair_status` | OAuth | Says whether one check is still running. Read-only. |
| `check_live_app` | OAuth | Starts a check of your live app. Every app gets one free check. |
| `get_check_result` | OAuth | Reads what a check (or a re-check) found. Read-only. |
| `confirm_fix` | OAuth | Re-checks the reported problems on your live app after a fix. |

## Connect

### Claude Code

    claude mcp add --transport http vibefix https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

    { "mcpServers": { "vibefix": { "url": "https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp" } } }

Or use the one-click link on [vibe-fixer.com/tools](https://vibe-fixer.com/tools).

### VS Code

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

    { "servers": { "vibefix": { "type": "http", "url": "https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp" } } }

### Claude (desktop and web)

Go to Customize, Connectors, press +, then Add custom connector. Paste `https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp` and press Add.

### Replit, Lovable and other tools

See [vibe-fixer.com/tools](https://vibe-fixer.com/tools). Any tool that takes a remote MCP server works with the address above. VibeFix is independent. Product names belong to their owners and are used only to say VibeFix works with them; VibeFix is not affiliated with or endorsed by them.

### As a plugin

    claude plugin marketplace add yos88da/vibefix-mcp
    claude plugin install vibefix@vibefix

This repository is also an [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) package (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`).

## Agent skill: tell your coding agent when to check

The skill tells a coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and others) when to call VibeFix: when you say your deployed app is broken, when new users can't sign up or log in, or right after you publish a sign-up, log-in or payment change. It only checks your own app, and only when you say yes.

| Agent | One-line install |
|---|---|
| Claude Code (skill + server) | `claude plugin marketplace add yos88da/vibefix-mcp && claude plugin install vibefix@vibefix` |
| Any agent with skills | `npx skills add yos88da/vibefix-mcp` |
| Cursor (project rule) | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yos88da/vibefix-mcp/main/agent-rules/cursor/vibefix.mdc --create-dirs -o .cursor/rules/vibefix.mdc` |
| Codex (AGENTS.md) | `curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yos88da/vibefix-mcp/main/agent-rules/AGENTS.md >> AGENTS.md` |

The skill is [`skills/vibefix-live-check/SKILL.md`](skills/vibefix-live-check/SKILL.md). The Cursor rule and the AGENTS.md section say the same thing in short. Cursor and Codex also need the server connected (see Connect above).

### Codex

    codex mcp add vibefix --url https://vibe-fixer.com/mcp
    codex mcp login vibefix

## Example prompts

- "Check my live app at https://example.com like a brand-new user."
- "Re-check the problems from my last check."
- "New people say the confirmation email never arrives. What is the likely cause?"

## Limits

- Only apps with a public web address can be checked.
- The AI agent is often right and sometimes wrong. Look at the evidence each finding shows.
- `assess_broken_app` works from a description alone and says so in its answer.

## Privacy and support

Privacy: [vibe-fixer.com/privacy](https://vibe-fixer.com/privacy). Terms: [vibe-fixer.com/terms](https://vibe-fixer.com/terms). Support: [help@vibe-fixer.com](mailto:help@vibe-fixer.com).

This repository contains documentation, plugin metadata and the agent skill only. The service itself is at vibe-fixer.com.

# digline

**Regression testing for LLM applications: sample your reference, declare a floor on the checks that need one, and a score drop is read against how much that score moves on its own. A flip from pass to fail is always a regression.**

<sub>CI is the merge queue's latest run — the gate a change passes on its way to `main`; a red can mean the queue turned a pull request away while `main` did not move.</sub>

---

  
  

*The agent above is the one editing your code, not one running in production.
digline runs in your pipeline over the suite you committed: it reads no
traces.*

Your prompt worked on Tuesday. On Thursday it works a little less — not enough
to break, enough for a user to notice in two weeks. No ordinary test catches it,
because there is no correct output to compare against, only a better or a worse
one.

digline gives you an **approved reference** — the baseline — and on every change
tells you whether you are below it: which case, which check, by how much. The
baseline is a JSON file in your repository, so it goes through code review and
it rolls back with `git`. No server, no account, no network call you have not
configured yourself.

When a check uses a model to grade, that grader does not always agree with
itself. Ask digline to sample and it records how much the score moved on its
own. Declare `floor_standard_errors` on that check and that measurement becomes
a floor: a drop outside it is reported with the interval on its line, and a drop
inside it is not a regression — the headline counts it, and `explain` prints the
interval. Declare nothing and the samples are still recorded, but the tolerance
decides alone.

```console
$ digline compare --suite suite.py --run latest
2 checks got worse compared with the reference. Every case could be judged. No case is suspended. The suite is unchanged from the reference.

how-do-i-return · llm_rubric · Score fell from 1.000000 to 0.700000.
how-do-i-return · contains · Went from passing to failing (1.000000 → 0.000000).
```

## Why digline

Most evaluation tools tell you whether an output is below a threshold. digline
also tells you whether it is *worse than it was* — the drift from 0.91 to 0.78
that trips no threshold and is the first thing a user feels.

The suite is **Python, not YAML**: a judge is an object, a target is a function,
and what may leave a perimeter is declared in code — none of which a
configuration file expresses without reinventing a language. Where a suite *is*
plain data it can be TOML instead, and the two forms build the same objects —
what TOML cannot express, it refuses by name rather than half-supporting. Built
for teams shipping LLM features for someone else, who have to show a customer
what was tested, when, under which commit, and who approved it.

Wondering how digline differs from promptfoo, DeepEval, or observability
platforms? See [How digline compares](https://digline.dev/comparison/?ref=github).

## Quickstart

With uv (recommended):

```bash
uv init && uv add digline
```

or with pip in an existing environment: `pip install digline`.

**Requires Python 3.12+**, which uv fetches for you if you do not have it. On
the pip path an older interpreter says `ERROR: No matching distribution found`
with `from versions: none`, which does not say why — that is what it means.

If you use Claude Code, digline also installs as a plugin with an MCP server — see
[Claude Code and MCP](#claude-code-and-mcp) below.

`suite.py` — complete and runnable, no API key:

```python
"""suite.py — complete and runnable: no API key, nothing else to install."""

from digline.core import Contains, CostBudget, JudgeReply, LlmRubric
from digline.run import Case, Response, Suite

ANSWERS = {
    "where-is-my-order": "Order 4821 ships Thursday. — Northwind Support",
    "how-do-i-return": "Any item, within 30 days, unused. — Northwind Support",
}

def judge(prompt: str) -> JudgeReply:
    """Your judge. digline composes `prompt` from the rubric, the question and
    the answer; it wants a score in [0, 1] and a reason back."""
    signed = "Northwind Support" in prompt
    concise = len(prompt.split()) <= 60
    return JudgeReply(
        score=0.4 + 0.3 * signed + 0.3 * concise,
        reason=f"signed={signed}, concise={concise}",
    )

def target(case: Case) -> Response:
    """Your application, called once per case. Canned here so this runs as is."""
    text = ANSWERS[case.id]
    return Response(output=text, cost_usd=0.004 + 0.001 * len(text) / 100)

suite = Suite(
    tenant="northwind",
    environment="staging",
    name="support",
    assertions=[
        Contains(needle="Northwind Support"),
        LlmRubric(
            rubric="Does the reply answer the question in at most three sentences?",
            judge=judge,
            threshold=0.7,
            tolerance=0.05,
        ),
        CostBudget(max_usd=0.02, tolerance=0.05),
    ],
    cases=[Case(id="where-is-my-order"), Case(id="how-do-i-return")],
)
```

`tenant="northwind"` is ours, like every tenant in this repository's examples,
and it has to become yours before the first run. A tenant is one customer: one
perimeter, and the directory your store is keyed on, `.digline/<tenant>/`.
Name it after the customer the suite is for. A suite copied to the next
customer with this line unchanged files that customer's runs in the first
one's directory, compares them against the first one's reference and promotes
over it, each with exit `0`.

When your judge is a real model, add a provider plugin:
`uv add digline-anthropic` (or `pip install digline-anthropic`), likewise
`digline-openai` and `digline-bedrock`.

```console
$ digline run --suite suite.py
2026-08-26T15-44-09-282929-00-00-e7421ec503ccefe8

$ digline promote --suite suite.py --run latest --replacing none
tenant 'northwind' · support baseline set to 2026-08-26T15-44-09-282929-00-00-e7421ec503ccefe8
```

Now make it worse — delete `— Northwind Support` from the second answer —
and ask again:

```console
$ di

# Car Rental Brain MCP server **The real cost of car hire, for AI assistants.** Second-driver fees, deposits, debit-card acceptance, desk hours and what excess cover really costs, measured at 120+ airports in Europe, the UK and the US, plus a link to live prices ranked by the total a person will actually pay. Free. No API key. No login. Read-only. **MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP):** ``` https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp ``` Listed in the official [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as `com.carrentalbrain/car-rental-brain`. Website: [carrentalbrain.com](https://carrentalbrain.com) · Agent page: [carrentalbrain.com/ai](https://carrentalbrain.com/ai/) ## Why it exists Car-hire search shows the headline price. The bill at the desk is different: a second driver adds a fee, the desk blocks a deposit on the card, many desks refuse debit cards, some close before a late flight lands, and the desk sells its own excess cover. Car Rental Brain measures these from its own repeated searches and answers with the numbers, so an assistant can say what a rental will really cost - not just what it is advertised at. ## Tools | Tool | What it answers | |---|---| | `get_capabilities` | What is measured, how fresh it is, which airports and countries are covered | | `list_airports` | Airports measured, with the typical price per day; filter by country | | `airport_costs` | One airport's real cost: car only, with a second driver, with full cover, automatic, no-deposit; by pick-up month; deposits; debit cards; desk hours and out-of-hours fees | | `compare_airports` | Rank airports by real cost, deposit, debit-card friendliness or late desk hours | | `supplier_terms` | Per supplier at an airport: price, second-driver fee, full-cover price, deposit, debit card, desk review scores | | `build_search_link` | A link for the person: live prices for their exact dates and needs, ranked by the total they will pay, where they can book | Every answer is dated and comes from measured searches, never estimates presented as fact. ## Example questions - "What does it really cost to hire a car at Faro Airport for a week in November with two drivers?" - "Which Spanish airport is cheapest for car hire in March?" - "I only have a debit card - where can I pick up a car in Portugal?" - "My flight lands at 23:30 in Malaga - which desks are still open?" - "Is the desk's excess cover cheaper than buying full coverage in advance at Lisbon?" ## Connect
Claude (claude.ai / Claude Desktop) Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → URL `https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp`. Or in `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "car-rental-brain": { "url": "https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp" } } } ```
ChatGPT Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced → Developer mode → Create → MCP server URL `https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp`, authentication: none.
Claude Code As a plugin (from this repository): ``` /plugin marketplace add jimiwalters-cmyk/car-rental-brain-mcp /plugin install car-rental-brain@car-rental-brain ``` Or add the server directly: ``` claude mcp add --transport http car-rental-brain https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp ```
Cursor / Windsurf / Cline / VS Code ```json { "mcpServers": { "car-rental-brain": { "url": "https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp" } } } ```
Stdio-only clients ```bash npx mcp-remote https://app.carrentalbrain.com/mcp ```
Plain HTTP (JSON API) The same tools are available as a plain JSON API (e.g. `https://app.carrentalbrain.com/api/v1/get_capabilities`) - see [carrentalbrain.com/ai](https://carrentalbrain.com/ai/).
## How the numbers are made Each airport is searched repeatedly across trip lengths and pick-up months; a report is published only once enough searches agree. Second-driver fees are the suppliers' own quoted fees (a fee nobody publishes is never counted as free). Desk excess-cover prices come only from each supplier's own published price list, with the source and the date read. Full method: [carrentalbrain.com/methodology](https://carrentalbrain.com/methodology). ## Affiliate disclosure Car Rental Brain is free. Booking happens on DiscoverCars through the link the tools return, and Car Rental Brain earns a commission on bookings, at no extra cost to the person booking. Results are ranked by the total the person will pay, never by commission. ## Privacy The tools take no personal data and need no account. Searches are logged without names or contact details. Privacy policy: [carrentalbrain.com/privacy](https://app.carrentalbrain.com/privacy). ## Contact hello@carrentalbrain.com ## Licence The files in this repository are licensed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE); see [NOTICE](NOTICE). The **Car Rental Brain name and logo are not covered by this licence** and remain the property of Jimi Walters. The server, its code and its data are not in this repository; use of the server is governed by [the terms](https://app.carrentalbrain.com/terms).

Free. No API key. No login. Read-only. **MCP endpoint (streamable HTTP):** ``` https://airfarebrain.com/mcp ``` Listed in the official [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as `com.airfarebrain/airfare-brain`. Website: [airfarebrain.com](https://airfarebrain.com) · Fee data: [airfarebrain.com/fees](https://airfarebrain.com/fees/) · For AI: [llms.txt](https://airfarebrain.com/llms.txt) ## Why it exists The fare a flight search shows is not what the trip costs. A cabin bag, a checked bag, a seat next to someone you know, checking in at the airport or paying by card can each add more than the fare itself, and the price goes up if you add them later or at the airport. Airfare Brain reads each airline's published fee pages, records every price with its source and date, and answers with the numbers, so an assistant can say what a flight will really cost. ## Tools | Tool | What it answers | |---|---| | `get_capabilities` | What is covered, how fees are researched and dated, what it does not do (no live fares, no booking) | | `list_airlines` | Every airline with a fee table: name, IATA code, the date its fees were checked, its page | | `airline_fees` | One airline's extras (bags, seats, priority, check-in, changes, payment): price range, when bought (at booking / later / at the airport), source URL, date checked | | `true_cost` | Fare + the extras the person chooses, for the whole party and each flight, with what it costs if added later or at the airport | | `trip_at_airport` | The whole trip into one airport: the flight's extras on an airline AND what car hire there really costs (Car Rental Brain's measured median per day), dated and linked | Ranges are shown exactly as the airline publishes them. A fee the airline does not publish is said to be unknown, never counted as free. Figures from a third party (only where the airline publishes none) are labelled "reported". ## Example questions - "I found a Ryanair flight for €39. What will it cost with a cabin bag and a 20kg bag, return?" - "Is easyJet or Wizz Air cheaper for two people with one checked bag between them?" - "What does Jet2 charge to choose a seat?" - "How much more is a bag at the airport than online on Wizz Air?" - "Does British Airways' Basic fare include a cabin bag?" - "Flying Ryanair into Malaga for a week with a 20kg bag and a hire car: what will it all cost?" ## Connect
Claude (claude.ai / Claude Desktop) Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → URL `https://airfarebrain.com/mcp`. Or in `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "airfare-brain": { "url": "https://airfarebrain.com/mcp" } } } ```
Claude Code (plugin) ``` /plugin marketplace add jimiwalters-cmyk/airfare-brain-mcp /plugin install airfare-brain@airfare-brain ``` Or add the server directly: `claude mcp add --transport http airfare-brain https://airfarebrain.com/mcp`
ChatGPT Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced → Developer mode → Create → MCP server URL `https://airfarebrain.com/mcp`, authentication: none.
Cursor / Windsurf / Cline / VS Code ```json { "mcpServers": { "airfare-brain": { "url": "https://airfarebrain.com/mcp" } } } ```
Stdio-only clients ```bash npx mcp-remote https://airfarebrain.com/mcp ```
Plain JSON All fee tables in one file: [airfarebrain.com/data/fees.json](https://airfarebrain.com/data/fees.json).
## How the numbers are made Each airline's fee pages are read by hand, every value is stored with the page it came from, a short quote and the date, and each table is re-checked monthly (a table past its re-check date is flagged on the site). Travellers can report what they actually paid; those reports are checked against the tables. ## Fee pages The same data as web pages, one per airline (checked bag, cabin bag, seats, with the date and the airline's own source): [Aer Lingus](https://airfarebrain.com/aer-lingus/) · [Air Canada](https://airfarebrain.com/air-canada/) · [Air France](https://airfarebrain.com/air-france/) · [Alaska Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/alaska-airlines/) · [American Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/american-airlines/) · [Austrian Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/austrian-airlines/) · [British Airways](https://airfarebrain.com/british-airways/) · [Delta Air Lines](https://airfarebrain.com/delta-air-lines/) · [easyJet](https://airfarebrain.com/easyjet/) · [Eurowings](https://airfarebrain.com/eurowings/) · [Finnair](https://airfarebrain.com/finnair/) · [Frontier Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/frontier-airlines/) · [Iberia](https://airfarebrain.com/iberia/) · [Jet2](https://airfarebrain.com/jet2/) · [JetBlue](https://airfarebrain.com/jetblue/) · [KLM](https://airfarebrain.com/klm/) · [Lufthansa](https://airfarebrain.com/lufthansa/) · [Norwegian](https://airfarebrain.com/norwegian/) · [Pegasus](https://airfarebrain.com/pegasus/) · [Ryanair](https://airfarebrain.com/ryanair/) · [SAS](https://airfarebrain.com/sas/) · [Southwest Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/southwest-airlines/) · [Swiss](https://airfarebrain.com/swiss/) · [TAP Air Portugal](https://airfarebrain.com/tap-air-portugal/) · [Transavia](https://airfarebrain.com/transavia/) · [Turkish Airlines](https://airfarebrain.com/turkish-ai …

# Skavio Agent Tools

Official connection metadata and documentation for Skavio LLC's hosted MCP tools and x402 HTTP API. This repository contains discovery metadata, not the production server source.

**Partner review / data-handling facts:** [public USDC MCP integration facts](guides/public-usdc-mcp-integration-facts.md). Maintainer: Skavio LLC; email: info@getskavio.com. GitHub contains metadata and documentation, **not** production source. Live runtime reports `1.30.0`; registry descriptor `1.1.5` is independently versioned.

**New practical guide:** [Verify an incoming USDC transfer from an AI agent using x402](guides/verify-usdc-with-x402.md) — live 0.02/0.03/0.05 USDC operation prices, free HTTP 402 discovery and payment-safe steps. [Try the hosted endpoint](https://getskavio.com/x402/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=x402_developers_20261023).

**LIVE — DeepSeek-only x402 HTTP Web APIs:** [Seven-route discovery](https://getskavio.com/.well-known/x402) · [OpenAPI](https://getskavio.com/x402/openapi.json). These four paid HTTP endpoints are separate from tenant-authenticated MCP Agent Tools:

| x402 HTTP tool | Route | Native Base USDC per request |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Web Fetch | `POST /x402/v1/web/fetch` | 0.01 |
| Web Search | `POST /x402/v1/web/search` | 0.02 |
| Web Extract | `POST /x402/v1/web/extract` | 0.02 |
| Extract + Analyze | `POST /x402/v1/web/extract/analyze` | 0.03 |

All four use DeepSeek Search, Fetch or Flash with no alternate provider. An unsigned call returns an x402-v2 HTTP 402 quote; compatible clients sign and retry with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. One real 0.01 USDC Web Fetch purchase on 28 October 2026 settled and delivered the requested result. Do not assume the other three have independent funded checkout results. Keys and signing remain in the buyer's wallet.

**Separate authenticated company Agent Tools:** [Legacy enterprise API integration notes](WEB_TOOLS.md). Those older web operations and their provider migration are not part of this new DeepSeek-only paid HTTP release.

## Use Skavio in Cursor and Claude Desktop

[**Connection instructions and ready-to-copy Cursor / Claude Desktop JSON**](MCP_CLIENT_SETUP.md) · [Cursor config](examples/cursor-mcp.json) · [Claude Desktop config](examples/claude-desktop-mcp.json). The publicly discoverable MCP server is `https://getskavio.com/mcp`; separate OAuth-protected Processing MCP is at `https://getskavio.com/processing/mcp`. Plain MCP clients do **not** automatically process x402 payments.

Connect an MCP client using Streamable HTTP at **https://getskavio.com/mcp**. Discovery and the `skavio_catalog` tool are free. Paid invocations use x402 MCP v2: inspect `PaymentRequired`, then retry with an authorization supplied by your wallet client in `params._meta["x402/payment"]`. Keep wallet keys in your own client. Paid MCP invocations accept native Circle USDC via x402 v2 on Base (`eip155:8453`) or Solana (`solana:5eykt4UsFv8P8NJdTREpY1vzqKqZKvdp`). The standalone HTTP Verify, Match and Evidence PDF routes accept Base USDC only. Obtain current payment requirements from the service.

| Tool | Advertised USDC per invocation | Purpose |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| skavio_catalog | Free | Discover capabilities |
| verify_native_usdc | 0.02 | Inspect native USDC transfer evidence |
| match_native_usdc_payment | 0.03 | Match recipient and exact amount |
| usdc_transfer_evidence_pdf | 0.05 | Receive bounded blockchain evidence PDF |
| domain_dns_tls_audit | 0.05 | Bounded public-domain DNS/TLS audit |

Transfer inspection supports Base, Polygon, Arbitrum, Optimism, Ethereum, Avalanche and Solana. MCP x402 payment supports Base and Solana; the standalone HTTP x402 routes remain Base-only. Evidence PDFs are not tax invoices.

HTTP documentation: https://getskavio.com/x402/docs

The three established Base USDC verification routes remain public: `/x402/v1/usdc/verify`, `/x402/v1/usdc/match`, and `/x402/v1/usdc/evidence.pdf`. Four additional paid DeepSeek web POST routes are listed above; all seven are indexed in the canonical discovery document.

Public unsigned challenge and discovery checks do not establish successful funded settlement or profitability. No revenue claim is made. The current public `tools/list` also advertises tenant-authenticated document, OCR, invoice, audio and web Agent Tools. These require a valid Agent Tools credential and cannot be used anonymously. The **separate** OAuth-protected Processing API and its developer kit are at https://github.com/skavio-eu/skavio-processing-api.

Published in the official MCP Registry as `eu.skavio/paid-micro-apis`, version `1.1.5`: https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers/eu.skavio%2Fpaid-micro-apis/versions/1.1.5. Other directory registrations are tracked separately. Prices and capabilities may change; inspect current server responses before authorizing payment.

## USDC payment verification for AI agents

Skavio USDC Payment Verification — x402 API inspects native Circle USDC transfers, matches an exact recipient and decimal amount, and generates blockchain evidence PDFs. Use it for merchant payment reconciliation, accountant transaction review and agent workflows. PDF evidence is not a tax invoice or a guarantee of third-party authorization.

# StarReel MCP > Turn a script into a finished, downloadable short-drama episode — from Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client. **StarReel** is a prepaid AI video-production pipeline. This MCP server exposes the whole factory — **120+ tools** covering every stage — so an AI agent can take a raw script all the way to a finished `.mp4`: ``` script → AI rewrite → cast / scenes / props extraction → storyboards → character portraits & sheets (anchor the people) + scene plates (anchor the backdrops) → keyframes → video shots → voiceover (TTS) → final cut (.mp4 link) ``` It is a thin, open client: all the heavy lifting (character-consistency gates, frame chaining, best-of-N auditing, billing) runs server-side at [starreel.ai](https://starreel.ai). ## Quick start 1. Create an API key with `produce` scope in **StarReel → Settings → API Keys** (`srk_live_...`, shown once). 2. Add the server to Claude Code: ```bash claude mcp add starreel -e STARREEL_API_KEY=srk_live_xxx -- npx -y @starreel/mcp ``` Or install the **Claude Code plugin** — MCP server + agent skill in one step (set `STARREEL_API_KEY` in your shell first): ```text /plugin marketplace add starreel/starreel-mcp /plugin install starreel@starreel ``` 3. Ask your agent: *"Take this script and produce a full episode: ``"* — it will quote each paid stage first and only spend after you confirm. ### Tool-catalog language Tool descriptions and the server instructions are authored in Simplified Chinese. Set `STARREEL_MCP_LANG=en` for the English edition: the server instructions (the entry-point decision tree) are shipped in English; tool descriptions are being translated in batches and any tool without an English entry yet falls back to Chinese (nothing goes blank — the startup log on stderr reports the current coverage, e.g. `lang=en ⚠ English catalog 40/230`). The same switch sends `Accept-Language` so backend-provided labels follow it: ```bash claude mcp add starreel -e STARREEL_API_KEY=srk_live_xxx -e STARREEL_MCP_LANG=en -- npx -y @starreel/mcp ``` ## Works with any MCP client Requires Node ≥ 18 (`npx`). The **standard config** below works as-is in **Cursor · Windsurf · Cline / Roo Code · Claude Desktop · Trae · Cherry Studio · Chatbox · DeepChat** and any client that reads an `mcpServers` JSON block: ```json { "mcpServers": { "starreel": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@starreel/mcp"], "env": { "STARREEL_API_KEY": "srk_live_xxx" } } } } ``` Clients with their own format:
Codex CLI — ~/.codex/config.toml ```toml [mcp_servers.starreel] command = "npx" args = ["-y", "@starreel/mcp"] env = { "STARREEL_API_KEY" = "srk_live_xxx" } ```
VS Code (Copilot agent mode) — .vscode/mcp.json or user mcp.json ```json { "servers": { "starreel": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@starreel/mcp"], "env": { "STARREEL_API_KEY": "srk_live_xxx" } } } } ```
Gemini CLI — ~/.gemini/settings.json ```json { "mcpServers": { "starreel": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@starreel/mcp"], "env": { "STARREEL_API_KEY": "srk_live_xxx" } } } } ```
No Node / can't run npx? (Coze, Dify, GPTs, custom agents) Drive the same pipeline over REST (`/v1/produce/*`) and paste [`SKILL.md`](./SKILL.md) into your system prompt — it carries the full workflow order, billing disciplines, and failure playbook. See the [API docs](https://api.shortreelai.com/docs/mcp).

readme.markdown:
# Remote Desktop Commander

**Build, explore, automate on your computer — from anywhere.**

Reach your computer's filesystem and terminal from any AI app that supports remote MCP connectors. Remote Desktop Commander is a hosted [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that relays a secure connection to your real machine, giving your AI assistant the same full file and shell access as the local server — without you needing to be at the keyboard.

- **Server endpoint:** `https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.0)
- **Dashboard:** [mcp.desktopcommander.app](https://mcp.desktopcommander.app)
- **Status:** currently in beta
- **Demo:** [watch the video](https://youtu.be/C2kH5itFsGg)

> This repository hosts the public manifests, documentation and issue tracker for the hosted service. The service implementation is not open source. For the open-source local (stdio) server, see [DesktopCommanderMCP](https://github.com/wonderwhy-er/DesktopCommanderMCP).

## What you can do

- **Build from scratch** — create features and applications with simple commands
- **Manage development environments** — set up servers, configure systems, handle processes
- **Explore existing codebases** — navigate and understand complex repositories
- **Edit documents in place** — work on Word, Excel, and PDF files where they live on disk
- **Manage context and documentation** — keep track of project details and technical specifications
- **Control multiple machines** — pair several computers and address them by name in one conversation

## Quick start

### 1. Start the device agent

On the computer you want to control:

```bash
npx @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander@latest remote
```

Your browser opens to a verification page showing a pairing code (also printed in the terminal — a standard OAuth device-flow check). Sign in, confirm the codes match, and the terminal reports "Device ready". Keep the agent running: close the terminal, no access.

### 2. Connect your AI client

Each client walks you through OAuth sign-in on first connect.

**claude.ai / Claude Desktop** — Settings → Connectors → **Add custom connector**, then enter:

```
https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp
```

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http remote-desktop-commander https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp
```

(If you work inside a checkout of this repo, Claude Code also picks up the included [`.mcp.json`](.mcp.json) automatically.)

**ChatGPT** — Settings → Apps & Connectors → Advanced settings → enable **Developer mode** (requires a plan that includes it), then **Create connector** and enter:

```
https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp
```

**Cursor** — one click: [**Add to Cursor**](cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=remote-desktop-commander&config=eyJ1cmwiOiAiaHR0cHM6Ly9tY3AuZGVza3RvcGNvbW1hbmRlci5hcHAvbWNwIn0=). Or add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` manually:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "remote-desktop-commander": {
      "url": "https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** — install the agent plugin (bundles this server):

```bash
copilot plugin install desktop-commander/remote-desktop-commander
```

Or add the server directly to `.vscode/mcp.json` in your workspace (or your user-level `mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "remote-desktop-commander": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.desktopcommander.app/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

**Gemini CLI:**

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/desktop-commander/remote-desktop-commander
```

### 3. Try it

These work against any machine running the agent, no setup needed:

> "List the contents of my home directory and tell me what's there."
>
> "Create a folder called ai-test in my Documents folder. Inside it, write a short Python script that prints the date, and run it."
>
> "Start a Python REPL on my machine, import pandas, and tell me which version is installed. Keep the session alive."
>
> "Search my home directory for files modified in the last 24 hours and group them by folder."

Full walkthrough with troubleshooting: [docs/SETUP.md](docs/SETUP.md)

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or newer (for `npx`) on each computer you want to control
- One terminal running the device agent per machine
- Works on **macOS, Windows, and Linux**

## Available tools

| Category | Tools |
|---|---|
| **Read & explore** | Read File, Read Multiple Files, List Directory, Get File Info |
| **Search** | Start Search, Get More Search Results, Stop Search, List Active Searches |
| **Write & edit** | Write File, Edit File Block, Move or Rename File, Create Directory, Write or Modify PDF |
| **Terminal & processes** | Start Process, Send Input to Process, Read Process Output, List Active Sessions, List System Processes, Terminate Session, Kill System Process |
| **Devices & account** | List Paired Devices, Current User Info, Ping Device, Shutdown Device Agent |
| **Configuration & help** | Get Configuration, Set Configuration Value, Get Prompt Library, Get Recent Tool Activity, Get Usage Statistics, Submit Feedback |

## How it works

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AI as AI app (web, mobile, desktop)
    participant S as mcp.desktopcommander.app
    participant D as Your computer (device agent)
    AI->>S: MCP tool call (OAuth 2.0 bearer)
    S->>D: relayed to your paired device
    D->>D: executes locally
    D->>S: result
    S->>AI: MCP response
```

- Authentication is standard **OAuth 2.0 with PKCE**; devices pair via the OAuth **device authorization flow** (the short-code approval you see at setup).
- The server only accesses data explicitly requested through tool calls; transmission is encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS).
- A machine is reachable **only while its device agent is running** — stop it with `Ctrl+C` and access ends. Devices can also be reviewed and revoked at any time from the [dashboard](https://mcp.desktopcommander.app).
- Tools execute with **your user account's permissions** on the paired

readme.markdown:
# exomem

Durable memory with sources, proof, history, and review for MCP-capable agents.

exomem turns an owned Markdown/Obsidian vault into a local knowledge substrate
for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, chatbots, CLI agents, and any client that can
call MCP tools. Your files stay plain, local, portable, and editable outside the
server.

```text
agent -> MCP tools -> exomem -> your Markdown / Obsidian vault
```

## Prove it in 30 seconds

```bash
uvx exomem demo
```

One command, no install, no config, no vault of your own needed:

```text
exomem demo — bundled sample vault, keyword mode, fully local
vault: /tmp/exomem-demo-XXXXXX

1. doctor: PASS (0.8s)
2. find "retrieval": PASS (0.1s)
   - Knowledge Base/Sources/Sessions/2026-06-30-sample-session.md
   - Knowledge Base/Notes/Insights/retrieval-needs-owned-files.md
3. get retrieval insight: PASS (0.0s)
   - title: Retrieval needs owned files
   - type: insight
   - excerpt: Local-first knowledge tools should retrieve from files the user already owns.
4. audit: PASS (0.0s)

demo PASS — total 1.0s. This is your proof: agents search files you own.
Next: connect your own vault with `exomem setup`
```

Runs fully local and read-only against a sample vault bundled in the package.
Add `--keep` to leave that copy on disk afterward and open it in Obsidian.

## Install in one line

**Mac / Linux** — paste into Terminal:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Artexis10/exomem/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

**Windows** — paste into PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Artexis10/exomem/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex
```

Either one installs `uv`, installs exomem, and walks you through `exomem setup`,
which wires up **every agent client on the machine** — Claude Code and Codex both
get the MCP server, all ten skills, and the capture/retrieve hooks.

Safe to run again later — it skips whatever's already done. If it can't prompt
you interactively (e.g. run from another script), it prints the exact command to
run next instead of guessing. Prefer to run each step yourself? See below or the
full manual walkthrough in
[QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/Artexis10/exomem/blob/main/QUICKSTART.md).

### Claude Code: install as a plugin

The plugin carries the skills and hooks. Its MCP entry is an optional shared
HTTP URL; it deliberately does **not** auto-start a full stdio server in every
Claude Code session:

```
/plugin marketplace add Artexis10/exomem
/plugin install exomem@exomem
```

Then choose the route. If you already run Exomem as a service for phone or
hosted access, reuse that one authenticated core:

```bash
exomem setup --vault "/path/to/vault" --mcp-url https://<host>/mcp
```

For local-only use, run `exomem setup --vault "/path/to/vault" --stdio`.
Stdio is intentionally explicit because each client session owns its process
and can load its own embedding runtime. When updating from an older plugin,
run `/plugin update exomem@exomem`, then `/reload-plugins` or restart Claude
Code before rerunning setup.

### claude.ai and ChatGPT

Neither platform can install skills programmatically — upload is manual. Build
the archives, then upload them in the client's settings:

```bash
exomem package-skills          # writes dist/skills/*.zip (all ten)
```

Point the client at your server as a connector (see
[docs/remote-quickstart.md](docs/remote-quickstart.md)). Neither platform has a
hook system, so capture there is skill-driven rather than automatic.

## Set it up in 5 minutes

```bash
uv tool install exomem   # or: pip install exomem
exomem setup --vault "/path/to/your/Obsidian"
```

Re-running the one-line installer upgrades an existing uv-tool install instead
of leaving an older `exomem` command on PATH. `exomem --version --json` is a
model-free provenance check, so it also works in the intentional lean CLI paired
with a fuller managed service.

One command does the whole local setup: the wizard scans your vault and shows
what's already there, initializes `Knowledge Base/`, runs the `doctor`
preflight, registers the server with every client it detects (Claude Code and
Codex), and installs the skills into each.

If cwd `.env` or the process contains `EXOMEM_BASE_URL`, setup registers its
canonical `/mcp` endpoint with Claude Code and Codex so they share the existing
service. Otherwise it uses the explicit local stdio fallback. Use `--mcp-url`
to choose a service directly, `--stdio` to force local stdio, and
`--replace-client-registration` when you deliberately want to replace an
existing manual route. Native clients handle OAuth; setup never stores bearer
tokens.

Config files it did not create are treated as yours: it merges rather than
overwrites, backs the file up first, and prints the diff.

Already have a vault full of notes? That's the normal case: `adopt` gives a
scan-first, read-only report of what's there, suggested knowledge packs, and
safe copy/compile-planning next actions. Exomem only ever writes under `Knowledge Base/` — your
existing files stay untouched unless you explicitly copy or compile selected material. See
[QUICKSTART.md § Already have a vault full of notes?](QUICKSTART.md#already-have-a-vault-full-of-notes)
for the full contract, including daily-notes vaults. Re-running `setup` is
safe; completed steps report `[skipped]`. Non-interactive:
`exomem setup --yes --vault "/path" --lean`.

The individual steps (`exomem init` / `doctor` / `install-skill` /
`install-hook`, plus `claude mcp add`) still exist as the manual path — see
[QUICKSTART.md](QUICKSTART.md).

The skill installs under the Claude Code name `exomem` — the same name as the
connector, so skill, server, and tools all read as one product. The skill is
recommended for Claude Code —
the server gives Claude the tools, the skill is what makes it use them. Hooks
are local-client reliability helpers for Claude Code and Codex: a read-side
reminder before answers, a write-side reminder at natural stopping points, and
a shared local conti

# قرآن ريلز — Quran Reels ⭐

**المستودع**: https://github.com/Ansygroup/quran-reels (عام · `main`) · النشر: Vercel · الدفع المستقبلي: `scripts/gh_push.sh`

**صانع فيديو قرآن مجاني وفوري** — نسخة مطوّرة بالكامل من quranreels.tech تعمل **داخل المتصفح** بدون خوادم معالجة وبدون قوائم انتظار وبدون حدود يومية.

🔗 **الفكرة في سطر واحد:** اختر الآيات ← شاهد المعاينة الحية ← اضغط «إنشاء» ← حمّل ملف MP4 عمودي 1080×1920 خلال ثوانٍ.

🌐 **منشور الآن:** https://quran-reels-tau.vercel.app

---

## ✨ المزايا (مقارنة بالأصل)

| | الأصل | هذه النسخة |
|---|---|---|
| الإنشاء | طابور خادم 1–3 دقائق + 10 فيديوهات/يوم + 30 ثانية تبريد | **فوري داخل المتصفح** بلا حدود وبدون تسجيل |
| المعاينة | غير متوفرة | **معاينة حية أثناء التصميم** (تشغيل/تقديم/تنقل بين الآيات) |
| الخصوصية | رفع للخادم | **الصوت والصور لا تغادر جهازك** (رفع خلفية محلي) |
| الأدوات | 24 أداة | **32 أداة** تعمل دون إنترنت حيث أمكن |
| التصدير | MP4 من الخادم | MediaRecorder داخل المتصفح: **MP4/WebM** حسب دعم المتصفح، مع تقدير الأبعاد 9:16 / 1:1 / 16:9 |

## 🎬 الصانع

- **47 قارئًا** (كل ayah mp3 من everyayah عبر `/proxy` موحّد المصدر — مطلوب لالتقاط الصوت في التصدير)
- **114 سورة** + نطاق آيات يدوي أو «رسائل سريعة» (الصبر، السكينة، الرزق، التوبة… 324 مرجعًا متحققًا)
- **ترجمة داخل الفيديو بـ8 لغات** (إنجليزية، فرنسية، تركية، إندونيسية، أردية، إسبانية، إيطالية) + عربي مبسّط
- **14 خلفية** (10 صور مولّدة + 4 تدرّجات) + رفع صورة من جهازك (محلي فقط)
- أنماط بطاقة (card/glow/banner) × 4 ألوان ذهبي/زمردي/فضي/وردي، عدّ حجم الخط، علامة مائية، إهداء «صدقة جارية» بثلاثة أنماط، إيقاف الحركة، شارة عنوان السورة، شريط تقدّم، ترجمة قابلة للإخفاء
- **معاينة حقيقية**: صوت كل آية + رسم Canvas بنفس كود التصدير (لا مفاجآت)
- **تصدير لحظي**: `canvas.captureStream` + `MediaRecorder` مع شريط تقدّم وإمكانية الإلغاء، ثم تحميل/مشاركة/فيديو فوري

## 🧰 الأدوات الـ32

مواقيت الصلاة (12 طريقة + تحديد موقع دقيق بتوقيت المنطقة) · القبلة (بوصلة + SVG + خريطة) · التاريخ الهجري/الميلادي · أذكار الصباح والمساء (حصن المسلم كامل — 132 فئة) · المسبحة · أسماء الله الحسنى · آية اليوم · آيات بالموضوع · حلقة التلاوة · خطة الختمة · **الختمة الجماعية برابط قابل للمشاركة** · مخارج الحروف · إذاعة القرآن (بث مباشر) · الأحاديث (النووية/القدسية مضمّنة + البخاري ومسلم وأبو داود والترمذي والنسائي وابن ماجه والموطأ بتحميل كسول) · تخريج الحديث · مصمّم البطاقات PNG · حاسبة الزكاة · المواريث (شاملة فرع واردث ووصية ووصية مطلقة) · أسماء المولودين (1017 اسمًا) · ألوان E · التقويم الإسلامي · عدّاد المناسبات · عدّاد الإفطار · تنبيهات الأذان (إشعارات + جرس) · أعمال اليوم · متتبع الصيام · قضاء الصلاة · حاسبة الكفارة · تعلم الصلاة · المساجد القريبة (OpenStreetMap) · الدعاء المختار

## 🏗️ البنية

```
quran-reels/
├── server.py              # خادم محلي: ثابت + /proxy (قائمة بيضاء) + /api/ip + /api/app-config
├── vercel.json            # إعدادات Vercel: outputDirectory=public + إعادة توجيه /proxy → /api/proxy + كاش
├── .vercelignore          # ما لا يُرفع عند النشر
├── api/                   # دوال Serverless (Node) — مرآة كاملة لـ server.py
│   ├── proxy.js           # نفس عقد /proxy: 400/403/502 + كاش 6 ساعات + ACAO *
│   ├── ip.js              # نفس عقد /api/ip مع نفس البديل الافتراضي (القاهرة)
│   └── app-config.js      # إعدادات عامة (Supabase URL + المفتاح العام) من متغيرات البيئة
└── public/
    ├── index.html         # الصفحة الكاملة (SEO + JSON-LD + FAQ)

# Bird AI Marketplace

Skills for driving the [Bird](https://bird.com) platform from your coding agent. Your agent operates Bird through the `bird` CLI; the `bird` plugin in this marketplace installs the skills that teach it Bird's workflows, and on clients that read the plugin's MCP declaration it wires up Bird's hosted MCP server too.

## Quick start

Every client starts the same way: install the CLI and sign in.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh   # install the bird CLI
bird auth login                                            # sign in (browser, no API key)
```

On macOS or Linux you can also install with Homebrew: `brew install messagebird/tap/bird`.

Then jump to your client below. The fastest path is to paste the setup prompt and let your agent do the rest; a manual path is under each one.

## No Bird account yet?

`bird auth login` signs in to an account you already have. An agent with **no** account can create one from the terminal — no browser, no password. Three commands take you from nothing to a stored credential:

```bash
# 1. Sign up. Emails a six-digit code to the address; no password is set.
bird auth signup you@example.com

# 2. Verify. Read the code from that email, then exchange it for a single-use onboarding ticket.
bird auth verify-email you@example.com --code 123456
# → { "onboarding_ticket": "obt_…", "user_id": "usr_…" }

# 3. Create your first org + workspace. Consumes the ticket, then mints and stores the credential.
#    --region picks where the account and its data live (us1 or eu1); the CLI routes there for you.
bird auth create-org "Acme" --workspace-name "Production" --region us1 --onboarding-ticket obt_…

# Confirm it worked — reports the account, org, and workspace you're now acting as.
bird auth status
```

The code arrives by email, so it comes from outside the CLI — read it from the inbox and pass it to step 2. Signup and verification are region-agnostic; you pick the region once, at `create-org`, so there is no host or environment variable to set. Every step is self-describing: append `--help` for the flags, `--example` for a ready-to-edit request body, or `--response-schema` for what it returns — none of them need a credential, so an agent can plan the whole chain before running it. Full walkthrough: [Self-serve signup](https://bird.com/docs/ai/self-serve-signup).

## Any Agent Plugins client

The plugin ships a root `plugin.json` and `mcp.json` following [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org/specification), the portable plugin format. A client that implements the specification loads it from this repository as it is: the skills and the hosted MCP server, in one install. Point the client at `github.com/messagebird/bird-ai` and install `bird` from `plugins/bird`.

For a client with its own plugin format, or none, find it below.

## Claude Code

Paste this prompt into Claude Code and it installs the CLI, signs you in, installs the skills, and sends a test email:

```text
Bird is a communications platform you can operate end to end: email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice through one API and one login. Set Bird up for me, end to end.
1. Install the Bird CLI: run `curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh`.
2. Sign me in: run `bird auth login` and open the browser link for me.
3. Install Bird's skills so you know the workflows: run `claude plugin marketplace add messagebird/bird-ai`, then `claude plugin install bird@bird-ai`.
4. Confirm who I am: run `bird whoami`, which prints the email of the account you're acting as.
5. Send me a test email so I see it land in my own inbox: use my address from `bird whoami` as the recipient, send from onboarding@messagebird.dev, then confirm delivery with `bird email get`. Subject: "Your Bird account is ready". Body: "You're set up and ready to send. This email is the proof. Cheers, The Bird team".
Then let's discuss next steps, given what Bird can do.
```

Or install the plugin manually:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add messagebird/bird-ai
claude plugin install bird@bird-ai
```

**MCP server:** installing the plugin registers Bird's hosted server at `https://mcp.bird.com`, so there is nothing to configure. You do have to sign in once, because the server is OAuth-gated: run `/mcp`, select `bird`, press Enter, and choose **Authenticate**. Your browser opens Bird's consent screen; approve it and the tools work. Until then `claude mcp list` reports `bird` as `! Needs authentication` and every tool call fails. For a headless run (`claude -p`) there is no `/mcp` panel, so authenticate first with `claude mcp login bird`.

## Cursor

Paste this prompt into Cursor:

```text
Bird is a communications platform you can operate end to end: email, SMS, WhatsApp, and voice through one API and one login. Set Bird up for me, end to end.
1. Install the Bird CLI: run `curl -fsSL https://cli.bird.com/install.sh | sh`.
2. Sign me in: run `bird auth login` and open the browser link for me.
3. Give yourself Bird's skills (Cursor installs plugins through its UI, so set them up by file instead): fetch the skills from https://github.com/messagebird/bird-ai and write them into `.cursor/rules/` as `.mdc` files.
4. Confirm who I am: run `bird whoami`, which prints the email of the account you're acting as.
5. Send me a test email so I see it land in my own inbox: use my address from `bird whoami` as the recipient, send from onboarding@messagebird.dev, then confirm delivery with `bird email get`. Subject: "Your Bird account is ready". Body: "You're set up and ready to send. This email is the proof. Cheers, The Bird team".
Then let's discuss next steps, given what Bird can do.
```

To set the skills up by hand, add the `messagebird/bird-ai` marketplace under **Settings → Plugins**, or write the skills from this repo into `.cursor/rules/` as `.mdc` files yourself.

**MCP server:** add the hosted server once in `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "bird": { "url": "https://mcp.bird.com" }
  }
}
```

readme.markdown:
Sitepeel for Claude Code and Codex

Give your coding agent any website's DESIGN.md, a clone prompt, an AI slop check, its files, fonts, colors and tech stack.

  sitepeel.dev ·
  MCP server ·
  DESIGN.md library ·
  Chrome extension

This is the Sitepeel plugin for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. It connects your agent to [Sitepeel's MCP server](https://sitepeel.dev/mcp/), which opens public web pages in a real browser and measures them. Your agent can then save a site's DESIGN.md into your project, rebuild a page's layout, check a landing page for AI slop, pull a logo or icon set, or tell you which fonts, colors and framework a site uses. The plugin also adds five short commands for the common jobs.

## Install in Claude Code

In a Claude Code session, add this repository as a marketplace and install the plugin:

```text
/plugin marketplace add Josephbadigar/sitepeel
/plugin install sitepeel@sitepeel
```

On Claude Code 2.1.275 or later, one line does both:

```text
/plugin install sitepeel --marketplace Josephbadigar/sitepeel
```

From your terminal instead:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add Josephbadigar/sitepeel
claude plugin install sitepeel@sitepeel
```

Start a new session after installing. Run `/mcp` to see the Sitepeel server and its tools.

## Install in Codex

Add this repository as a plugin marketplace, then install the plugin:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add Josephbadigar/sitepeel
codex plugin add sitepeel@sitepeel
```

You can also open `/plugins` inside Codex, pick the Sitepeel tab and install it from there. Start a new session afterwards so Codex loads the skills and tools.

## Sign in

The first time your agent uses Sitepeel, it opens the browser so you can sign in to Sitepeel (free). It stays connected after that. There is no API key to copy.

## Commands

In Claude Code, type these after installing. In Codex, the same skills are named `$sitepeel:design-md`, `$sitepeel:clone` and so on, or you can ask in plain words.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/sitepeel:design-md stripe.com` | Saves the site's DESIGN.md in your project root, so new UI follows its colors, fonts and spacing |
| `/sitepeel:clone linear.app/pricing` | Rebuilds the page's look and layout in your project, with placeholders for the site's own text and images |
| `/sitepeel:slop example.com` | Scores how AI-generated the page looks (0 to 100) and lists each tell with a fix |
| `/sitepeel:assets vercel.com svg` | Lists the page's images, SVGs, icons, videos and other files, and downloads the ones you pick |
| `/sitepeel:inspect notion.com` | Finds the page's fonts, color palette and tech stack |

You don't have to use the commands. Once the plugin is installed you can just ask, for example "get the DESIGN.md of linear.app and restyle my settings page to match it".

## Tools

The plugin adds one remote MCP server, `https://sitepeel.dev/mcp`, with these tools:

| Tool | What it returns |
| --- | --- |
| `get_design_md` | A site's DESIGN.md in the Google Stitch format: colors, type, spacing, radii and components |
| `search_design_library` | Brands from the DESIGN.md library that match a name, font, color, style or category |
| `clone_prompt` | One prompt that rebuilds a page's look and layout |
| `check_ai_slop` | A 0 to 100 score, a verdict, the tells found with a fix for each, and a fix prompt |
| `extract_assets` | Images, SVGs, icons, videos, audio, fonts, Lottie and 3D files, with download links |
| `find_fonts` | Font families, where each is used, weights, sizes and the type scale |
| `get_color_palette` | The palette with roles, hex values and CSS variables |
| `detect_tech_stack` | Framework, CMS, hosting, libraries and analytics, with the evidence found |

More tools are on the way, such as full-page screenshots and responsive checks. They show up in the plugin on their own when they go live on the server, with no update needed.

Every result links to its page on sitepeel.dev. Please credit "Sitepeel (sitepeel.dev)" when you use one.

## Other apps

Any app that supports remote MCP servers can use Sitepeel without this plugin. Add `https://sitepeel.dev/mcp` as a Streamable HTTP server. For example:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http sitepeel https://sitepeel.dev/mcp
codex mcp add sitepeel --url https://sitepeel.dev/mcp
```

Setup for Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini CLI, Zed, Claude Desktop and claude.ai is on [sitepeel.dev/mcp](https://sitepeel.dev/mcp/).

## What the plugin does on your machine

The plugin has no code of its own. It holds:

- `.mcp.json`, which points your agent at `https://sitepeel.dev/mcp`
- five skills in `skills/`, plain instructions that tell the agent which Sitepeel tool to call
- the manifests for Claude Code (`.claude-plugin/`) and Codex (`.codex-plugin/`, `.agents/plugins/`)

When your agent calls a tool, it sends the page address you gave to sitepeel.dev, which opens that public page and sends back the result. Your project files are not sent. The skills only write to your project when you ask, for example to save DESIGN.md or download a file. See the [privacy policy](https://sitepeel.dev/privacy/) and [terms](https://sitepeel.dev/terms/).

## Good to know

- Only public pages work. For pages behind a login, use the [Sitepeel Chrome extension](https://sitepeel.dev/extension/), which reads the page open in your browser.
- A new page takes about 15 to 40 seconds to measure. If a tool answers "pending", the agent calls it again.
- Results are an independent measurement of the public page, not the site owner's official design system. A site's text, images and logos belong to its owner.
- Ready DESIGN.md files for more than 160 brands are in the [DESIGN.md library](https://github.com/Josephbadigar/design-md), with style guides at [sitepeel.dev/design-md/examples](https://sitepeel.dev/design-md/examples/).

## Support

Questions or problems: support@sitepeel.dev or [sitepeel.dev/contact](https://sitepeel.dev/contact/).

readme.markdown:
# Altmetric MCP Server

Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that enables AI agents to access Altmetric APIs for tracking the attention and reach of research outputs across news outlets, policy documents, social media, and other online platforms.

Altmetric monitors where research is being discussed beyond traditional academic citations - from mainstream media coverage to policy citations, patent references, and social media engagement - providing a comprehensive view of real-world research impact.

There are two ways to connect:

- **Hosted server (recommended)** - point your AI client at `https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp` and sign in with your Altmetric account. No API keys to copy or store, and you automatically get the tools for whatever you have access to (Explorer, Details Page, or both). Start here.
- **Run locally** - run the server on your own machine with your own API keys, over stdio. For offline use or when you'd rather manage keys directly. See *Run locally with your own API keys* below.

## What access you need

The server works with access to either one of Altmetric's APIs on its own - the **Details Page API** or the **Explorer API** - and gives you the tools for whichever you have. To get the full potential of Altmetric, having **both is strongly recommended**, because they answer different questions:

- **Details Page API** - the attention for a specific research output, looked up by identifier (DOI, PubMed ID, etc.), and a search of recent attention by timeframe.
- **Explorer API** - searching, filtering and aggregating research outputs, mentions, audience demographics and journals across the whole Altmetric database, and across your own institution's outputs.

With only one, you get only that API's tools. See [Tools](#tools) for which tools come with each API, and [request API access](https://www.altmetric.com/solutions/altmetric-api/) if you're missing one.

## Connect to the hosted server (recommended)

The easiest way to use Altmetric in your AI client is the hosted server at `https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp`. Point your client at that URL and sign in with your Altmetric account when prompted - the client runs a standard OAuth flow in your browser, so there are no API keys to copy or store. You get exactly the tools your account has access to.

### Claude Desktop

1. Open **Settings → Customize → Connectors** and click **Add custom connector**.
2. Name it `Altmetric` and enter the URL `https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp`.
3. Click **Add**, then **Connect**, and sign in when the browser window opens.

Verify by asking Claude: *"Use the Altmetric tools to look up the attention score for DOI 10.1038/nature12373"*

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http altmetric https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp
```

Then run `/mcp` inside Claude Code, select **altmetric**, and authenticate - a browser window opens for sign-in.

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (per project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "Altmetric": {
      "url": "https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Cursor runs a browser sign-in the first time the server is used.

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code 1.101 or later):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "Altmetric": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Open the Command Palette, run **MCP: List Servers**, select **Altmetric**, and start it; sign in when prompted.

### ChatGPT

Open **Settings → Connectors → Advanced** and turn on **Developer mode**, then **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter `https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp`, and complete the OAuth sign-in. Requires a paid plan (Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, or Edu); custom connectors aren't available on the free tier. All Altmetric tools are read-only, so the read-only restriction on Plus/Pro plans doesn't limit them.

### Other MCP clients

Any client that supports the **Streamable HTTP** transport with OAuth can connect. Point it at `https://mcp.altmetric.com/mcp`. On the first request the server returns `401` with a `WWW-Authenticate` header pointing at its discovery document (`/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`), which the client uses to run the OAuth flow against Altmetric Explorer automatically.

### How sign-in works

The hosted server is an OAuth 2.1 **resource server**. Your client obtains a bearer token from Altmetric Explorer (the authorization server) for the `mcp` scope. The server exchanges that token for your account's entitlements and calls the Altmetric APIs on your behalf - your bearer token is **never** forwarded to those APIs. The advertised toolset reflects your entitlements, so you only ever see the tools for the products you can use.

## Example prompts

Once connected, ask in plain language - your client picks the tool. Each of these exercises a
different one:

| Prompt | Tool it uses | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| *"What's the Altmetric attention score for DOI 10.1038/nature12373, and how much of it came from news versus policy?"* | `get_citation_counts` | Details Page, free tier |
| *"Which research outputs were picked up by policy documents in the last month?"* | `search_citations` | Details Page, free tier |
| *"Show my institution's 2025 research outputs that got news coverage, ranked by attention."* | `explore_research_outputs` | Explorer, institutional |
| *"Which countries is the audience for our cancer research in, over the past year?"* | `explore_demographics` | Explorer, institutional |

You only see the tools your account is entitled to, so the Explorer prompts need institutional
access. The full toolset is in [Tools](#tools) below.

## Data sources and licensing

Every tool calls Altmetric's own APIs - the Details Page API and the Explorer API, both first-party
Altmetric (Digital Science) services. The server proxies no third-party API and holds no third-party
data of its own.

What those APIs return includes attention collected from thir

readme.markdown:
# House AI for Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and other AI apps

House AI is an AI interior design studio. This repo connects it to AI assistants and coding agents through the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). Share a photo of a room, a house or a yard, pick a style, and House AI shows you a photorealistic redesign of that same space. You can also preview a wall paint color or new flooring, empty a cluttered room, furnish an empty one, and find real furniture and decor like the pieces in your design.

House AI is used in 175+ countries and is a top 10 design app in the US, Canada and Australia.

- **Server:** `https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Docs:** https://www.houseaiapp.com/connector
- **Sign-in:** your House AI account (email, Google or Apple). Designs use your House AI credits, exactly as in the app, and are saved to your House AI history. Browsing styles works without signing in.

## Connect

### Claude (claude.ai, Desktop, mobile)
Settings, then Connectors, then **Add custom connector**, and enter `https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp`. Claude asks you to sign in the first time a tool needs your account.

### ChatGPT
Open Plugins, select **+**, then **Add custom MCP server**. Enter `https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp`, choose OAuth, and select **Create as a plugin** ([OpenAI's steps](https://developers.openai.com/plugins/deploy/connect-chatgpt)). You can attach a room photo right in the chat.

### Claude Code
As a plugin from this repo:
```
/plugin marketplace add Apex-Byte-Technologies/house-ai-mcp
/plugin install house-ai@house-ai-mcp
```
Or directly:
```
claude mcp add --transport http house-ai https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp
```
Then run `/mcp` to sign in.

### Cursor and VS Code
Use the **Add to Cursor** and **Install in VS Code** buttons on https://www.houseaiapp.com/connector, or add this server:
```json
{ "mcpServers": { "house-ai": { "url": "https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp" } } }
```

### Codex
```toml
[mcp_servers.house_ai]
url = "https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp"
```
Then run `codex mcp login house_ai`.

### Gemini CLI
```
gemini extensions install https://github.com/Apex-Byte-Technologies/house-ai-mcp
```

### Any other MCP client
Add `https://mcp.houseaiapp.com/mcp` as a Streamable HTTP server. If your client can't sign in with OAuth, create a personal API token at https://www.houseaiapp.com/app/connector and send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Sign-in |
|---|---|---|
| `search_design_styles` | Browse interior, exterior and landscaping styles | No |
| `get_design_style` | A style's palette, materials, furniture, lighting and decor | No |
| `get_house_ai_app_link` | Download link for the House AI app | No |
| `get_photo_upload_link` | A private, 30-minute photo upload page | Yes |
| `redesign_room` | Redesign a room from a photo in a chosen style | Yes |
| `redesign_exterior` | Restyle a house exterior or redesign a yard | Yes |
| `paint_walls` | Preview a new wall paint color | Yes |
| `change_flooring` | Preview new flooring | Yes |
| `empty_room` | Remove furniture and clutter from a room photo | Yes |
| `furnish_empty_room` | Virtually stage an empty room | Yes |
| `find_furniture_and_decor` | Search real furniture and decor, optionally under a budget | Yes |
| `shop_this_look` | Find products like an item in a design | Yes |
| `list_my_designs` | Your recent House AI designs | Yes |
| `get_my_credits` | Designs you can still make today or this plan period | Yes |

Each design uses one House AI credit. Product results link to each retailer's own site.

## Try asking

- "Help me redesign my living room in a Japandi style."
- "Here's a photo of my kitchen. Show me a modern farmhouse remodel."
- "What would my house look like with white siding and a black front door?"
- "Find a jute rug under $200 like the one in that design."

## Privacy, terms and support

- Privacy policy: https://www.houseaiapp.com/privacy-policy#connector
- Terms of service: https://www.houseaiapp.com/tos
- Support: https://www.houseaiapp.com/contact-us or support@addictingelements.com

The House AI server itself is not open source. This repo holds the public connection files (Claude Code plugin, Cursor plugin, Gemini CLI extension and MCP Registry entry).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE) for the files in this repo.
