readme.markdown:
# Hustle Got Real MCP Server

Connect Codex, Claude or any MCP client to Hustle Got Real (HGR). Analyze store data, review listings, monitor stock and prices, and manage dropshipping workflows across eBay, Amazon, Shopify and more with live account context.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/` (Streamable HTTP)
- ChatGPT compatibility endpoint: `https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/mcp`.
- **Auth:** OAuth, sign in with your Hustle Got Real account
- **Website:** https://hustlegotreal.com/mcp/
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.hustlegotreal/mcp`

## What you can do

- Find products and sources, and list them to your sales channels in bulk.
- Review listings, listing quality, and price and stock history; relist, update or end listings.
- Manage pricing rules and Price Warrior repricing.
- Work through orders: auto-ordering, purchase status, dispatch, tracking IDs and shipping details.
- Read dashboards, sales, analytics and notifications.
- Run AI publisher agents and AI listing optimization.
- Manage channels, templates, business policies, virtual assistants, support tickets and the affiliate dashboard.

## Connect

The server uses OAuth. Your client opens a browser window, you sign in with your Hustle Got Real account and approve access. You do not copy an API key.

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter `https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/` and select **Connect**.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http hgr https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and authenticate `hgr`.

### Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add hgr --url https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/
codex mcp login hgr
```

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "hgr": { "url": "https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/" }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"hgr","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/"}'
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http hgr https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/
```

### ChatGPT and other clients

Add a custom connector (in ChatGPT, developer mode) with the URL `https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/`. Any client that supports Streamable HTTP and MCP OAuth works.

## Tools

The server exposes about 170 tools. Your client gets the current list and schemas from `tools/list`. Examples:

- **Listings:** `hgr_get_listings`, `hgr_get_active_listings`, `hgr_get_listing_price_history`, `hgr_get_listing_stock_history`, `hgr_update_listing`, `hgr_relist_listing`, `hgr_terminate_listing`
- **Pricing:** `hgr_get_pricing_rules`, `hgr_add_pricing_rule`, `hgr_update_pricing_rule`, `hgr_get_price_warrior`, `hgr_update_price_warrior_settings`
- **Orders:** `hgr_get_sales`, `hgr_search_orders`, `hgr_process_order_lines`, `hgr_mark_order_lines_as_purchased`, `hgr_generate_tracking_id`, `hgr_get_autoordering_configuration`
- **AI agents:** `hgr_get_ai_agent_dashboard`, `hgr_create_ai_publisher_agent`, `hgr_get_ai_publisher_history`, `hgr_post_ai_publishnow`
- **Account and support:** `hgr_get_authenticated_user`, `hgr_get_subscription_summary`, `hgr_list_channels`, `hgr_list_support_tickets`, `hgr_create_support_ticket`

## Authentication and account

OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration, tied to your HGR account. No shared public token.

You need a Hustle Got Real account. See the plans on hustlegotreal.com.

## Links

- Website: https://hustlegotreal.com
- MCP setup page: https://hustlegotreal.com/mcp/
- Privacy policy: https://hustlegotreal.com/privacy/

## About this repository

This repository is the public home of the hosted Hustle Got Real MCP server. It holds this setup guide and the registry metadata (`server.json` for the official MCP Registry, `glama.json` for Glama). The server runs as a hosted service at `https://mcp.hustlegotreal.com/`. Its source code is not in this repository.

Found a problem or have a question? Open an issue.

# Designelier MCP Server

Generate coordinated icon sets, spot illustrations and transparent design assets for websites and apps from any MCP client. Plan a pack from a short brief or your page, review the exact quote, and generate only after you confirm.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.designelier.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Auth:** OAuth, sign in with your Designelier account
- **Website:** https://designelier.com/mcp
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.designelier/mcp`

## What you can do

- Plan a matching icon set or spot illustrations (1 to 6 assets in one shared style and palette) from a short brief.
- Plan a full artwork pack for a website from its public URL.
- See the planned subjects, the style and the exact credit quote first. Planning is free.
- Generate only after you confirm the quote. Download a ZIP with SVG files and full-canvas and cropped transparent WebP files.

The SVG files embed raster artwork. They are not editable vector paths.

## Connect

The server uses OAuth. Your client opens a browser window, you sign in with your Designelier account and approve access. You do not copy an API key.

name: AutoContent
description: Turn documents, URLs and text into videos, podcasts, slides, infographics and recurring content.

readme.markdown:
# AutoContent MCP Server

Turn PDFs, URLs, documents, videos and text into podcasts, videos, slide decks, infographics, articles, guides, ebooks and quizzes from any MCP client. Your assistant plans the asset, shows the quote, and AutoContent generates it on your account.

- **Endpoint:** `https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1` (Streamable HTTP)
- **Auth:** OAuth, sign in with your AutoContent account
- **Website:** https://autocontentapi.com/mcp
- **Official MCP Registry:** `com.autocontentapi/platform`

## What you can do

- Create projects and add knowledge sources: PDFs, URLs, documents, videos and text.
- Generate videos (five video types), podcasts, slide decks, infographics, articles, practical guides, ebooks and quizzes.
- Preview a generation and its quote before you approve it, then edit results or give feedback.
- Set up recurring Content Loops that keep producing new content.
- Create custom voices and avatars for your brand, and check your usage.

## Connect

The server uses OAuth. Your client opens a browser window, you sign in with your AutoContent account and approve access. You do not copy an API key.

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, enter `https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1` and select **Connect**.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http autocontent https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1
```

Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code and authenticate `autocontent`.

### Codex CLI

```bash
codex mcp add autocontent --url https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1
codex mcp login autocontent
```

### Cursor

Add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "autocontent": { "url": "https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1" }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

```bash
code --add-mcp '{"name":"autocontent","type":"http","url":"https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1"}'
```

### Gemini CLI

```bash
gemini mcp add --transport http autocontent https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1
```

### ChatGPT and other clients

Add a custom connector (in ChatGPT, developer mode) with the URL `https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1`. Any client that supports Streamable HTTP and MCP OAuth works.

## Tools

Your client always gets the current list and schemas from `tools/list`. Main tools:

- **Projects and knowledge:** `create_project`, `list_projects`, `get_project`, `update_project`, `add_source`, `list_sources`, `set_project_logo`, `remove_project_logo`
- **Discovery and generation:** `get_capabilities`, `preview_generation`, `generate`, `get_generation`, `preview_generation_edit`, `edit_generation`, `feedback_asset`
- **Content Loops:** `create_content_loop`, `list_content_loops`, `update_content_loop`, `run_content_loop`
- **Brand resources:** `create_custom_voice`, `get_voice`, `delete_voice`, `create_custom_avatar`, `get_avatar`, `delete_avatar`
- **Account:** `get_usage`

More tools cover project archive, collections, source status and search, generation lists and cancellation, and asset details.

## Authentication and account

OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration. Sign in with your AutoContent account. Scopes: `platform.read`, `platform.write`, `platform.generate`, `platform.billing.read`.

You need an AutoContent account. Generations use your account balance.

## Links

- Website: https://autocontentapi.com
- MCP setup page: https://autocontentapi.com/mcp
- Documentation: https://docs.autocontentapi.com
- Privacy policy: https://autocontentapi.com/privacy-policy
- Terms: https://autocontentapi.com/terms

## About this repository

This repository is the public home of the hosted AutoContent MCP server. It holds this setup guide and the registry metadata (`server.json` for the official MCP Registry, `glama.json` for Glama). The server runs as a hosted service at `https://mcp.autocontentapi.com/v1`. Its source code is not in this repository.

Found a problem or have a question? Open an issue.

## License

The contents of this repository are available under the [MIT License](LICENSE).

readme.markdown:
Commercializer

Commercial strategy for medical device and life-science companies, read from the governed registers.
Bring it into the AI assistant you already use.

Connected, your assistant works on your company the way the [Commercializer](https://commercializer.ai) app does. It reads
the governed registers (FDA clearances and approvals, EU and other registrations, recalls and adverse event reports,
registered trials, patents, payments to clinicians, public tenders and company filings), cites every record it uses,
keeps the findings worth remembering on your company's profile, and runs workflows that deliver a pathway decision, a
submission checklist, a market entry plan, a competitor footprint or a company brief, asking you at each decision.

Everything it does happens as you, in the workspace you choose, and is listed on the **MCP** page of your workspace under
its name, where you can disconnect it at any time.

- **The server:** `https://commercializer.ai/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; sign in with OAuth 2.1, or use an API key).
- **This repository:** [`github.com/Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp`](https://github.com/Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp), the plugin and a guide for every assistant.
- **The page:** [commercializer.ai/product/assistant](https://commercializer.ai/product/assistant).
- **Let the assistant set itself up:** give it [`https://commercializer.ai/mcp/llms.txt`](https://commercializer.ai/mcp/llms.txt). It says how to connect from
  each client, how to sign in, how to work the workspace and every tool.

| **Claude Code** | `/plugin marketplace add Commercializer-ai/commercializer-mcp` | [Claude Code](docs/claude-code.md) |

| **Copilot coding agent** (on github.com) | Repository settings → Copilot → MCP servers, with an API key | [Copilot coding agent](docs/copilot-coding-agent.md) |
| **Microsoft Copilot Studio** (agents for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams) | Tools → Add a tool → Model Context Protocol, OAuth dynamic discovery | [Copilot Studio](docs/microsoft-copilot-studio.md) |
| **Cursor** (editor and CLI) | [Add to Cursor](https://cursor.com/en/install-mcp?name=commercializer&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2NvbW1lcmNpYWxpemVyLmFpL21jcCJ9), or `cursor-agent mcp login commercializer` | [Cursor](docs/cursor.md) |
| **Codex** (CLI, IDE, app) | `codex mcp add commercializer --url https://commercializer.ai/mcp` | [Codex](docs/codex.md) |
| **Antigravity** (and Gemini CLI) | `serverUrl` in `mcp_config.json` | [Antigravity](docs/antigravity.md) |
| **Devin Desktop, Windsurf, Kiro, Zed, Goose and others** | the server URL, or `mcp-remote` for a stdio-only client | [Other clients](docs/other-clients.md) |
| **A script or your own code** | an API key as `Authorization: Bearer` | [API keys](docs/api-keys.md) |
| **Any assistant, on its own** | give it `https://commercializer.ai/mcp/llms.txt` | [For assistants](docs/agents.md) |

Signed in to Commercializer, the **MCP** page of your workspace walks the same steps for the assistant you pick and makes
an API key when you need one.

## The plugin

This repository is also a plugin: the server, a skill that teaches the assistant how to work the workspace (read before
stating a figure, cite every read, keep findings, use the tools, run workflows), and five skills you can call by name.

| Skill | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `ask` | Hands a question to Commercializer's agent; the answer comes back with every record cited. |

It follows the open [Agent Plugins](https://agent-plugins.org) format (`plugin.json`, `mcp.json`, `skills/`) that
ChatGPT, Codex, GitHub Copilot, VS Code and Cursor read, and carries a Claude Code manifest (`.claude-plugin/`) beside it.

name: Midplane
description: A gateway between AI agents and Postgres: table access, masking at the source, approvals and audit.

env.name: MIDPLANE_TOKEN
env.description: A token from `midplane token`, verified at start and on every call. It stays in this entry, so give it a --ttl (seconds) as long as the entry should work: the default is an hour.

readme.markdown: A gateway between AI agents and your Postgres databases. Every statement is checked against your policy and recorded before it runs. Quickstart · Documentation · Midplane Cloud Agents get useful once they can read your real tables, but a database role that reads every column and writes every row is not a control you can show a security reviewer. Midplane is that control. Agents connect to the gateway over MCP; it parses each statement with Postgres' own parser, decides it against your policy, records it, and only then runs it, with masks written into the query itself. ## What it enforces - **Table access**, denied by default, per table. - **Masking** at the source: hashes, partial values, generalized dates, NULLs, applied before any filter, join or aggregate sees the raw value. - **Guardrails**: one statement at a time, writes need a `WHERE`, no writes hidden in a `WITH`, reads in read-only transactions with timeouts. - **Approvals**: writes held for a person, bound to the exact statement and checked against the row count the approver saw. - **Containment**: once an agent reads a column labeled untrusted (support tickets, emails), its writes are held and secret tables are closed to it. - **An audit log** on the gateway's own disk, hash-chained, exported and verified with one command. The gateway runs in your network, next to your databases. It opens its connections to Midplane Cloud and to Midplane's relay, and neither connects to it. On your own machine or at [your own URL](https://midplane.ai/docs/gateway/deploy#your-own-url), agents connect to the gateway directly, with no relay. ## Get started - **A sample database, no account**: the [quickstart](#quickstart) below. - **Your own database, with Midplane Cloud**, for policy in a dashboard, approvals and a query log; the cloud never holds a database credential or sees a row. Follow [get started](https://midplane.ai/docs/get-started). Midplane Cloud is invite-only for now: [get access](https://midplane.ai/#get-access). - **Your own database, no account**: [local mode](https://midplane.ai/docs/gateway/local-mode). The gateway is the `midplane` npm package, run with `npx`, or the image `ghcr.io/midplaneai/midplane`. Both are built from this repository's tags with provenance, and the image is signed: [verifying a release](https://midplane.ai/docs/releases). ## Quickstart You need Node 24.16 or newer, Docker, and an MCP client such as Claude Code. ```sh git clone https://github.com/midplaneai/midplane.git cd midplane/examples/quickstart docker compose up -d --wait ``` Then follow [its steps](examples/quickstart): a sample shop database and the gateway in local mode, with nothing leaving your machine. Ask your agent: | Ask | What happens | | --- | --- | | "List our customers with their emails and phone numbers." | Emails hashed, phones cut to the last four digits, signup dates to the month | | "Delete all support tickets." | Denied: a write needs a `WHERE` | | "Mark ticket 2 as closed." | Held for approval; local mode has nobody to ask, so it's refused | | "Summarize ticket 1." | Its body carries a prompt injection; reading it taints the agent | | "Now show me the API keys." | Denied: a tainted agent can't read secret tables | In Midplane Cloud, **Try with sample data** runs the same sample linked, where the held write waits for your approval instead. ## Documentation [midplane.ai/docs](https://midplane.ai/docs): [how it works](https://midplane.ai/docs/how-it-works), [deploying the gateway](https://midplane.ai/docs/gateway/deploy), [configuration](https://midplane.ai/docs/gateway/configuration), [masking](https://midplane.ai/docs/policies/masking), [approvals and taint](https://midplane.ai/docs/policies/approvals-and-taint), [audit](https://midplane.ai/docs/audit) and [troubleshooting](https://midplane.ai/docs/troubleshooting). Its source is in [docs/](docs/). ## Contributing Bugs and questions go to [issues](https://github.com/midplaneai/midplane/issues); building and testing is in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Found a way around a mask, a policy or the audit log? Report it privately: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## License MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

readme.markdown:
# News and Media Mention Monitor MCP Server

An MCP server for the Mamba Labs News and Media Mention Monitor actor on Apify. Give it company names, brands, people, or topics. It reads Google News for each one and returns one row per article: headline, outlet, date, the publisher's own URL and domain, and a headline sentiment label. With only_new on, a repeat call with the same state_key returns only articles it has not returned before.

## What's Inside

- [What it does](#what-it-does)
- [Quick start](#quick-start)
- [Prerequisites](#prerequisites)
- [Example prompts](#example-prompts)
- [Tool](#tool)
- [Inputs](#inputs)
- [Pricing](#pricing)
- [Your keys](#your-keys)
- [Full actor documentation](#full-actor-documentation)
- [License](#license)

## What it does

Each news.google.com link is resolved to the article's URL on the publisher's site. An article found by two of your search terms comes back once. When a run returns no article, one free summary row says why: nothing matched, everything was returned before, or Google News did not answer. All of the work runs on Apify. This package is a thin client that starts the actor run, waits for it, and hands back the dataset rows.

## Quick start

You need Node.js 18 or newer and an Apify account with an API token.

Add this to your Claude Desktop config (`claude_desktop_config.json`), Cursor, or any MCP client:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "mamba-news-media-mention-monitor": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "@mambalabsdev/mcp-news-media-mention-monitor"
      ],
      "env": {
        "APIFY_TOKEN": "your-apify-token"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart the client. The `monitor_news_mentions` tool appears.

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 18 or newer.
- An Apify API token from [console.apify.com/account/integrations](https://console.apify.com/account/integrations), set as `APIFY_TOKEN`. The server lists its tool without a token; a call needs one.

## Example prompts

- "What did the news say about Gong and Salesloft this week?"
- "Find news articles about our company from the last 30 days and list the outlets."
- "Any negative headlines about Acme Robotics since my last check?"

## Tool

`monitor_news_mentions`. One tool. Example arguments:

```json
{
  "queries": ["\"Acme Robotics\""],
  "since_days": "7",
  "state_key": "acme-weekly"
}
```

## Inputs

Every buyer facing input of the actor, unchanged. Omitted inputs take the actor's own defaults. Numbers and yes or no values are sent as strings.

| Input | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `queries` | array | 1 to 50 search terms. Required |
| `exclude_terms` | array | Up to 20 words to leave out |
| `since_days` | string | Days back, 1 to 90. Default 7 |
| `country` | string | Google News country edition. Default US |
| `language` | string | Language code. Default en |
| `resolve_publisher_url` | string | true (default) or false |
| `only_new` | string | true (default) or false |
| `state_key` | string | Name for this watch list |
| `max_articles` | string | Per search term, 1 to 100. Default 50 |
| `max_charge_usd` | string | Optional cap on the run's cost |

## Pricing

Pay per event on Apify, billed to your Apify account. Prices in USD.

| Event | Free plan | Bronze | Silver | Gold |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `article-row`, per article returned | $0.0023 | $0.002185 | $0.00207 | $0.001955 |
| `apify-actor-start`, per run start | $0.0015 | $0.0015 | $0.0015 | $0.0015 |

An article skipped by only_new is not charged. A summary row is free.

## Your keys

The actor needs no key and holds none. Proxy traffic adds nothing to your price: Mamba Labs pays the platform costs of the run.

## Full actor documentation

[apify.com/mambalabs/news-media-mention-monitor](https://apify.com/mambalabs/news-media-mention-monitor)

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

name: DeepDNA local
description: Reads a raw DNA file on your computer and reports the variants DeepDNA curates, with sources.

readme.markdown:
# DeepDNA MCP server

A remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that gives AI agents cited pharmacogenomic and gene-variant lookups, so answers can quote CPIC and DPWG guidance and its sources. This repository also holds a [local package](#read-a-raw-dna-file-on-your-own-computer) that reads a raw DNA file on the user's own computer; nothing from the file is sent to DeepDNA, but what the package reports becomes part of the conversation with the AI model.

```text
https://deepdna.ai/mcp
```

Streamable HTTP, stateless, no API key, no account. Listed in the official MCP registry as `ai.deepdna/knowledge`.

> Educational information only, not medical advice. The server reports what curated sources and guidelines say about a gene, a variant or a drug–gene pair. It does not diagnose, prescribe or recommend a dose.

## Tools

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `list_genes` | The genes in the knowledge base, with a one-line summary and category for each |
| `lookup_gene` | Everything curated about one gene: function, key variants with rsIDs, phenotypes, drug interactions, what a consumer genotyping array can and cannot tell you, and sources |
| `lookup_variant` | One variant by dbSNP rsID: gene, star-allele or common name, alleles on the plus strand of GRCh37, effect, frequency note and sources. Takes the rsID only, never a genotype |
| `lookup_drug_gene` | Guidance for a gene, optionally for one drug: guideline (CPIC or DPWG where one exists), summary, phenotype groups and sources |
| `check_medications` | Splits a list of generic drug names into drugs with a curated record (gene, and a `basis` field: CPIC or DPWG guideline, drug label, or primary literature) and drugs not covered. Needs no genotype |

All five tools are read-only.

Two prompts, `medication_review` and `explain_variant`, package the common questions for clients that show MCP prompts.

Coverage today is 12 genes: CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, SLCO1B1, VKORC1, UGT1A1, G6PD, MTHFR, COMT, HFE, APOE and BRCA1, with 51 curated drug–gene pairs across 11 of them: 40 cite a CPIC or DPWG guideline, the rest a drug label or the primary literature; the `basis` field in `check_medications` says which (`guideline` is null, or "drug label", when no guideline exists). It is a small, reviewed set, not a mirror of PharmGKB/ClinPGx. Every record lists its sources. The `level` field (the guideline's evidence grade) is `null` for every pair today.

## Connect

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http deepdna https://deepdna.ai/mcp
```

**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) and other clients that use an `mcpServers` file:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deepdna": { "type": "http", "url": "https://deepdna.ai/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "deepdna": { "type": "http", "url": "https://deepdna.ai/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Claude Desktop and claude.ai:** add `https://deepdna.ai/mcp` as a custom connector.

**Gemini CLI** (installs the remote, read-only server `https://deepdna.ai/mcp` as an extension, not the local package; `gemini-extension.json` is in this repo):

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/alfonsoguv/deepdna-mcp
```

## Try it without a client

```bash
curl -s https://deepdna.ai/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"lookup_drug_gene","arguments":{"gene":"CYP2C19","drug":"clopidogrel"}}}'
```

The answer carries the CPIC recommendation for clopidogrel by CYP2C19 metabolizer group, the sources it was written from, and the disclaimer. The same data is available as plain REST, documented in the [API docs](https://deepdna.ai/docs/) and the [OpenAPI spec](https://deepdna.ai/openapi.json):

```text
GET https://deepdna.ai/api/v1/pgx/CYP2C19/clopidogrel
GET https://deepdna.ai/api/v1/variants/rs4244285
```

## Read a raw DNA file on your own computer

The remote server takes no genotype: its tools have no field for one. For a raw DNA file there is a local package in this repository. It reads the file on the user's computer and reports what it shows at each position DeepDNA curates, with the cited records. Nothing from the file is sent to deepdna.ai: the package downloads the same public records for every user, and `lookup_drug_gene` sends only the gene and drug names. What `read_dna_file` returns (the letters and counts at the curated positions) becomes part of the conversation with the AI model your client uses, under that provider's terms.

**Claude Code** (needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); the package is on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/deepdna-mcp/)):

```bash
claude mcp add deepdna-local -- uvx deepdna-mcp@0.1.2
```

The [`plugin/`](plugin/) folder packages the same command as a Claude plugin, for Claude Code and for Cowork sessions on the user's computer.

Clients that use an `mcpServers` file (if the client cannot find `uvx`, put its full path, from `which uvx`, in `command`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deepdna-local": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["deepdna-mcp@0.1.2"] }
  }
}
```

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `read_dna_file` | What a 23andMe, AncestryDNA or MyHeritage/FamilyTreeDNA export (.txt, .csv or .zip) shows at each curated position |
| `lookup_drug_gene` | Guidance for a gene, optionally for one drug, from the public API. Sends only the gene and drug names |

- Each position gets one of four states: `read`, `no_call`, `not_in_file`, or `unexpected_letters` (letters that fit neither the record nor its complement). A missing or unreadable position is unknown, never normal.
- For positions the record marks as `countable` (no phasing or other variants are needed to read them), it gives how many copies of the variant allele the file shows, with the record's text and sources.
- `genes` limits the answer to what the user asked about. APOE, BRCA1 and HFE are disease-risk genes: they are

readme.markdown:
# Sniptide

A self-hostable pastebin for code snippets, configs, and secrets.
Share multi-file pastes with passwords, expiry, or burn-after-read links.
Organize reusable snippets in collections, sync `.env` files, and connect coding agents through the CLI or MCP server.

## Self-host

Run Sniptide and Postgres with Docker Compose:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Dino-Kupinic/sniptide.git
cd sniptide
printf 'BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=%s\nBETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3000\n' "$(openssl rand -hex 32)" > .env
docker compose up -d
```

Open [localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000) and create an account.
Use your public HTTPS URL for `BETTER_AUTH_URL` when deploying to a server.
See the [self-hosting guide](https://docs.sniptide.com/self-hosting) for HTTPS, configuration, backups, and upgrades.

The official Docker image supports AMD64 and ARM64 at `ghcr.io/dino-kupinic/sniptide`.

## Connect a coding agent

Add the MCP server to Claude Code, which signs you in to Sniptide in the browser through OAuth:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http sniptide https://app.sniptide.com/api/mcp
```

For a client without OAuth, create a token in Settings, API tokens, and pass it with `--header "Authorization: Bearer $SNIPTIDE_TOKEN"`.

Use `<your-instance-url>/api/mcp` on a self-hosted instance.
The [MCP guide](https://docs.sniptide.com/mcp) covers Cursor and a local server, and the [CLI](https://docs.sniptide.com/cli) installs a collection as an agent skill.
This repository is also an [Agent Plugin](https://agent-plugins.org): `plugin.json` bundles the MCP servers in `mcp.json` with the skills in `skills/`.

## Documentation

- [User guide](https://docs.sniptide.com)
- [CLI](https://docs.sniptide.com/cli) and [MCP server](https://docs.sniptide.com/mcp)
- [Self-hosting](https://docs.sniptide.com/self-hosting)
- [Development](docs/development.md) and [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [Operations and scaling](docs/scaling.md)

The API reference is available at `/docs/api` on your instance.

# Uniswap Universal Router Decoder & Encoder

> Many thanks to **everyone** who has ☕️ [offered some **coffees**!](https://github.com/Elnaril/uniswap-universal-router-decoder/discussions/11) ☕️
> or ⭐ [**starred** this project!](https://github.com/Elnaril/uniswap-universal-router-decoder/stargazers) ⭐  
> It is **greatly** appreciated! :)

---

  

---

#### Project Information

#### Code Quality

---

## Release Notes
See the [release notes page](https://github.com/Elnaril/uniswap-universal-router-decoder/wiki/Release_Notes)

### v4.0.0 - breaking changes
- Update COMMAND_TYPE_MASK to 0x7f to match UR
- Add support for the PAY_PORTION_FULL_PRECISION command (0x07)
- Add support for the BALANCE_CHECK_ERC20 command (0x0e)
- Add support for the V3_POSITION_MANAGER_PERMIT command (0x11)
- Add support for the V3_POSITION_MANAGER_CALL command (0x12)
- Add support for the EXECUTE_SUB_PLAN command (0x21)
- Add `revert_on_fail` to the encoder methods for the commands whose failure the UR can tolerate
- Capture the bytes some callers append after the UR arguments as `trailing_data`, and re-append them when rebuilding
  the calldata, so a decoded call can be rebuilt byte-for-byte
- Make the chained function builders public and expose the `encoder` & `decoder` modules
- Reduce CI time
- Add a `publish.yml` GitHub Actions workflow that automatically publishes the package to PyPI and the MCP Registry with OIDC
  Trusted Publishing
- Agent-friendly changes:
  - Add `Encoder.function_input()` / `AsyncEncoder.function_input()` to rebuild the calldata from a decoded call
  - Add `decoded_input_to_dict()` and `transaction_to_dict()` to render the decoder output as JSON-friendly dicts
  - Add the `ur-decode` and `ur-encode` command line tools, including `ur-encode v3-path` and its `encode_v3_path` MCP
    counterpart
  - Add the `ur-mcp` MCP server (optional `mcp` extra) so AI agents can drive the codec, including `encode_calldata`
    to rebuild the calldata from a decoded call
  - Annotate the MCP tools as read-only so a host can auto-approve them, and give them human-readable titles
  - The command descriptions (`ur-encode list` / `describe` and the `list_commands` / `describe_command` MCP tools) now
    describe the decoded call format and its ABI parameters, instead of the encoder methods
  - Add the MCP Registry metadata (`server.json`) to make the `ur-mcp` server discoverable
  - Add `AGENTS.md` and `llms.txt` for AI agents, plus a `mcp` PyPI keyword
  - Add `tests/test_version_consistency.py` to keep the packaging version, `server.json` and the README `mcp-name:`
    marker in sync

---

## Overview and Points of Attention

The object of this library is to decode & encode transactions sent to the Uniswap Universal Router (UR)
on Ethereum Mainnet, though it would work on any compatible chain where the UR is deployed. See Version Mapping below.
This Python SDK is based on, and intended to be used with [web3.py](https://github.com/ethereum/web3.py)

The target audience is Python developers who are familiar with the Ethereum blockchain concepts and web3.py, and how DEXes work.
The same codec is also available without Python, through the `ur-decode` / `ur-encode` command line tools and the optional
`ur-mcp` MCP server (see "Command line interface" and "MCP server" below): both print JSON, so shell scripts and AI
agents can drive it too.

⚠ Before using this library, ensure you are familiar with general blockchain concepts. The Python API also expects
[web3.py](https://github.com/ethereum/web3.py) knowledge in particular.

⚠ Not all UR functions supported by this SDK are available through the CLI or MCP tools: 
run `ur-encode list` and look for the "rebuildable" flag.

readme.markdown:
# @quiqsol/mcp

Connect [QuiQSol](https://quiqsol.com) to Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor and any AI agent.

This package gives you two things:

- **`quiqsol mcp`**: a local [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server over stdio, for apps that launch a command (Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code).
- **`quiqsol`**: a command line for your terminal, scripts and agents, with JSON output.

Both run on the QuiQSol remote MCP server at `https://api.quiqsol.com/mcp`. Tools, permissions and safety rules live on the server, so this package stays small, has zero dependencies and never needs an update to gain new tools.

MIT licensed.

## What your agent can do

| Product | Read | Act |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CRM | Search; list and get leads, contacts, companies, deals, notes, tasks; view the pipeline | Create and update leads, contacts, companies and deals; move deal stages; add notes; create and complete tasks |
| Help Desk | List and read tickets with their full conversation | Reply (preview first), add internal notes, change status |
| Inbox | List conversations across WhatsApp, website chat and social; read messages | Reply inside the WhatsApp 24-hour window (preview first) |
| Invoices | List and read invoices and totals | Create draft invoices; send (preview first) |
| Projects | List projects and tasks | Create and update tasks |
| Forms | List forms and submissions | |
| Analytics | Business overview, sales, Help Desk and invoice summaries | |

## Security model

- **Scoped access.** Every key and connection carries explicit scopes (`crm:read`, `crm:write`, `helpdesk:read`, `helpdesk:write`, `inbox:read`, `inbox:send`, `invoices:read`, `invoices:write`, `invoices:send`, `projects:read`, `projects:write`, `forms:read`, `analytics:read`). An agent only sees the tools its scopes allow.
- **Your own permissions.** An agent acts as the person who created the key or approved the connection, inside that person's role. It can never do more than they can in the app.
- **Nothing reaches a customer without approval.** Ticket replies, inbox replies and invoice sends return a preview first. They only go out when called again with `confirm: true`, which agents are instructed to do only after you approve.
- **Untrusted content is labelled.** Every result is wrapped as workspace data, with customer-written text marked as data, never instructions.
- **No secrets in output.** Tokens, hashes and keys are stripped from every result server-side.
- **Revocable and audited.** Revoke any key or connection in Settings > Developer Platform. Every call is listed in the API activity log there.

## Get a key

In QuiQSol, open **Settings > Developer Platform > AI agents**, choose **Create AI agent key**, pick the scopes and copy the key (shown once).

Claude and ChatGPT do not need a key: add `https://api.quiqsol.com/mcp` as a connector and sign in with OAuth. See the [setup guide](https://quiqsol.com/developers/ai-agents).

## Use with Claude Desktop, Cursor or any stdio MCP client

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "quiqsol": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@quiqsol/mcp", "mcp"],
      "env": { "QUIQSOL_API_KEY": "aur_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Desktop: Settings > Developer > Edit Config. Cursor: `~/.cursor/mcp.json` or Settings > MCP.

Clients that support remote servers can skip the package and point straight at the server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "quiqsol": {
      "url": "https://api.quiqsol.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer aur_live_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http quiqsol https://api.quiqsol.com/mcp
```

## Use the CLI

```bash
npm install -g @quiqsol/mcp
quiqsol login
quiqsol whoami
```

```bash
quiqsol leads list --status NEW --limit 10
quiqsol leads create --first-name Ada --last-name Obi --email ada@example.com --source WEBSITE
quiqsol deals pipeline
quiqsol deals move 66f0c2aa66f0c2aa66f0c2aa "Proposal sent"
quiqsol tickets list --status OPEN --mine
quiqsol tickets reply 66f0c2aa66f0c2aa66f0c2aa --body "Your refund was processed today."
quiqsol inbox list --channel whatsapp --unread
quiqsol invoices create --contact-id 66f0c2aa66f0c2aa66f0c2aa --item "Website design:1:450000" --due-date 2026-11-30
quiqsol invoices send 66f0c2aa66f0c2aa66f0c2aa
quiqsol analytics overview --days 30
```

Any tool, by name:

```bash
quiqsol tools
quiqsol call crm_list_deals '{"stage":"Negotiation","limit":5}'
```

Output is JSON on stdout (pretty in a terminal, compact when piped). Commands that reach a customer show a preview and ask before sending; in scripts they print the preview and exit with code `3` unless you pass `--yes`.

| Exit code | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 0 | Done |
| 1 | Error (message on stderr) |
| 2 | Usage error |
| 3 | Preview only, nothing was sent |

Configuration: `QUIQSOL_API_KEY` and `QUIQSOL_API_URL` override the saved login in `~/.config/quiqsol/config.json` (written with owner-only permissions).

## Use from code

```js
const { QuiqsolClient } = require('@quiqsol/mcp');

const quiqsol = new QuiqsolClient({ apiKey: process.env.QUIQSOL_API_KEY });
const { data } = await quiqsol.callTool('crm_list_leads', { status: 'NEW', limit: 5 });
```

Prefer plain HTTP? The same tools are available as REST at `https://api.quiqsol.com/public/v1/agent` (`GET /tools`, `POST /tools/{name}`).

## Requirements

Node.js 18 or later.

## License

MIT. The QuiQSol platform itself is a commercial service; this connector is open source so you can read exactly what runs on your machine.

readme.markdown: # Munin > Your whole customer operation, behind one MCP endpoint. Website · See it in action · Documentation · MCP Registry CRM, conversations, outreach, CMS, knowledge base, and analytics on one Postgres schema — exposed as MCP tools your agents drive, not screens you click through. Headless the way a headless CMS is: the dashboard owns settings, auth, and the human half of the work — an inbox where a person takes over a conversation, and a review queue where they approve what the agent proposed — but there is no admin UI to click your way through the data itself. Every action runs through MCP tools, callable from any MCP-compatible client (Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, custom runners) — same tools, same permissions, same audit log, whether a human or an agent is driving. Munin even ships its own: an in-process, per-org agent runner that answers live conversations and works the curation queue against an LLM provider you configure — so the platform runs out of the box, with external MCP clients optional. The console — settings, auth, the inbox, and the review queue. It drives the same MCP tools your agents call. The review queue — outbound never sends itself. An agent drafts, files the evidence behind the draft, and waits; approving is the human's keystroke. The embeddable chat widget — answering a live customer from the knowledge base, ready to hand off to a human and be picked back up by the agent. ## Modules at a glance | Module | Tools | What it does | |---|---|---| | Knowledge Base | `kb_*` | documents, hybrid search, audience scoping | | Conversations | `conv_*` | channels, messages, handover | | CRM | `crm_*` | contacts, companies, deals | | CMS | `cms_*` | collections, entries, assets | | Outreach | `outreach_*` | campaigns, drafts, propose-only | | Analytics | `analytics_*` | page-view + search events | These six modules aren't separate products — they share one Postgres schema, one permission model, and one audit log. Together with integrations and platform plumbing they add up to 223 MCP tools and 58 skills. Watch how they tie together: ## Core modules #### Knowledge Base - Markdown articles organized into spaces, each scoped to the audiences allowed to see it. - Hybrid search that blends keyword matching with meaning-based results. - Website import — crawl a public site and turn each page into an article in the background, automatically dropping articles when their source page disappears. - Full version history with restore, plus a review queue for proposed edits. - Agents revise a long article in place with targeted text replacements, instead of rewriting the whole body to change a sentence. #### Conversations - One inbox across email, chat widget, voice (Threll.ai / Vapi), and SMS (Twilio / MessageBird). - Inbound *and* outbound — agents answer conversations and can place outbound calls. - Images in and out on every channel: customers send screenshots, operators and the agent reply with them, and the agent can see what it was sent. - Email that behaves like email — start by forwarding to a generated address, quoted history reconstructed from Gmail, Outlook and Apple Mail replies, auto-replies and bounces filed away instead of queued, junk senders remembered, undelivered messages surfaced and retried. - Per-topic reply automation: the agent starts out drafting for approval on a topic, and is promoted to sending on its own once you trust it there. - Assignable, organized by topic, searchable across every message, and filterable by status, origin, channel, topic and age. - Built-in handoff to a human, with notifications to your own systems as conversations change. #### CRM - Contacts, companies, deals, activities, pipelines, and segments. - AI-written summaries and suggested next actions, kept separate from what people edit by hand. - Consent tracking — the lawful basis and source for each contact, required before they can be added to any outreach — with address deliverability tracked separately, so a bounced address never reads as a withdrawn consent. - Automatic duplicate detection that proposes merges for review, plus bulk contact import. #### CMS - Content collections with structured fields, and entries you can publish in multiple languages, each locale with its own slug. - Rich content blocks for article bodies — callouts, quotes, media, and more — addressable by key, so an agent can add, replace, remove or reorder a single block. - Scheduled publishing and a media library that keeps your master image and serves sized derivatives. - Full version history with restore, search, and cross-references between entries. - A public content API serves your site or app, with draft preview links for custom frontends and engagement tracking built into every entry. #### Outreach - Propose-only outbound across email, SMS, and voice calls — campaigns, segments, and drafts for both first touches and replies. - Multi-step sequences with cadence rules that stop the moment someone replies. - Every proposal reports the exact address or number an approval would reach, and an approved send can be scheduled rather than fired immediately. - Outcomes extracted from replies and from finished calls, written back onto the record. - Recipients are drawn only from contacts who have recorded consent (see CRM). - Every message waits for human approval; nothing is ever sent automatically. #### Analytics - Captures page views and on-site searches across anything you want to measure, one row per view with read depth, reported per tracker. - CMS pages are tracked automatically; for any other page, you add a small tracking snippet. - Conversion funnels and per-visitor journeys — once someone is identified, their visits link to a CRM contact, including the anonymous ones from before. A signed email on identify means the website and the inbox resolve to one person. - Breakdow …

readme.markdown:
ausecon is a Model Context Protocol server that gives an AI assistant structured access to Australia’s official economic and financial data, straight from the ABS, RBA, and APRA. Open source, free, and no API key. Every series comes back fresh & fully source-traceable, and all three sources share one response shape. Documentation  ·  Getting started  ·  Tool reference  ·  Changelog --- ## Why this exists Australian economic data is authoritative but awkward to reach. It sits behind three different portals with three different formats, and each one expects you to already know its identifiers. ausecon puts that data in front of an AI assistant with nothing to sign up for and no key to manage. Every series is fetched from the source, cached for up to an hour, stamped with when it was actually retrieved, and returned in the same `metadata · series · observations` shape whether it came from the ABS, the RBA, or APRA. Ask for "the cash rate" or "quarterly real GDP growth" and the assistant works out the right call. 14read-only tools 83economic concepts 16derived indicators 8prompt templates 3data sources ## What you get Fresh & source-traceable Every value is fetched from the source, cached for up to an hour, and stamped with its provenance (retrieved_at, source, server_version). If a source is down after the cache expires, the old copy is returned flagged stale and never served silently. Three sources, one shape ABS, RBA and APRA all return the same metadata · series · observations structure, so anything written against one source works for the other two. Transparent derived series Formula-based indicators like real_cash_rate, with the formula and its input series returned alongside the numbers. Source-native control Drop down to get_abs_data, get_rba_table or get_apra_data when you need a specific dataflow, table, or series ID. Convenience tools Latest observations, top movers, and the release calendar, each in a single call. Works with your client Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Codex or Smithery. stdio locally, Streamable HTTP when hosted. ## Data sources | Source | Coverage | | :----- | :------- | | **ABS**  ·  Australian Bureau of Statistics | National accounts, prices, labour force, population | | **RBA**  ·  Reserve Bank of Australia | Cash rate, monetary & financial aggregates, exchange rates | | **APRA**  ·  Aust. Prudential Regulation Authority | ADI & insurer statistics, with release-cadence estimates | ## Try it instantly (no install) A hosted read-only, no-API-key instance speaks MCP over Streamable HTTP at: ```text https://mcp.auseconmcp.com/mcp ``` Point any MCP client that supports remote servers at that URL. In Claude Code: ```bash claude mcp add --transport http ausecon https://mcp.auseconmcp.com/mcp ``` > The hosted instance may take a few seconds to wake on the first request. Run on its own it just sits there waiting for a client, so there is nothing to see until one connects. ## Connect your client
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport stdio ausecon -- uvx ausecon-mcp-server ```
Codex ```bash codex mcp add ausecon -- uvx ausecon-mcp-server ```
Claude Desktop Add to your `claude_desktop_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "ausecon": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["ausecon-mcp-server"] } } } ```
Cursor Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (project): ```json { "mcpServers": { "ausecon": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["ausecon-mcp-server"] } } } ``` Or paste this one-click link into your browser: ```text cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=ausecon&config=eyJjb21tYW5kIjoidXZ4IiwiYXJncyI6WyJhdXNlY29uLW1jcC1zZXJ2ZXIiXX0= ```
Windsurf Add to `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`: ```json { "mcpServers": { "ausecon": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["ausecon-mcp-server"], "env": {} } } } ```
VS Code Or add to `.vscode/mcp.json` (workspace) or your user `mcp.json`: ```json { "servers": { "ausecon": { "type": "stdio", "command": "uvx", "args": ["ausecon-mcp-server"] } } } ```

readme.markdown:
# Moderation API MCP Server

Let AI agents run your [Moderation API](https://moderationapi.com) account: work through review queues, investigate authors, tune policies and wordlists, respond to incidents and report on how moderation is going.

This is a hosted (remote) [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server. Connect Claude, Cursor or any other MCP client to:

```
https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp
```

There is nothing to install. The server has one tool for each endpoint of the [REST API](https://docs.moderationapi.com/api-reference/introduction), and it calls the same API as your code, so rate limits, quotas and request logs work the same way.

## What your agent can do

- **Triage the review queue.** "Go through today's unresolved items, reject the obvious spam, and show me the 5 you're unsure about." The agent does the first pass; you make the judgment calls.
- **Investigate an author.** "Is user 8812 a bad actor? Check their history and suspend them if it's a pattern."
- **Tune policies from real examples.** "These 10 comments got flagged but are fine, and these 3 got through. Fix it." The agent tests the examples without storing them, finds the thresholds or wordlist entries that separate them, and updates the channel.
- **Respond to incidents.** "There's a raid of crypto scam posts in the last hour. Find them, block the authors, and add the domains to the blocklist."
- **Set up moderation without the dashboard.** "Set up moderation for our new marketplace: a channel for listings, one for messages, and a webhook to our endpoint." Then send test content to check it.
- **Report and audit.** "How did moderation go this month?" Queue stats, actions and author trends turned into a summary.
- **Combine with your other tools.** A daily queue digest in Slack, an issue when a policy keeps misfiring, a draft reply to the user whose post was removed.

The server also ships prompts (recipes) for these jobs: `triage-queue`, `check-author`, `tune-policy`, `incident-response` and `moderation-report`. More example prompts: [What your agent can do](https://docs.moderationapi.com/ai/examples).

## Tools

| Area | What the tools do |
| - | - |
| Content | Submit content and read the result, with or without storing it; allow or reject content |
| Review queues | List queues and items, resolve and unresolve items one by one or up to 100 at a time, queue statistics |
| Authors | List, look up, create and update authors; block, suspend and unblock them |
| Actions | List and run moderation actions on content and authors; create and change actions |
| Policies | Read and change channels and their policies; create and change wordlists and their words |
| Analytics | Summary, most flagged policies and authors, numbers per channel, volumes over time, automation |
| Projects | List, create, change and duplicate projects; create API keys |
| Webhooks | List, create and change webhooks |
| Feedback | Send a feature request to the Moderation API team |

Read-only tools are marked as read-only, so your agent can run them without asking. Tools that change or delete data are marked as such, and most agents ask you before they run them.

## Setup

You need a Moderation API account with the **Owner**, **Admin** or **Developer** role. [Sign up free](https://moderationapi.com).

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http moderation-api https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp
```

Or install the [plugin](https://docs.moderationapi.com/ai/overview), which adds the MCP server and the setup skill together.

### Claude and Claude Desktop

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, and enter `https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp`.

### Cursor

Add the server to `.cursor/mcp.json` in your project, or to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for all projects:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "moderation-api": {
      "url": "https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Other clients

Add a remote MCP server with the URL `https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp` and the Streamable HTTP transport.

## Sign in

The first time your agent uses the server, your browser opens:

1. Sign in with your Moderation API account.
2. Pick the organization the agent can use.
3. Approve the connection.

The agent can reach the projects that you can reach. Each connection gets its own API key, shown on the **API keys** page and named after the app and your email. Delete the key to end the connection. When the agent resolves queue items or runs actions, the review queue shows you as the reviewer.

### Without a browser

Agents that cannot open a browser, for example in CI, can send an API key instead:

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http moderation-api https://mcp.moderationapi.com/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer $MODAPI_SECRET_KEY"
```

A project key reaches one project. An organization key reaches the projects you allow it to.

## Projects

Tools that work on content in a project take an optional `projectId`. You can give the project ID or its name. When it's left out and the key reaches more than one project, the tool returns the projects to choose from.

## Other tools for agents

- **Setup skill**: lets a coding agent add Moderation API to your app's code. `npx skills add moderation-api/skills`
- **CLI**: sign in, create a project and write API keys from the terminal. `modapi init`

See [Build with AI agents](https://docs.moderationapi.com/ai/overview).

## Links

- [Documentation](https://docs.moderationapi.com/ai/mcp)
- [Moderation API](https://moderationapi.com)
- [MCP Registry listing](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=com.moderationapi): `com.moderationapi/moderation-api`

# @ghostpaw/affinity

**Agent contacts: people, promises and yearly dates, with a radar for who is drifting.**

A local social CRM: contacts, identities, relationships, journal events,
commitments and recurring dates in one SQLite file. One self-contained binary
per platform, an MCP server, and a zero-dependency TypeScript library.

## Install

Each line downloads the latest release for one platform, checks it against
`SHA256SUMS`, puts `ghostpaw-affinity` on your `PATH` and prints the version.

**Linux x64**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=linux-x64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ghostpaw-affinity ~/.local/bin/ && { case ":$PATH:" in *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;; *) echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile; export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH";; esac; } && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**Linux arm64**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=linux-arm64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && mkdir -p ~/.local/bin && mv ghostpaw-affinity ~/.local/bin/ && { case ":$PATH:" in *":$HOME/.local/bin:"*) ;; *) echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile; export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH";; esac; } && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**macOS Apple silicon**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=darwin-arm64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo mv ghostpaw-affinity /usr/local/bin/ && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**macOS Intel**

```sh
cd "$(mktemp -d)" && T=darwin-x64 && V=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/latest | sed 's|.*/v||') && F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz && U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V && curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" && grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - && tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/bin && sudo mv ghostpaw-affinity /usr/local/bin/ && ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

**Windows x64 (PowerShell)**

```powershell
$r='GhostPawJS/affinity'; $v=(irm "https://api.github.com/repos/$r/releases/latest").tag_name; $f="ghostpaw-affinity-$($v.TrimStart('v'))-windows-x64.zip"; $u="https://github.com/$r/releases/download/$v"; $t=(New-Item -ItemType Directory (Join-Path $env:TEMP ([guid]::NewGuid()))).FullName; iwr "$u/$f" -OutFile "$t\$f" -UseBasicParsing; iwr "$u/SHA256SUMS" -OutFile "$t\SHA256SUMS" -UseBasicParsing; $want=((Get-Content "$t\SHA256SUMS" | Where-Object { $_ -like "* $f" }) -split '\s+')[0]; if (-not $want -or (Get-FileHash "$t\$f" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash -ne $want) { throw "checksum mismatch for $f" }; $d=Join-Path $env:LOCALAPPDATA 'Programs\ghostpaw\bin'; Expand-Archive "$t\$f" $t -Force; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $d | Out-Null; Copy-Item "$t\ghostpaw-affinity.exe" $d -Force; $p=[Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable('Path','User'); if (";$p;" -notlike "*;$d;*") { [Environment]::SetEnvironmentVariable('Path',"$p;$d",'User') }; $env:Path="$d;$env:Path"; ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

These commands install the latest release in `~/.local/bin` on Linux, `/usr/local/bin` on macOS (asks for sudo), or `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\ghostpaw\bin` on Windows; Linux adds it to PATH via `~/.profile` only if missing, and Windows adds it to the user PATH (open a new terminal afterwards). To pin a version, set `V=0.6.0` instead of resolving latest (`$v='v0.6.0'` in PowerShell).

For a pinned Linux/macOS download to the current directory with no profile or PATH edits, choose the matching `T` (`linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `darwin-arm64`, or `darwin-x64`):

```sh
V=0.6.0
T=linux-x64
F=ghostpaw-affinity-$V-$T.tar.gz
U=https://github.com/GhostPawJS/affinity/releases/download/v$V
curl -fsSL -O "$U/$F" -O "$U/SHA256SUMS" &&
  { case "$T" in darwin-*) grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | shasum -a 256 -c - ;; *) grep " $F\$" SHA256SUMS | sha256sum -c - ;; esac; } &&
  tar -xzf "$F" ghostpaw-affinity && ./ghostpaw-affinity --version
```

Then:

```sh

```

Contacts live in `~/.ghostpaw/affinity.db` unless `--db <path>` or the
`GHOSTPAW_AFFINITY_DB` environment variable says otherwise; relative paths
resolve against the current directory.

readme.markdown:
Decision system for software built with AI Keep your project's direction in human hands as agents do more of the work. Nauro records the project decisions you approve, including their reasons and rejected alternatives. It brings those reasons into later agent sessions. **Status:** Stable (1.x). ## See it in practice https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f75ede99-db11-4460-bc09-801c86df1e19 *A Codex session, then a Claude session in Pareto, Nauro's development mock project.* ## Is Nauro a fit? Nauro supports longer-lived work across sessions, tools, and handoffs. If a small repo plus a reliable AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md keeps agents oriented, Nauro may be more than you need. Retrieval is advisory. New or revised decisions require your explicit approval. Local use needs no account; the record is plain Markdown on your machine. Cloud sync is optional. Nauro sends no product analytics. ## Get started ### Desktop app (macOS) The free app installs the CLI, connects agents, and sets up a project. Its read-only viewer shows the project record. [Download for macOS (Apple silicon)](https://github.com/Nauro-AI/nauro-app-releases/releases/latest/download/Nauro-macOS-arm64.dmg), signed and notarized. [Setup guide](https://nauro.ai/docs/desktop-app).
Watch the desktop app tour https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e23d3d7f-2d5b-4ce4-be18-fcaff74e7973
### CLI ```bash uv tool install nauro ``` [Install uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/), or use `pipx install nauro` with Python 3.10 or newer. ## Try the demo (optional) Pennykeep is the bundled fictional budgeting app. - **Request:** Replace envelope budgeting with spending charts to simplify onboarding. - **Prior decision:** In the fictional tester history, passive tracking did not help users control spending. The team accepted extra setup so users assign income before spending. - **Possible plan:** Simplify envelope setup, or ask whether to revisit the budgeting model. No account or agent setup required. On macOS or Linux: ```bash mkdir -p /tmp/nauro-demo && cd /tmp/nauro-demo nauro init --demo nauro check-decision "Replace envelope budgeting with a passive spending tracker and charts" ``` Look for **Envelope budgeting method** in the related decisions. This retrieves prior reasoning; it does not run an agent or change decisions. [PowerShell and demo guide](https://nauro.ai/docs/quickstart#demo). ## Use it on your repo For CLI setup: ```bash cd your-repo nauro adopt --with-skills --with-subagents ``` Skip this command if the desktop wizard already adopted your repository. Restart your agent, then run `/nauro-adopt` in Claude Code, `$nauro-adopt` in Codex, or `@nauro-adopt` in Cursor. Review the proposed project record. Approve one existing decision you want future sessions to remember. Start a fresh session and ask about a task where it matters. Check how the agent uses the reason. Adopt wires Cursor only when `~/.cursor` or a repository `.cursor/` exists; otherwise run `nauro setup cursor`. Cursor requires a working durable absolute Nauro executable for global MCP wiring. Claude/Codex retain their existing fallback behavior. Follow [Cursor migration](packages/nauro/README.md#cursor-migration) before changing legacy wiring. Run `nauro status` to inspect configuration and executable availability. See [agent workflows](https://nauro.ai/docs/agents-and-skills) and [setup details](https://nauro.ai/docs/quickstart). The bundled `nauro-investigator` studies Claude and Codex logs for supported findings about Nauro use and development work. See the [investigator guide](docs/investigator.md) for a bounded first run and a research notebook that later runs can resume. An existing `AGENTS.md` is preserved unless you run `nauro sync`. Its `# Manual` section survives replacement. ## Documentation [Documentation](https://nauro.ai/docs) covers commands, storage, and cloud access. Semantic versioning covers the CLI, local stdio MCP contract, store format, and curated `nauro-core` API. Cloud sync and hosted MCP are versioned separately. Website: [nauro.ai](https://nauro.ai). ## Development ```bash uv sync --all-packages --all-extras uv run pytest packages/nauro-core/tests/ -x -q uv run pytest packages/nauro/tests/ -x -q ``` Report bugs and request features in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/Nauro-AI/nauro/issues). Apache 2.0. Named for Peter Naur's *Programming as Theory Building* (1985).

# @ghostpaw/codex

**Agent memory as beliefs with a source, a certainty and a revision history.**

```bash
ghostpaw-codex --help
```

Local, evidence-backed memory for agents. One SQLite file, zero runtime
dependencies.

Codex stores what an agent believes as claims with a source, a certainty,
evidence counts, decay and an honest revision history. Agents search before
they remember, confirm or correct instead of appending, and see which beliefs
are stale, fading or weakly evidenced. It runs as a TypeScript library, an MCP
server, a CLI and an Agent Skill, all generated from the same seven tools.

Website: [codex.ghostpaw.dev](https://codex.ghostpaw.dev/)

The release binary includes its runtime. npm and library use require **Node.js 24+**.

## Install

### Release binary (default)

Each line downloads the latest release asset, checks it against the release's SHA256SUMS and installs `ghostpaw-codex` into `~/.local/bin`. On Linux and macOS the trailing `export` puts that folder on PATH for the current shell only: neither the line nor `install.sh` edits `~/.profile` or any other shell startup file. The Windows script adds its folder to the user PATH (open a new terminal afterwards).

linux-x64:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --target linux-x64 && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

linux-arm64:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --target linux-arm64 && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

darwin-arm64:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --target darwin-arm64 && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

darwin-x64:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --target darwin-x64 && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

windows-x64 (PowerShell):

```powershell
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.ps1 | iex
```

To keep `~/.local/bin` on PATH in new shells, append it to `~/.profile` once (this is the only step that edits a startup file):

```sh
echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> ~/.profile
```

To pin a release instead of taking the latest, pass `--version`:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/install.sh | sh -s -- --target linux-x64 --version 0.6.0 && export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
```

```text
$ ghostpaw-codex --version
ghostpaw-codex 0.6.0 (binary, linux-x64)
$ ghostpaw-codex --version --short
0.6.0
$ ghostpaw-codex --version --json
{"name":"ghostpaw-codex","version":"0.6.0","variant":"binary","target":"linux-x64"}
```

`variant` is `binary`, `npm` or `library`; `target` is `null` outside the release binary.

A session with the 0.5.2 linux-x64 binary against a small database of five beliefs:

The same session as an [animated GIF](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GhostPawJS/codex/main/docs/assets/cli.gif).

Other release installers:

```sh
mise use -g github:GhostPawJS/codex
ubi --project GhostPawJS/codex --exe ghostpaw-codex --in ~/.local/bin
eget GhostPawJS/codex
```

For [aqua](https://aquaproj.github.io/docs/reference/registry-config/), define a
`github_release` package in `aqua.yaml`:

```yaml
registries:
  - name: codex
    type: local
    path: codex-registry.yaml
packages:
  - name: GhostPawJS/codex@v0.6.0
    registry: codex
```

`codex-registry.yaml`:

```yaml
packages:
  - type: github_release
    repo_owner: GhostPawJS
    repo_name: codex
    asset: ghostpaw-codex-{{trimV .Version}}-{{.OS}}-{{.Arch}}.tar.gz
    format: tar.gz
    replacements: { amd64: x64 }
    overrides:
      - goos: windows
        asset: ghostpaw-codex-{{trimV .Version}}-windows-{{.Arch}}.zip
        format: zip
    files:
      - name: ghostpaw-codex
```

Install scripts verify SHA256SUMS. To verify a downloaded archive's
[build attestation](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):

```sh
gh attestation verify <archive> -R GhostPawJS/codex
```

Set `GHOSTPAW_VERIFY=attestation` for attestation verification in `install.sh`.
Binaries are unsigned; macOS binaries carry an ad-hoc signature. For a browser
download on macOS, remove quarantine with
`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine /path/to/ghostpaw-codex`.
Linux binaries require glibc 2.28+; use npx on Alpine.
See the [binary build workflow](.github/workflows/release-binaries.yml).

Approximate sizes for 0.5.2 (Node 26.12.1 inside each binary):

| Target | Archive | Binary |
|---|---|---|
| linux-x64 | 41.7 MB tar.gz | 117.4 MB |
| linux-arm64 | 41.2 MB tar.gz | 115.2 MB |
| darwin-arm64 | 44.8 MB tar.gz | 146.7 MB |
| darwin-x64 | 46.4 MB tar.gz | 149.5 MB |
| windows-x64 | 38.4 MB zip | 105.6 MB |

The npm package is about 920 KB unpacked and needs Node 24+. Every release is
installed and run on ubuntu-24.04, macos-15 and windows-2025 by the
[install check](.github/workflows/install-check.yml).

### npx / npm (for npm-based environments)

The [npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@ghostpaw/codex) requires Node 24+:

```sh
npm install -g @ghostpaw/codex
npx -y @ghostpaw/codex --help
```

### Library (for harnesses embedding it in code)

Requires Node 24+:

```sh
npm install @ghostpaw/codex
```

```ts

```

# Mailoo

**Mailoo** (`@bitfloo/mailoo`) is a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for email (IMAP/SMTP), calendar, reminders, and ManageSieve automation developed and maintained by **Bitfloo**.

Enables AI assistants and autonomous agents to read, search, send, manage, schedule, and analyze emails, calendars, Reminders, and ManageSieve filter scripts across multiple accounts. Exposes up to 57 tools (with `full`, `core`, and `minimal` toolset profiles), up to 7 prompts, and 6 resources over MCP with `outputSchema` / `structuredContent`, OAuth2 support _(experimental)_, email scheduling, calendar extraction, analytics, provider-aware label management, real-time IMAP IDLE watcher with AI-powered triage, customizable presets and static rules, ManageSieve filters, and a guided setup wizard.

Behaviour for Sent copies, IMAP4rev2, Sieve, attachment `savePath`, read-only side effects, and reconnect backoff is documented in [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md) and [`docs/tools.md`](docs/tools.md).

## Highlights

| Feature | In this tree |
|---------|:------------:|
| Multi-account IMAP/SMTP | ✅ |
| Send / reply / forward (with `dryRun` preview) | ✅ |
| Drafts & templates | ✅ |
| Provider-aware labels & bulk ops | ✅ |
| Schedule future emails | ✅ |
| Real-time IMAP IDLE watcher | ✅ |

## Security & Sandboxing Architecture

Policy and how to report a vulnerability: **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)**.

Mailoo is engineered with defense-in-depth sandboxing so AI agents can safely interact with untrusted mail and external servers:

- **Zero Shell Execution (`execFile` only)** — Native OS integrations (macOS `osascript` for Calendar/Reminders/notifications, Linux `notify-send`, Windows `powershell`, and crontab installation) invoke `child_process.execFile` with strict argument arrays (`shell: false`), eliminating command injection vectors.
- **SSRF & DNS-Rebinding Protection (`net.BlockList`)** — Outbound alert webhooks validate URLs against an IPv4/IPv6 `net.BlockList` covering loopback, RFC 1918 private ranges, link-local/cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`, `100.100.100.200`), CGNAT, NAT64, 6to4, and reserved prefixes both at configuration time and at socket connection time (`createWebhookConnectLookup`), preventing DNS-rebinding attacks (`src/safety/validation.ts`).
- **Symlink-Free Write Containment (`savePath`)** — Attachment and `.eml` exports via `savePath` are strictly confined to the working directory, walk every path segment with `lstat`, refuse hidden dotfiles and OS persistence directories (`Library/LaunchAgents`, `.ssh`, `.gnupg`), and open targets with `O_CREAT | O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` under a **50 MiB** cap (**5 MiB** inline base64 cap). An `.eml` export is capped by its own size; an attachment by its encoded size in the message, which for base64 runs above the file size ([details](docs/tools.md#download_attachment)).
- **Prompt Injection Fencing (`<<<UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL_CONTENT>>>`)** — Untrusted email subjects, sender headers, message bodies, previews, and authentication results are wrapped in `<<<UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL_CONTENT>>>` … `<<<END_UNTRUSTED_EXTERNAL_CONTENT>>>` delimiters (stripping any forged markers inside the payload) so LLMs treat external mail as data, not instructions.
- **Strict Credential File Permissions (`0600`)** — `config.toml` is written and verified with mode `0600` inside a `0700` config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/mailoo/config.toml`). Passwords and message bodies are redacted from the JSONL write audit log (`src/safety/audit.ts`).
- **TLS & STARTTLS Verification** — `tls` enforces implicit TLS with certificate verification (`verify_ssl = true` by default); `starttls` fails closed if the server does not advertise `STARTTLS`. Turning both off is accepted only for a loopback host. ManageSieve refuses `AUTHENTICATE PLAIN` over unencrypted sockets without `STARTTLS`.
- **Operational Guardrails (`MCP_EMAIL_READ_ONLY`, `MCP_EMAIL_TOOLSET`, `dryRun`)** —
  - `MCP_EMAIL_READ_ONLY=true` disables all write tools, background watchers, hooks, and schedulers at startup, exposing only the 31 read-only tools.
  - `MCP_EMAIL_TOOLSET=full|core|minimal` scopes the registered tool surface to match the agent's capability tier and context budget.
  - `dryRun: true` on high-risk tools (`send_email`, `reply_email`, `forward_email`, `send_draft`, `delete_email`, `bulk_action`, `delete_mailbox`, `sieve_put_script`, `sieve_delete_script`) validates all parameters and account resolution and returns a `[DRY RUN]` preview without modifying server state.
- **Per-Account Rate Limiting** — `rate_limit` (default 10 sends/minute) enforces an independent token bucket per account (`src/safety/rate-limiter.ts`). Buckets live in memory, so each server process and each `mailoo scheduler check` run counts on its own.

readme.markdown:
# LLMtoMD MCP Server

Turn PDFs, Office documents, websites and audio into clean, AI-ready Markdown, and let your AI assistant search and answer questions across everything you've converted.

LLMtoMD is a **hosted** MCP server. There's nothing to install or run: connect your client to the endpoint below and sign in with your LLMtoMD account.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Endpoint** | `https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp` |
| **Transport** | Streamable HTTP |
| **Auth** | OAuth 2.1 (PKCE + dynamic client registration). Your client opens a sign-in page; no API keys to copy. |
| **Registry** | [`com.llmtomd/llmtomd`](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=llmtomd) on the official MCP Registry |
| **Account** | Free sign-up at [llmtomd.com](https://llmtomd.com/login?mode=register) |

## Connect

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

[**Install in VS Code**](vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22llmtomd%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.llmtomd.com%2Fmcp%22%7D)

Or add it by hand: **Command Palette → MCP: Add Server → HTTP**, enter `https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp`, and sign in when prompted. You can also add it to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "llmtomd": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp" }
  }
}
```

### Claude (web and desktop)

**Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, paste `https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp`, then sign in.

### ChatGPT

**Settings → Apps & Connectors → Create** (developer mode), use `https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp` with OAuth, then sign in.

### Cursor and other clients

Any MCP client that supports remote Streamable HTTP servers with OAuth works. Point it at `https://mcp.llmtomd.com/mcp`.

## Tools

**Convert**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `convert_url` | Convert a web page or a publicly reachable file URL into Markdown |
| `convert_file` | Convert a small local file (sent inline) into Markdown |
| `upload_file` | Get a one-time upload URL for large or binary files (big PDFs, scans, audio, video) |
| `convert_upload` | Convert a file uploaded with `upload_file` |

**Your library**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list_documents` | List documents in your LLMtoMD library, newest first |
| `get_document` | Fetch a stored document's full Markdown |
| `search_documents` | Semantic search across your documents |
| `ask_documents` | Answer a question from your documents, with sources |
| `list_collections` | List your collections (projects) and their document counts |
| `save_note` | Save text or Markdown into your library so it's searchable later |

**Coding-task scope guard**

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `start_task` | Record the approved file boundary of a coding task before editing |
| `check_scope` | Check changed files against that boundary |
| `approve_scope` | Widen the boundary when a human approves extra files |
| `close_task` | Mark a task finished |
| `list_tasks` | List task scopes and their status |

## Supported formats

PDF (including scanned PDFs via OCR), Word (DOCX), PowerPoint (PPTX), Excel (XLSX), HTML and whole-site crawls, images, and audio/video transcription. See [llmtomd.com/formats](https://llmtomd.com/formats).

## Privacy and security

Source files are processed and deleted automatically within 24 hours. Converted documents stay in your account until you delete them. You can disconnect a client at any time from your LLMtoMD dashboard, which cuts its access immediately. See [llmtomd.com/security](https://llmtomd.com/security) and [llmtomd.com/privacy](https://llmtomd.com/privacy).

## Pricing

A free plan is available, and conversions use credits. See [llmtomd.com/pricing](https://llmtomd.com/pricing).

## Support

Email [support@llmtomd.com](mailto:support@llmtomd.com) or [open an issue](../../issues) in this repository.

---

This repository documents the hosted LLMtoMD MCP server. The service itself is closed source; the documentation here is MIT licensed.
