readme.markdown: # ZeroDOM ### Point it at an app as two users. It finds the broken access control. ZeroDOM drives your **real, logged-in browser** as two identities, replays the same requests as each, and flags where one user reaches what another can't — **IDOR / broken access control**, caught deterministically. Open-core, runs local, no account, no API key, nothing leaves your machine. Under the hunt is a deterministic, token-lean perception engine for AI agents — the same core powers scan, crawl and any browser-driving task. IDOR is just where it bites hardest. **[Site](https://zerodom.vexralabs.com)** · **[Docs](https://zerodom.vexralabs.com/docs)** · **[Playground](https://zerodom.vexralabs.com/playground)** · **[Discord](https://discord.gg/tVRznUb5Ez)** · **[Quickstart ↓](#quickstart)** A normal user is denied the admin console (401) — then walks in by flipping one client-controlled cookie. ZeroDOM proves it: same request, two identities, 401 vs 200. Full recording (mp4). --- ## Contents - [Why ZeroDOM](#why-zerodom) - [Quickstart](#quickstart) - [How it hunts — `compare` & `sweep`](#how-it-hunts--compare--sweep) - [Use it from an AI agent (MCP)](#use-it-from-an-ai-agent-mcp) - [Why the agent sees so few tokens](#why-the-agent-sees-so-few-tokens) - [More of the CLI](#more-of-the-cli) - [How it compares](#how-it-compares) - [Install](#install) - [Security & scope](#security--scope) - [Limitations](#limitations) - [Editions](#editions) - [Contributing & development](#contributing--development) - [License](#license) --- ## Why ZeroDOM **Two audiences, one engine:** - **AppSec — [`compare` / `sweep`](#how-it-hunts--compare--sweep):** deterministic two-identity authorization testing that runs **headless in CI or your recon pipeline** — no GUI, no account. `scan --js` adds DOM-XSS sinks, the callable API surface and header posture; `repeat` / `probe` / `race` turn recon into verification (Repeater, mass-assignment diff, and a TOCTOU burst). - **AI agents — [MCP](#use-it-from-an-ai-agent-mcp):** a flat interaction graph that cuts **~71% of the tokens** vs Playwright's `aria_snapshot`, with handles that resolve 1:1 and don't drift when the page re-renders. **Broken access control is the #1 web vulnerability** (OWASP A01) and the one automated scanners miss — because catching it means knowing *who should be allowed to do what*, not just fuzzing one session. The usual answer is a human in Burp, clicking through the app as one user, then again as another, diffing by eye. ZeroDOM does that mechanically. Give it two logged-in sessions; it replays the same request as each and reports the deterministic tells: - **`access-boundary-split`** — one identity gets `200`, the other `401/403` on an identical request. If the only difference between them is client-controllable (a cookie, header or param), that's broken access control. - **`cross-identity-identical-response`** — two users get a **byte-identical** body on a per-user resource: a cross-tenant IDOR. No LLM guessing, no "the AI thinks maybe." ZeroDOM surfaces the tell with the exact replay that proves it — a reviewable diff you drop straight into a bug report. **You confirm the bug.** It drives your **real Chrome** (relay mode) over `chrome.debugger`, so your cookies, MFA and SSO are already done — or a throwaway browser (`--stealth`) if you'd rather not touch your session. Either way the page's markup never leaves your machine, and it's **read-only by default**: destructive actions and out-of-scope hosts are refused. > It works equally well as a one-line CLI, a recon pipeline stage, or a native tool an > **AI agent** drives through MCP. Same deterministic primitives, three front doors. --- ## Quickstart **See it run in 10 seconds** — no account, no browser download (bare `zerodom ` is a static fetch, no Chromium needed): ```bash pip install zerodom # or: uvx zerodom · npm i @vexralabs/zerodom zerodom https://news.ycombinator.com # the interaction graph + a token report ``` That's the perception engine — a flat, 1:1-addressable graph instead of 12k tokens of HTML. **Now the flagship — find an IDOR.** Save two logged-in sessions as Playwright `storage_state` files (one per account), then diff a protected endpoint across both: ```bash zerodom compare https://app.example.com/api/admin/dashboard \ --as user=user.json --as admin=admin.json ``` ```jsonc { "identities": { "user": { "status": 401, "bytes": 2616 }, "admin": { "status": 200, "bytes": 3469 } }, "only_admin": ["Manage users", "Billing & plans", "Overview"], "note": "admin authorized (200) where user denied (401) — broken access control if the only difference is client-controllable" } ``` That's the whole loop: same request, two identities, a 401-vs-200 split → a lead to confirm. `only_admin` lists the privileged controls the normal user should never see. **Don't have storage-state files?** Capture one with `context.storage_state(path="user.json")` in Playwright, or export cookies from a logged-in session. **Want the whole app, not one URL?** → [`zerodom sweep`](#how-it-hunts--compare--sweep). --- ## How it hunts — `compare` & `sweep` ### `zerodom compare` — one endpoint, across identities Fetch one URL under each saved session and diff the responses. Byte-identical content across two users on a private resource is a cross-tenant IDOR; a 401-vs-200 split is a broken boundary. `only_` lists the actionable nodes each identity sees that the other doesn't. ```bash # Sweep a range of object ids through two identities: seq 1 500 | sed 's#^#https://app.example.com/api/invoice/#' \ | zerodom compare - --as alice=alice.json --as bob=bob.json \ | jq 'select(.identical_body_pairs | length > 0)' ``` ### `zerodom sweep` — the whole app, one command `compare` tests one URL. **`sweep` does the entire app:** it crawls as one identity to map th …

readme.markdown:
# Flowsimp MCP Server

Create flowcharts from chat. Flowsimp's hosted [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server turns Mermaid flowchart syntax or a plain indented outline into a shareable diagram link and an editable board in the [Flowsimp](https://flowsimp.com) editor.

- **Endpoint:** `https://flowsimp.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP (remote)
- **Auth:** none, no API key or account needed
- **Price:** completely free to use
- **Registry name:** `com.flowsimp/flowsimp` in the [official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0/servers?search=com.flowsimp)
- **Docs:** https://flowsimp.com/mcp

The server is stateless. It does not store your diagrams, because each diagram is encoded in the link it returns. Open the editable link to rearrange shapes, edit text, and export PNG or SVG.

This repository holds the public documentation and the registry metadata (`server.json`, `.mcp.json`) for the hosted server.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create_flowchart` | Builds a flowchart from Mermaid flowchart syntax or an indented outline (up to 16,000 characters). Optional `title`, and optional `mode`: `flowchart` (default) or `network`. Returns a read-only `shareUrl`, an editable `editUrl`, and the node and connection counts. |
| `list_templates` | Lists the built-in templates (flowchart, process, swimlane, decision tree, user flow, org chart, network, mind map) with a link that opens each one in the editor. |

Example `create_flowchart` input:

```json
{
  "text": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B{Approved?}\n  B -->|Yes| C[Ship it]\n  B -->|No| D[Revise]",
  "title": "Release check"
}
```

Example result (links shortened):

```json
{
  "shareUrl": "https://flowsimp.com/view#…",
  "editUrl": "https://flowsimp.com/?board=…",
  "nodeCount": 4,
  "connectionCount": 3,
  "title": "Release check"
}
```

An indented outline works too:

```text
Customer submits order
  Payment approved?
    Yes: Pack and ship
    No: Email customer
```

## Connect a client

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Open **Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector**, name it `Flowsimp`, and paste:

```
https://flowsimp.com/mcp
```

No authentication settings are needed.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http flowsimp https://flowsimp.com/mcp
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` (global) or `.cursor/mcp.json` (project):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "flowsimp": {
      "url": "https://flowsimp.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code (GitHub Copilot agent mode)

Add to `.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "flowsimp": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://flowsimp.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### ChatGPT

In workspaces or plans that support custom MCP connectors (developer mode), create a connector with the URL `https://flowsimp.com/mcp` and no authentication. You can also add a GPT Action from the OpenAPI description at `https://flowsimp.com/openapi.json`.

### Clients that only support local (stdio) servers

Use the [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote) bridge:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "flowsimp": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://flowsimp.com/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Example prompts

- "Make a flowchart of our customer refund process and give me the Flowsimp link."
- "Turn this Mermaid code into an editable diagram: …"
- "Draw a decision tree for whether to approve a vacation request."
- "Map the user sign-up flow for a mobile app, from landing page to first login."
- "Show me the Flowsimp templates, then start me on a swimlane diagram."
- "Create a simple network diagram: router, firewall, two web servers, and a database."

## HTTP API

The same create action is available without MCP:

```bash
curl -X POST https://flowsimp.com/api/flowchart \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"text": "flowchart TD\n  A[Start] --> B[Next]"}'
```

The OpenAPI description is at https://flowsimp.com/openapi.json.

## Limits

- Text input is capped at 16,000 characters.
- Calls are rate limited per IP.

## Links

- Flowsimp editor: https://flowsimp.com
- MCP docs: https://flowsimp.com/mcp
- Text to flowchart: https://flowsimp.com/text-to-flowchart
- About: https://flowsimp.com/about

## License

The contents of this repository are released under the [MIT License](LICENSE). © 2026 Dreamer Studio.

readme.markdown: Funplay MCP for Cocos An Embedded MCP Server for Cocos Creator Editor 中文 | English > If this project helps your Cocos workflow, please consider giving it a Star. It helps more developers discover the project and supports ongoing development. --- Funplay MCP for Cocos is an MIT-licensed Cocos Creator extension that embeds an HTTP MCP server directly inside the editor. It lets AI assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code Copilot, Trae, Kiro, Qoder, Kimi Code, OpenCode, CodeBuddy, and DeepSeek Harness (DSH) inspect and operate your running Cocos project. The package follows the same product direction as Funplay MCP for Unity: keep the default tool surface focused, provide a one-click client configuration window, and make one high-flexibility execution tool the primary workflow. For Cocos, the primary tool is `execute_javascript`: - `context: "scene"` runs JavaScript in the active Cocos scene/runtime context - `context: "editor"` runs JavaScript in the Cocos editor/browser context > *"Create a login page UI with account/password fields and a main login button."* > > Your AI assistant can call `execute_javascript`, build the UI hierarchy under the active Canvas, attach Cocos components, inspect the result, and capture a screenshot for validation. ## Quick Start If you just want to connect quickly, do these three things: - Install this repository as a Cocos Creator extension - Open `Funplay > MCP Server` - Use the built-in one-click MCP client configuration ### 1. Install as a Cocos Creator Extension Recommended install: use the official [Cocos Store page](https://store.cocos.com/app/detail/8913) and install the extension into your target Cocos Creator project. For local development or unreleased builds, clone or copy this repository into your Cocos project extension directory: ```bash cd /path/to/your-cocos-project mkdir -p extensions git clone https://github.com/FunplayAI/funplay-cocos-mcp.git extensions/funplay-cocos-mcp ``` Then restart Cocos Creator or reload extensions from the editor. For a non-git install, download `Funplay.CocosMcp.v.zip` from the GitHub Releases page, unzip it, and move the extracted `funplay-cocos-mcp` folder into your project `extensions/` directory. #### Install for All Projects (Recommended) Install and open the extension in any project first. Then open `Funplay > MCP Settings` and click **Install for All Projects** in the All Projects section. The extension downloads the latest GitHub Release, verifies `SHA256SUMS.txt`, and installs it into the active Cocos Creator version's managed global extension directory: - macOS / Linux: `~/.CocosCreator/builtin-extensions//funplay-cocos-mcp` - Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.CocosCreator\builtin-extensions\\funplay-cocos-mcp` Cocos Creator scans and registers the installed copy immediately. Projects opened or created with that Creator version then load it automatically, and the MCP server keeps its default autostart behavior. Reopen an already-running project if its project-level copy has priority. No extension files are copied into each project's `extensions/` directory. Global extensions are isolated by Cocos Creator version. If you use multiple Creator versions, run **Install for All Projects** once from each version. The installer does not delete the current project copy, which protects development worktrees. If both copies exist, MCP Settings shows a duplicate-install warning. After confirming that the global copy works, remove or disable the project copy to avoid extension conflicts. ### 2. Start the MCP Server Open the editor menu: ```text Funplay > MCP Server ``` New projects get a stable project-derived port in `20000–29999`. Existing saved configurations keep their fixed port (including `8765`). Use the exact URL shown in MCP Server; if a temporary fallback port is active, click **Pin Current Port** or **Use Per-Project Port** before configuring a client. If the configured port is already occupied, the extension first checks whether the existing listener belongs to the same Cocos project. Same-project listeners are reused safely; unrelated listeners trigger automatic fallback to the next available local port. The panel is intentionally small: - Enable or disable the MCP server - Open focused Tool Exposure, MCP Settings, and Project Skills windows - Automatically check the installed version against the latest GitHub release - Open the release page or install verified release packages from the panel - Install once in the Cocos Creator global extensions directory so existing and new projects can use it automatically - Configure AI clients with one click and preview the selected client config - Keep advanced tool profile editing, transport settings, and installation management out of the main server window - Follow the Cocos Creator interface language automatically, or select Chinese/English per project in MCP Settings - Toggle **Print MCP logs** in Settings to silence MCP console messages without losing Recent Activity or internal diagnostics All management pages use consistent headings, aligned controls, and lightweight sections. Tool Exposure groups per-tool toggles by category; Project Skills highlights available actions and folds away file paths and backups. Recent Activity shows each call's summary and actual result as an expandable object/array tree, with execution logs and return values in separate sections for scripts. Output sections and the standalone log-viewing panel are removed. Short action notices preserve success/failure feedback, while diagnostic logs remain available to MCP tools and resources. Script tools capture per-call `console.log/info/warn/error/debug` output, including logs before a failure, independently of **Print MCP logs**. Capture is isolated across concurrent and nested calls and stops when the script settles; global/project logs and logs …

readme.markdown:
# DeepDNA MCP server

A remote [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that gives AI agents cited pharmacogenomic and gene-variant lookups, so answers can quote CPIC and DPWG guidance and its sources. This repository also holds a [local package](#read-a-raw-dna-file-on-your-own-computer) that reads a raw DNA file on the user's own computer; nothing from the file is sent to DeepDNA, but what the package reports becomes part of the conversation with the AI model.

```text
https://deepdna.ai/mcp
```

Streamable HTTP, stateless, no API key, no account. Listed in the official MCP registry as `ai.deepdna/knowledge`.

> Educational information only, not medical advice. The server reports what curated sources and guidelines say about a gene, a variant or a drug–gene pair. It does not diagnose, prescribe or recommend a dose.

## Tools

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `list_genes` | The genes in the knowledge base, with a one-line summary and category for each |
| `lookup_gene` | Everything curated about one gene: function, key variants with rsIDs, phenotypes, drug interactions, what a consumer genotyping array can and cannot tell you, and sources |
| `lookup_variant` | One variant by dbSNP rsID: gene, star-allele or common name, alleles on the plus strand of GRCh37, effect, frequency note and sources. Takes the rsID only, never a genotype |
| `lookup_drug_gene` | Guidance for a gene, optionally for one drug: guideline (CPIC or DPWG where one exists), summary, phenotype groups and sources |
| `check_medications` | Splits a list of generic drug names into drugs with a curated record (gene, and a `basis` field: CPIC or DPWG guideline, drug label, or primary literature) and drugs not covered. Needs no genotype |

All five tools are read-only.

Two prompts, `medication_review` and `explain_variant`, package the common questions for clients that show MCP prompts.

Coverage today is 12 genes: CYP2C19, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, SLCO1B1, VKORC1, UGT1A1, G6PD, MTHFR, COMT, HFE, APOE and BRCA1, with 51 curated drug–gene pairs across 11 of them: 40 cite a CPIC or DPWG guideline, the rest a drug label or the primary literature; the `basis` field in `check_medications` says which (`guideline` is null, or "drug label", when no guideline exists). It is a small, reviewed set, not a mirror of PharmGKB/ClinPGx. Every record lists its sources. The `level` field (the guideline's evidence grade) is `null` for every pair today.

## Connect

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http deepdna https://deepdna.ai/mcp
```

**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`) and other clients that use an `mcpServers` file:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deepdna": { "type": "http", "url": "https://deepdna.ai/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "deepdna": { "type": "http", "url": "https://deepdna.ai/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Claude Desktop and claude.ai:** add `https://deepdna.ai/mcp` as a custom connector.

**Gemini CLI** (installs the remote, read-only server `https://deepdna.ai/mcp` as an extension, not the local package; `gemini-extension.json` is in this repo):

```bash
gemini extensions install https://github.com/alfonsoguv/deepdna-mcp
```

## Try it without a client

```bash
curl -s https://deepdna.ai/mcp \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "Accept: application/json, text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"lookup_drug_gene","arguments":{"gene":"CYP2C19","drug":"clopidogrel"}}}'
```

The answer carries the CPIC recommendation for clopidogrel by CYP2C19 metabolizer group, the sources it was written from, and the disclaimer. The same data is available as plain REST, documented in the [API docs](https://deepdna.ai/docs/) and the [OpenAPI spec](https://deepdna.ai/openapi.json):

```text
GET https://deepdna.ai/api/v1/pgx/CYP2C19/clopidogrel
GET https://deepdna.ai/api/v1/variants/rs4244285
```

## Read a raw DNA file on your own computer

The remote server takes no genotype: its tools have no field for one. For a raw DNA file there is a local package in this repository. It reads the file on the user's computer and reports what it shows at each position DeepDNA curates, with the cited records. Nothing from the file is sent to deepdna.ai: the package downloads the same public records for every user, and `lookup_drug_gene` sends only the gene and drug names. What `read_dna_file` returns (the letters and counts at the curated positions) becomes part of the conversation with the AI model your client uses, under that provider's terms.

**Claude Code** (needs [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/); the package is on [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/deepdna-mcp/)):

```bash
claude mcp add deepdna-local -- uvx deepdna-mcp@0.1.2
```

The [`plugin/`](plugin/) folder packages the same command as a Claude plugin, for Claude Code and for Cowork sessions on the user's computer.

Clients that use an `mcpServers` file (if the client cannot find `uvx`, put its full path, from `which uvx`, in `command`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "deepdna-local": { "command": "uvx", "args": ["deepdna-mcp@0.1.2"] }
  }
}
```

| Tool | What it returns |
|---|---|
| `read_dna_file` | What a 23andMe, AncestryDNA or MyHeritage/FamilyTreeDNA export (.txt, .csv or .zip) shows at each curated position |
| `lookup_drug_gene` | Guidance for a gene, optionally for one drug, from the public API. Sends only the gene and drug names |

- Each position gets one of four states: `read`, `no_call`, `not_in_file`, or `unexpected_letters` (letters that fit neither the record nor its complement). A missing or unreadable position is unknown, never normal.
- For positions the record marks as `countable` (no phasing or other variants are needed to read them), it gives how many copies of the variant allele the file shows, with the record's text and sources.
- `genes` limits the answer to what the user asked about. APOE, BRCA1 and HFE are disease-risk genes: they are

# Atlas Mind

[![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-demo-635bff.svg)](https://atlas-mind.anakior.app/) [![Licence: AGPL v3](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-AGPL--3.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE) ![Python 3.11+](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-blue.svg) ![Dependencies: standard library](https://img.shields.io/badge/deps-standard%20library-green.svg) ![Database: none](https://img.shields.io/badge/database-none-green.svg)

> **It's your mind, not someone else's.**

Notion, and every hosted notes app, ask you to pour your thinking into *their* structure, on *their* servers, in *their* format. You rent the space; they hold the keys. Atlas Mind inverts that: your knowledge is **plain files in your own git repository**, served by an **engine you can read line by line** and throw away without losing a single note. Your AI comes to *your* library through an open protocol; it never pulls your brain into its own.

Own the data. Own the engine. Own the mind.

  

> 🔗 **[Try the live demo →](https://atlas-mind.anakior.app/demo/)** (offline build, some features missing) · **[What is Atlas Mind?](https://atlas-mind.anakior.app/)**

**Atlas Mind** is a self-hostable wiki / knowledge base engine, and an external brain you share with your AI. It serves a single-page viewer from a folder of documents (a *mind*), keeping the **engine** (the code) cleanly decoupled from your **content** (your notes, in their own git repository). Built on three ideas:

- **Multi-format, not just Markdown.** Markdown is first-class (rendered, linked, searched). Standalone **HTML** decks and dashboards, **PDFs**, **Word `.docx`**, **images** and **JSON** are previewed inline, rendered in your browser, nothing uploaded anywhere.
- **AI-native.** It exposes an **MCP** endpoint (thirty-four tools to read, write, triage, map, rewind and audit your mind), and `atlas init` scaffolds the conventions (`AGENTS.md`, `agents/`, `ai-sessions/`) so an assistant knows how to use your mind.
- **Lightweight & self-contained.** A single Python HTTP server on the **standard library**: **no database**, accounts and share links live as plain JSON on disk, frontend libraries and fonts are vendored. A running instance **never sends your content anywhere**: your mind never leaves your disk, and nothing you write trains anyone's model. Its only outbound request by default is reading an MCP client's public metadata when you connect that client over OAuth (switchable off).

It is not a multi-tenant SaaS, a real-time collaborative editor, or a plugin marketplace. One focused mind per instance, fully yours.

## Install

Installing puts a self-contained `atlas` command on your PATH (the viewer assets ship inside the package, no separate download).

```bash
# Easy way: uv or pipx (isolated env, no virtualenv to manage)
uv tool install atlas-mind        # or: pipx install atlas-mind
atlas serve ~/my-mind

# Run once without installing, straight from PyPI
uvx atlas-mind serve ~/my-mind    # or: pipx run atlas-mind serve ~/my-mind

# With pip (a virtualenv is recommended)
pip install atlas-mind
```

Requires **Python >= 3.11** and a **git repository for your content**.

## Quick start

```bash
atlas init ~/my-mind     # scaffold a mind: atlas.toml, example docs, AGENTS.md, git init
atlas serve ~/my-mind    # build once if needed, then serve on http://127.0.0.1:8765
```

`init` is never destructive (it refuses a non-empty directory without `--force` and keeps any file already present). `serve` listens on `127.0.0.1:8765` with authentication off by default. To produce the static viewer without serving: `atlas build ~/my-mind [--offline]`.

See `atlas --help` for all commands (`user`, `token`, `share`, `deploy`).

## Use it with your AI (MCP)

Atlas Mind is designed to be the external memory your assistant reads and writes. On a deployed instance, point your assistant at **`https://<your-atlas>/mcp`** and it connects over **OAuth**: you sign in to your Atlas (2FA included), review what the assistant asks for (read, inbox, write — untick what you don't want to grant) and allow it. The connection shows up in **Settings → Tokens**, where you can revoke it; it renews itself silently, and only asks again after 30 days unused.

Clients either register themselves (dynamic client registration) or identify by the URL of a public metadata document, which Atlas fetches when you connect them; `[oauth] client_metadata_fetch = false` in `atlas.toml` turns that fetch off.

You can also mint a token yourself, from the web UI — **Settings → Tokens**, bound to your account — which prints a URL with the token in it. Locally (or to script it), the CLI does the same:

```bash
atlas token create ~/my-mind --label claude
# → prints the MCP URL: https://<your-atlas>/mcp/<token>
```

The MCP endpoint exposes **thirty-four tools** in six groups:

- **read**: `brief` (a context pack on a topic: the best sections, within a token budget), `search_docs` (ranked, each hit with its section and how far to trust it: last editor, AI or human, stale, contested), `grep_docs` (exact lines), `read_doc` (whole doc, a line range or one section), `list_tree`, `recent_docs`, `changes_since` (what changed since a cursor the agent keeps), `resume_session` (pick up a saved work session: its resume command, the open points and how long each has been carried, what changed since)
- **write**: `create_doc`, `edit_doc` (returns the diff; `dry_run`, and a `base_version` guard so a concurrent change is never overwritten), `move_doc` (fixes incoming `[[backlinks]]`), `delete_doc` (soft-delete to `.trash/`)
- **graph**: `get_links`, `get_backlinks`, `list_by_tag`, `get_mind_topology`
- **time-travel** (your mind is a git repo): `doc_history`, `doc_at`, `doc_diff`, `search_history`, `then_and_now` + `show_shift` (what the mind said on a topic at a past date next to what it says now, claim by claim, every quote checked word for word against the version it cites), `changelog`, `doc_blame`, `doc_revert

readme.markdown:
# kenotex-mcp

**Let your coding agent manage your real todos, calendar, and habits.**

[Kenotex](https://kenxcomp.com/kenotex/?ct=npm-mcp) is a native planner for Mac and iPhone.
This package is its MCP server: point Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Zed, or any MCP
client at it, and the agent works on the actual items in the app — creating todos with
categories and recurrence, scheduling calendar events, ticking off daily or interval check-in habits.
Not a scratchpad, not a markdown file. Everything lives in a local SQLite database on your
own machine.

> **Your agent writes on your Mac. It's on your iPhone via iCloud.**

Works with **Claude Code**, **Claude Desktop**, **Cursor**, **Zed**, **OpenClaw**, and
anything else that speaks MCP over stdio.

## Get the app

These tools drive the Kenotex **macOS** app — it hosts the local server this package talks
to, so you need it installed and running. Free to download, with in-app purchases.

**The MCP integration is not one of those purchases.** Every tool in this package talks to
the app's local HTTP server, which has no subscription gate — the whole integration works
on the free tier.

**→ [kenxcomp.com/kenotex](https://kenxcomp.com/kenotex/?ct=npm-mcp)**

## Prerequisites

- **macOS 26 or later** — the app's minimum. The iPhone app syncs over iCloud, but the MCP
  server talks to the Mac.
- The Kenotex macOS app must be **running** (it hosts the local HTTP server on port 21519).
- Node.js 20+ or Bun.

## Install

Globally:

```bash
npm install -g kenotex-mcp
# or
bun add -g kenotex-mcp
```

Or use it directly via npx / bunx (no install):

```bash
npx kenotex-mcp
```

## Configure in an MCP client

### Claude Desktop

Edit `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "kenotex": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "kenotex-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Claude Desktop. You'll see the Kenotex tools appear in the 🛠️ menu.

### Cursor / Zed / OpenClaw

Same pattern: point the MCP config at `kenotex-mcp` as the `command`.

### Environment overrides

- `KENOTEX_HOST` — override base URL (default `http://127.0.0.1:21519`).
- `KENOTEX_TOKEN` — skip filesystem token discovery and use this token.

## Tools exposed

| Category   | Tool                                                |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| Todo       | `create_todo` `list_todos` `get_todo` `update_todo` `complete_todo` `delete_todo` |
| Event      | `create_event` `list_events` `get_event` `update_event` `delete_event` |
| Habit      | `create_habit` `list_habits` `get_habit` `update_habit` `set_habit_check` `list_habit_checks` `delete_habit` |
| Category   | `list_categories` `create_category`                 |
| Reminder   | `add_reminder` `remove_reminder`                    |

**`create_todo` requires a `categoryId`** — todos can no longer be created uncategorized. The flow is: call `list_categories` and reuse a matching category's id; if none fits, call `create_category` and use the returned id, then `create_todo`.

**Habits are check-in trackers** (medication, water, stretching) — **daily** by default (up to 6 dose times/day), or **interval** (Q times every N days / N times a week / N times a month) via `cadence`. Use `create_habit` for routines the user ticks off; use `create_todo` + recurrence for one-off tasks or *fixed-slot* schedules (a particular weekday, a particular day of the month) — `cadence` counts how many times per period, recurrence pins which day. Writes take `times: ["HH:mm", …]`; reads return `times: [{id, time}]` — pass a slot's `id` as `slotId` to `set_habit_check` for a multi-dose habit (omit it to check all of today's doses). `cadence: {"unit":"day"|"week"|"month","interval":N,"quota"?:Q,"startDate"?:"yyyy-MM-dd"}` makes an interval habit — `quota` defaults to 1, out-of-range is a 422 and is never clamped, `startDate` defaults to today and can never be changed afterwards, and an interval habit takes at most one dose time:

| `unit` | `interval` | `quota` | period |
|---|---|---|---|
| `day` | 1–365 | 1–`interval` | N calendar days, so `quota ≤ N`; `day/1` takes quota 1 = explicitly daily |
| `week` | 1–8 | 1–7×`interval` | N week(s) |
| `month` | 1–12 | 1–min(31×`interval`, 365) | N whole **calendar** months (1st → last day), so the due day is always month end and the period's length follows the calendar rather than a fixed 30 days |

Examples: `{"unit":"day","interval":3}` = every 3 days · `{"unit":"day","interval":5,"quota":2}` = twice every 5 days · `{"unit":"week","interval":1,"quota":2}` = twice a week · `{"unit":"month","interval":1,"quota":2}` = twice a month.

Reads add `cadence`, `isIntervalHabit` and `currentPeriod {start,end,dueDay,doneCount,quota,done}` (`quota` is the period's effective quota — the configured quota clamped to the period's checkable days from `startDate` on, so a 31-a-month habit reports 28 in February and 17 for a first month started on the 14th) — use `currentPeriod.done` for "is this period satisfied" (`checkedToday` stays a calendar-day fact). `update_habit {"cadence": null}` turns an interval habit back into a daily one (anchor kept). A daily cadence with a future start — `{"unit":"day","interval":1,"startDate":"<future yyyy-MM-dd>"}` — makes a daily habit that starts that day: until then reads report `isStarted: false` and `set_habit_check` is a 422 on `date`. Interval habits are checked per calendar day (no `slotId`; `date` never in the future). Checking is explicit **set-state** (`checked: true|false`, `date` defaults to today, idempotent, `false` un-checks). **`delete_habit` permanently deletes the habit and its entire check-in history** — set an `endDate` via `update_habit` to stop-but-keep-records instead.

**App version**: habit tools require the Kenotex app release that ships `/v1/habits` (1.2.9+, local API v2). `cadence` additionally requires the release that advertises local API **v3** — against

# RevClamp MCP Server & CLI (`revclamp-mcp`)

**`revclamp-mcp`** is a standalone, zero-dependency **Open-Source Model Context Protocol (MCP) Server & CLI** (`index.mjs` + `local_engine.mjs`) implementing **9 deterministic B2B FinOps, Stripe `2025-03-31.basil`, Visa CE 3.0, EU/XI VIES VAT, Shopify Plus B2B Net-15/30/60, and Webhook Security tools** in pure Node.js.

- **100% Local In-Process Execution (Default — Zero Network / Zero API Key Required):** All 9 MCP tools (`initialize`, `tools/list`, and `tools/call`) execute locally in-process inside [`local_engine.mjs`](./local_engine.mjs) using pure Node.js (`node:crypto` HMAC-SHA256 verification, integer-cent double-entry accounting, 72-hour webhook replay state machines, and `18,000` UTF-16 code unit CE 3.0 linting). Zero network calls are ever made unless `REVCLAMP_API_KEY` or `REVCLAMP_MCP_URL` is explicitly configured.
- **Optional Hosted Cloud Workspace Sync (`REVCLAMP_API_KEY`):** When `REVCLAMP_API_KEY` (`rg_live_...`) is configured, `revclamp-mcp` connects to [**RevClamp Enterprise**](https://revclamp.com) (`https://api.revclamp.com/api/mcp`) to unlock the **90-day SQLite WAL usage & audit ledger**, **24/7 autonomous Stripe dispute & entitlement webhook outbox**, and **real-time EU Commission VIES SOAP gateway consultation numbers**.

## Local Open-Core (`local_engine.mjs`) vs. Hosted Cloud (`REVCLAMP_API_KEY`)

| Capability | Local Open-Core Default (Zero API Key) | Hosted Cloud (`REVCLAMP_API_KEY`) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Execution & Network** | 100% in-process (`local_engine.mjs`), zero network calls | HTTPS JSON-RPC to `https://api.revclamp.com/api/mcp` (`redirect: "error"`) |
| **Usage & Audit Storage** | Stateless evaluation of caller-supplied JSON snapshots | **Persistent 90-day SQLite WAL ledger** + Stripe historical backfill |
| **Dispute & Entitlement Action** | Returns non-destructive `submit: false` draft & `revoke_entitlement` decision | **24/7 autonomous Stripe webhook outbox** (`disputes.update` & signed revoke webhooks) |
| **EU & `XI` B2B VAT (`VIES`)** | Deterministic syntax & `GR -> EL` normalization (`FORMAT_ONLY` default, `valid: null`) | **Live EU Commission VIES SOAP consultation IDs** + circuit-breaker retry queue (`viesMode: "LIVE"` + `REVCLAMP_API_KEY`) |
| **Monthly Event Tiers** | Unlimited local in-process evaluations (0 network cost) | **Free Sandbox** (`5,000` events/mo) · **Starter $19/mo** (`100k`) · **Growth $59/mo** (`1M`) · **Scale $199/mo** (`5M`) |
| **Data Privacy (`INV-SAAS-04`)** | Nothing ever leaves your machine | Only explicit `tools/call` arguments are sent over TLS after local live-secret scrubbing (`scanMcpClientPayloadForSecrets` in `index.mjs` blocks `sk_live_`, non-test `whsec_`, `shpat_` locally) |

## Open-Source MCP Tools Implemented in `local_engine.mjs` (9)

| Tool Name | Domain | Local In-Process Implementation (`local_engine.mjs`) | Execution Mode |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |

| `revclamp_stage_stripe_dispute_ce3` | Visa 10.4 / CE 3.0 | Evaluates 120d–365d prior undisputed charges (`ip_subnet`/`device_id` overlap) against caller-supplied `usageEvents` (`demo: true` for sample) and stages a non-destructive `submit: false` draft (`<= 18,000` UTF-16 code units) | Local In-Process (or Optional Cloud Key) |
| `revclamp_validate_eu_vat_vies` | EU & `XI` B2B VAT | Normalizes 27 EU member states + Northern Ireland (`XI`) VAT IDs (`GR -> EL`), checks syntax locally (`FORMAT_ONLY`, `valid: null`), simulates `errorWrappers` (`demo: true`), or queries live EU VIES (`viesMode: "LIVE"` + `REVCLAMP_API_KEY`) | Local In-Process (or Optional Live VIES) |

readme.markdown: katana-markdown-linter A markdownlint-compatible Rust engine, kml CLI, formatter, safe fixer, editor server, and agent-ready MCP server. Installation | CLI Usage | Library API | Editor Integration | MCP Server --- ## What is kml `katana-markdown-linter` is a fast Markdown lint engine for technical writing, specification documents, and AI-agent-assisted documentation workflows. The project shares the KatanA visual identity, but keeps a standalone boundary: the crate, CLI, wrappers, editor server, and MCP server do not depend on KatanA Desktop. See [Markdown syntax support](docs/markdown-syntax-support.md) for the tested specification baseline, shared syntax boundaries, and safe-fix verification. ## Features - **markdownlint-compatible checks** for the active upstream rule catalog - **Safe fixes** for low-risk rule violations and explicit opt-in unsafe fixes - **Formatter mode** for layout normalization without changing author intent - **Embeddable Rust API** for applications that need linting or fixing in-process - **`kml` CLI** with JSON output, stdin support, ignore handling, and statistics - **Editor integration** through a stdio Language Server Protocol server - **MCP server** for agents and tools that need structured lint access - **Multi-channel distribution** through Cargo, GitHub Releases, npm, PyPI, and Homebrew ## Library API Use the crate directly when embedding linting into another Rust application. - `lint(content, options)` - `fix(content, options)` - `available_rules()` - `localized_available_rules(language_code)` - `implemented_rules()` - `missing_rules()` - `rule_catalog()` - `localized_rule_catalog(language_code)` - `resolve_locale_code(language_code)` - `resolve_locale_code_or(language_code, fallback)` - `localized_rule_description(rule_id, fallback_description, language_code)` - `supported_locales()` - `upstream::get_rule_documentation(rule_id, locale)` - `MarkdownLintConfig` - `MarkdownLintConfig::schema()` - `MarkdownLintConfig::to_lint_options()` `available_rules()` returns canonical English metadata. For user-facing rule catalogs, call `localized_available_rules(language_code)`, `localized_rule_catalog(language_code)`, `RuleMeta::localized_description(...)`, or `localized_rule_description(...)` so applications can pass UI language codes without reimplementing kml's fallback policy. `Locale` is `#[non_exhaustive]` from v0.6.0. Consumers that match on `Locale` should include a wildcard arm and prefer `resolve_locale_code(...)` or `resolve_locale_code_or(...)` for UI language strings. Rule descriptions and rule Markdown documentation are localized for `en`, `ja`, `zh-CN`, `zh-TW`, `ko`, `pt`, `fr`, `de`, `es`, and `it`. Minimal embedding examples are available under [`examples/`](examples/): - `embedding.rs`: string checks, file tree checks, string fixes, config loading and config-to-options conversion ## Installation ### Cargo ~~~bash cargo install katana-markdown-linter ~~~ The binary target is `kml`. Use Cargo when you want the Rust crate and CLI from the same channel. ### npm The npm package is a thin launcher that downloads the matching GitHub Release archive for `kml`, `kml-mcp`, or `kml-mcp-remote` on first use: ~~~bash npm install -g katana-markdown-linter kml version ~~~ Use `npx` for one-off runs: ~~~bash npx --yes katana-markdown-linter@0.20.1 check README.md npx --yes katana-markdown-linter@0.20.1 kml-mcp --workspace-root /absolute/path/to/workspace bunx --package katana-markdown-linter@0.20.1 kml-mcp --workspace-root /absolute/path/to/workspace ~~~ ### PyPI The PyPI package is a thin Python launcher that downloads the matching GitHub Release archive for `kml`, `kml-mcp`, or `kml-mcp-remote` on first use: ~~~bash pipx install katana-markdown-linter kml version ~~~ If you do not use `pipx`, install with your normal Python environment manager. Use `uvx` for one-off runs without installing the launcher into your active environment: ~~~bash uvx --from katana-markdown-linter==0.20.1 kml check README.md uvx --from katana-markdown-linter==0.20.1 kml-mcp --workspace-root /absolute/path/to/workspace ~~~ ### GitHub Releases Standalone `kml` archives are attached to GitHub Releases. Choose the archive that matches your Rust target triple: ~~~bash curl -LO https://github.com/HiroyukiFuruno/katana-markdown-linter/releases/download/v0.20.1/kml-v0.20.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz curl -LO https://github.com/HiroyukiFuruno/katana-markdown-linter/releases/download/v0.20.1/kml-v0.20.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz.sha256 shasum -a 256 -c kml-v0.20.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz.sha256 tar -xzf kml-v0.20.1-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz ~~~ ### Homebrew Homebrew formula publication is part of the release flow. Install with: ~~~bash brew install HiroyukiFuruno/katana/kml ~~~ ### VS Code Install the **KatanA Markdown Linter** extension from the VS Code Marketplace or sideload the local package. The extension acts as a thin wrapper around the `kml lsp` server and verifies version compatibility on startup. ~~~bash # Sideload for MVP testing cd editors/vscode npm install npm run compile code --extensionDevelopmentPath=$PWD ~~~ ### Zed Install the **KatanA Markdown Linter** extension from the Zed extension registry or sideload from the repository. # ShapelessAI

[ShapelessAI](https://shapelessai.com) runs your social presence: it drafts, schedules, and
publishes content across your connected platforms, holds your Brand Memory, and keeps standing
agents working while you sleep.

This repo is the public home of the **agent surface**: the `shapeless` CLI, the MCP server, the
Claude Code plugin, and the issue tracker. Your agent or script drives a ShapelessAI account: write
and schedule posts, create jobs and resume stuck ones, approve and publish, edit Brand Memory,
manage the standing agents.

**The documentation lives at [shapelessai.com/docs](https://shapelessai.com/docs)** - routes,
scopes, platform limits, refusal codes, one page per subject. Every page also answers raw
Markdown: append `.md` to its path (`https://shapelessai.com/docs/posts.md`) or send
`Accept: text/markdown`. An agent that wants all of it in one fetch should read
[shapelessai.com/llms-full.txt](https://shapelessai.com/llms-full.txt).

## Install

```bash
npx shapelessai --help      # one-off
npm i -g shapelessai        # keeps `shapeless` on your PATH
```

Node 20 or newer.

## Authenticate

Mint a key in the studio: **Settings -> API keys** (`/studio/api-keys`). Give it
only the scopes the caller needs - `read`, `write`, or `publish`. Only `publish`
can put content out.

```bash
shapeless login             # paste the key; we verify it and store it 0600
export SHAPELESS_API_KEY=slk_...   # or: env var, beats the stored key
```

Config lives in `~/.config/shapeless/config.json`. `SHAPELESS_BASE_URL`
overrides the API host (default `https://shapelessai.com`). `shapeless logout`
forgets the local copy; revoke the key itself in the studio.

Every command takes `--json` to print the raw API response, and `--help`.

## Post

Write it yourself and put it on the rail - now, at a time, or in the account's next free queue
slot. Needs the `publish` scope.

```bash
shapeless connections                     # the accounts and their ids
shapeless platforms                       # limits, media rules, settings schema (no key needed)

shapeless posts create --to <connectionId> --text "Shipping day."                       # now
shapeless posts create --to <connectionId> --text "..." --at 2026-09-21T09:00:00+03:00  # at a time
shapeless posts create --to <connectionId> --text "..." --queue                         # next free slot
shapeless posts create --to <connectionId> --text "..." --media k1,k2 \
  --first-comment "Link: https://..."      # LinkedIn, X, Bluesky
shapeless posts create --to <youtubeConnectionId> --text "..." --media <clip.mp4 key> \
  --title "The video title" --settings '{"privacyStatus":"unlisted"}'
```

The MCP tool is `posts_create` with the same arguments: `connectionId`, `text`, `mediaKeys`,
`title`, `scheduledAt` **or** `queue: true`, `settings`, `firstComment`. Read `platforms_list`
first for the platform's limits and its `settingsSchema`.

**Free plan**: ten posts a day on the rail, counted on the UTC day each post goes out on, so a
week planned ahead is ten a day rather than ten in total. The eleventh answers
`402 {code: "free_daily_cap", limit, day, resetsAt}`, which names the day that is full. X bills
per post, so Free posts to X once a day and without links (`402 free_x_daily_cap`, `free_x_link`);
the $9 Scheduler plan lifts the daily cap and carries 150 X posts a month, and the agent plans have
no cap. Composing, scheduling and publishing never spend credits, and Free also carries 125
credits a month for the agent team. Details:
[shapelessai.com/docs/posts](https://shapelessai.com/docs/posts).

## Jobs: durable runs

A job is a run the server keeps going whether or not you stay connected - the
right shape for agents and cron.

```bash
# Fire and forget
shapeless jobs create draft three posts about our beta launch

# Watch it live (tails the event stream, falls back to polling)
shapeless jobs create plan this week --label "Weekly plan" --budget 2.50 --watch

# Come back later
shapeless jobs list               # 200 newest; prints a cursor if older jobs exist
shapeless jobs list --before <cursor>   # the next page back
shapeless jobs show <id>          # transcript summary + outputs
shapeless jobs tail <id>          # re-attach to the live stream

# Put files on the message - the agent sees the image, not just its name
shapeless jobs create does this thumbnail work? --attach ./thumb.png --attach ./notes.md
shapeless jobs continue <id> and this one --media-key workspace-assets/<account>/logo.png

# Resume a stuck or failed run - history is rebuilt server-side
shapeless jobs continue <id> keep going, but make the second post shorter --watch

shapeless jobs stop <id>
```

## Posts: the queue

```bash
shapeless posts list --status proposed
shapeless posts show <id>
shapeless posts approve <id> <id> <id>    # proposed -> scheduled  [publish]
shapeless posts dismiss <id>
shapeless posts publish <id>              # out, now  [publish]
shapeless posts mark-posted <id> --url https://...
```

## Agents, Brand Memory, assets

```bash
shapeless agents list
shapeless agents create --name "Daily reach" --prompt "..." --days mon,thu --hours 9
shapeless agents edit <id> --status paused        # or: shapeless agents pause <id>
shapeless agents wake <id>                        # run it now  [publish]

shapeless brain ls
shapeless brain get positioning.md
shapeless brain put voice.md --file ./voice.md    # or pipe on stdin
shapeless brain import ./pitch-deck.pdf
shapeless brain export --out brain.zip

shapeless assets list
shapeless assets upload ./logo.png
shapeless connections
```

The hosted server is **`https://shapelessai.com/mcp`**. Add that URL to any host that speaks
remote MCP - Claude (Settings -> Connectors -> Add custom connector), ChatGPT (Developer mode),
Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, VS Code, Gemini CLI - and it opens a ShapelessAI tab to sign in and
allow. OAuth, no key. The steps for each host, in the vendor's words, are at

# CodeDebut MCP server

Ask your AI assistant what launched today. [CodeDebut](https://codedebut.com) is a daily launch board for new
software: makers launch, people upvote, and the #1 of each day becomes the Debut of the Day. This MCP server lets
Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code and any other MCP client search those launches, read product pages, find
alternatives and follow the daily ranking from inside a chat.

- **Endpoint:** `https://codedebut.com/api/mcp` (remote, Streamable HTTP, JSON-RPC 2.0)
- **Auth:** none. No account, no API key, no cookies.
- **Access:** read-only. All 10 tools return public data that is also on codedebut.com.
- **Setup page:** https://codedebut.com/mcp · **Server card:** https://codedebut.com/.well-known/mcp/server-card.json
- **Contact:** hello@codedebut.com

This repository holds the server's public contract: the tool catalogue it returns from `tools/list`
([`tools.json`](tools.json)), the registry manifest ([`server.json`](server.json)) and a small stdio bridge
([`index.js`](index.js)) for clients that can only start local servers. The server itself runs on codedebut.com.

## Connect

**Claude Code**

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http codedebut https://codedebut.com/api/mcp
```

Add `--scope user` to have it in every project.

**Claude.ai and Claude Desktop:** Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. Name it CodeDebut, paste the
URL and leave the OAuth fields empty.

```
https://codedebut.com/api/mcp
```

**ChatGPT:** Settings → Apps → Advanced settings → turn on Developer mode, then create an app named CodeDebut
with the same URL and no authentication.

**Cursor** (`~/.cursor/mcp.json` or `.cursor/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "codedebut": { "url": "https://codedebut.com/api/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**VS Code** (`.vscode/mcp.json`; the top-level key is `servers`)

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "codedebut": { "type": "http", "url": "https://codedebut.com/api/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Windsurf** (`~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "codedebut": { "serverUrl": "https://codedebut.com/api/mcp" }
  }
}
```

**Gemini CLI**

```sh
gemini mcp add --transport http codedebut https://codedebut.com/api/mcp
```

**OpenAI Codex** (`~/.codex/config.toml`)

```toml
[mcp_servers.codedebut]
url = "https://codedebut.com/api/mcp"
```

**Clients that only run local (stdio) servers**

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "codedebut": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://codedebut.com/api/mcp"] }
  }
}
```

Or run the bridge in this repo: `git clone https://github.com/kenil9630/codedebut-mcp && cd codedebut-mcp && npm install`,
then point your client at `node /path/to/codedebut-mcp/index.js`. `docker build -t codedebut-mcp .` builds the
same bridge as an image.

**Check it responds**

```sh
curl -s -X POST https://codedebut.com/api/mcp \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"tools/list"}'
```

## Tools

Exact schemas and annotations are in [`tools.json`](tools.json). Every tool is annotated `readOnlyHint: true`.

| Tool | What it returns | Arguments |
|---|---|---|
| `search_products` | Launches matching keywords (name, tagline, description, tags, maker) | `query`, optional `category`, `pricing`, `limit` |
| `get_product` | One product's full page: description, website, tags, pricing, platforms, maker, launch history with day ranks and upvotes, latest comments | `slug` (or exact name) |
| `find_alternatives` | Products in the same category, closest first (shared tags, then upvotes) | `product`, optional `limit` |
| `browse_category` | Top products in a category, most upvoted first | `category`, optional `pricing`, `limit` |
| `list_categories` | Categories with product counts and page links | none |
| `get_launches` | Every launch on a day, ranked by upvotes. Today's ranks are live; past days are final | optional `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, UTC) |
| `get_debut_of_the_day` | The #1 launch of a day; the latest finished day by default | optional `date` |
| `get_trending` | Most upvoted launches today, this week or this month | optional `period`, `limit` |
| `list_jobs` | Open jobs on the CodeDebut jobs board | none |
| `get_launch_options` | How to launch on CodeDebut: submit link, next free launch day, plans and prices | none |

Results carry `pageUrl` (the product's page on CodeDebut, to cite as the source) and `website` (the product's own
site). Links to products' sites carry `utm_source=codedebut.com&utm_medium=ai_assistant`, so makers can see the
visits that came from assistants.

**Paid placements are labelled.** Featured products are listed first in `search_products`, `browse_category` and
`find_alternatives` results and carry `"featured": true`. Boosted launches carry `"boosted": true`. Payment never
changes a rank or an upvote count.

## Things to ask

- "What launched on CodeDebut today?"
- "Find me an open-source uptime monitor on CodeDebut."
- "Which product was yesterday's Debut of the Day?"
- "What are the alternatives to this week's top AI launch on CodeDebut?"
- "How do I launch my app on CodeDebut, and what does Featured cost?"

## Limits

120 requests a minute per IP address. Over that, the server answers HTTP 429 with `Retry-After: 60`.
The endpoint is stateless: no sessions, and `GET` returns 405 because there is no server-to-client stream.

## Launch your product

Every product on CodeDebut gets a permanent page, and that page is what assistants find through this server.
[Submit yours](https://codedebut.com/submit), free, or see [Featured and Launch Day Boost](https://codedebut.com/pricing).

## Development

```sh
npm install
npm test        # starts the bridge over stdio and calls two tools on the live server
```

Set `CODEDEBUT_MCP_URL` to point the bridge at another endpoint, e.g. a local copy of the site.

# DechoNet MCP Server

**[dechonet.com](https://dechonet.com)** · [Remote MCP (no install)](https://dechonet.com/mcp) · [Phishing link check](https://dechonet.com/util/phishing) · [Free web tools](https://dechonet.com/util) · [HTTP API](https://dechonet.com/developers) · [Detection benchmark](https://dechonet.com/benchmark) · [Status](https://dechonet.com/status)

Domain security reconnaissance for AI agents via the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io).

**30 tools. No API key needed for non-commercial use.** Phishing/smishing link checks, exposed admin page checks (admin screens, test servers, dev tools left open), DNS, SSL/TLS, post-quantum TLS readiness, HTTP security headers, email authentication, port scan, DNS propagation, reverse DNS, ASN/BGP, RDAP/WHOIS, subdomain discovery (CT logs), lookalike/typosquat detection, OWASP-mapped observable checks, brand-impersonation exposure, go-live readiness, **MCP server checks** before you connect one, **domain change history** — what changed since the last check — **infrastructure history and pivots** (past nameservers/IPs/issuers, and other domains seen on the same rare infrastructure), and a daily **watch** you can set from the agent.

Every result comes back interpreted, not just as raw JSON: a status, the key numbers, each issue with severity and confidence, and the concrete action to take. That is what an agent needs to tell a human what to do next.

**Part of [DechoNet](https://dechonet.com).** Every tool here is also a free web tool at **[dechonet.com](https://dechonet.com)** — no sign-up — backed by error-fix [guides](https://dechonet.com/guides). This package brings the same checks to AI agents.

## Zero-install: remote endpoint

No npx, no install. Point any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP at:

```
https://dechonet.com/mcp
```

| Client | How to connect |
|---|---|
| Claude Code | `claude mcp add --transport http dechonet https://dechonet.com/mcp` |
| Claude app / Desktop | Listed in the [Claude connectors directory](https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/dechonet): Customize → Connectors, search DechoNet → Connect. Or + Add → Add custom connector with the URL (Free plan: one custom connector) |
| ChatGPT | [chatgpt.com/plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins) → + → Add custom MCP server → URL under Connection, no authentication → Create as a plugin (work/school accounts need an admin to allow custom MCP servers) |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/mcp.json`: `{"mcpServers":{"dechonet":{"url":"https://dechonet.com/mcp"}}}` |
| VS Code (Copilot) | Command Palette → **MCP: Add Server** → HTTP → `https://dechonet.com/mcp` → server ID `dechonet` → Global → Copilot Global (`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`). `.vscode/mcp.json` is deprecated. |
| Gemini CLI | `gemini mcp add --transport http dechonet https://dechonet.com/mcp` (in `settings.json` use `httpUrl`, not `url`) |
| Codex | `codex mcp add dechonet --url https://dechonet.com/mcp` |
| Windsurf | `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`: `{"mcpServers":{"dechonet":{"serverUrl":"https://dechonet.com/mcp"}}}` |
| Any stdio-only client | npm package — see Quick Start below |

Step-by-step for each client: [dechonet.com/mcp](https://dechonet.com/mcp). The remote endpoint also serves 3 curated prompts (`audit_domain`, `monitor_setup`, `investigate_changes`) and 2 reference resources.

## Quick Start (stdio, Claude Desktop)

Add to your `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dechonet": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "dechonet-mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

Config file location:
- **macOS**: `~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`
- **Windows**: `%APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json`

Restart Claude Desktop; DechoNet shows up in the chat input's tools menu. (Claude Desktop can also skip the install and add `https://dechonet.com/mcp` as a custom connector — see the table above.)

## Install

```bash
# Via npx (no install needed)
npx dechonet-mcp

# Or install globally
npm install -g dechonet-mcp
```

## Command line

The same checks work from a terminal or a CI step — no MCP client needed:

```bash
npx dechonet-mcp ssl example.com
npx dechonet-mcp email example.com --json
npx dechonet-mcp scan example.com --fail-on bad   # exit 2 when the overall grade is D or F
```

Checks: `dns`, `ssl`, `http`, `email`, `port`, `propagation`, `rdns`, `asn`, `whois`, `subdomains`, `lookalike`, `scan`, `owasp`, `golive`, `pqc`, `mcp`, `phishing`, `exposure`, `changes`, `history`, `impersonation`, `ip`, `subnet` (or any tool name below). `--json` prints the structured result, `--raw` keeps the raw data, `--port` sets the TLS port. Exit codes: 0 done, 1 the lookup failed, 2 the result reached `--fail-on` (`bad` or `warn`). With no arguments the package runs as the MCP server.

| `ssl_check` | SSL/TLS certificate, chain, expiry, HSTS, CT history, A-F grade |
| `http_security` | HTTP redirect trace + 10 security headers audit, A-F grade |
| `email_auth` | SPF, DMARC, DKIM, BIMI, MTA-STS, DANE + blacklist check |
| `port_scan` | Open TCP ports with service identification |
| `dns_propagation` | DNS propagation across 6 public resolvers |
| `reverse_dns` | PTR record + FCrDNS verification |
| `asn_lookup` | ASN/BGP network identification + abuse contact |
| `whois_lookup` | RDAP/WHOIS domain registr

readme.markdown:
# FreeApply

Free AI job applications that run on your computer. FreeApply finds jobs that fit your settings, applies through the
AI app you already use, tracks every application in a local dashboard and checks Gmail for employer replies. Any role,
any field.

**Website:** https://www.mybotsai.com · **Install:** https://www.mybotsai.com/install/ ·
**Downloads:** https://www.mybotsai.com/appserver/ · **Release notes:** [release-notes/](release-notes/README.md) · **Source:** https://github.com/FreeApply/freeapply

Current version: **1.0.6** ([notes](release-notes/1.0.6.md)). The app and its legal documents share one version
number.

## What it does
- **Finds jobs that fit**: roles, pay floor and locations from your settings, on the job sites you choose. Duplicates
  and reposts it has already tracked are skipped.
- **Applies for you** on employer sites and job boards with your real details, your résumé and answers you saved once,
  at a measured pace.
- **Never invents experience.** Cover letters and answers are checked against your résumé and settings before they
  are used.
- **Knows when to stop.** CAPTCHAs, new accounts, passwords and questions your settings don't answer go to the Issues
  tab for you.
- **Tracks everything** in a dashboard at `http://127.0.0.1:7878`, reachable only from your computer.
- **Watches for replies**: with the Gmail app password you connect in setup, new employer emails show up in the
  dashboard within about 15 minutes, and your AI app sorts them every 4 hours by default (the Gmail connector works
  too).
- **Keeps going on its own** once setup is done, while your AI app is open; Start and Stop are at the top of the
  dashboard, with what it's working on right now.

## Install
| App | How |
|---|---|
| Claude Desktop | Download [`freeapply.mcpb`](https://www.mybotsai.com/appserver/freeapply.mcpb) and double-click it, or drag it into Settings → Extensions. Nothing else to install. |
| Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf | Windows: `irm https://www.mybotsai.com/appserver/install.ps1 \| iex`macOS and Linux: `curl -fsSL https://www.mybotsai.com/appserver/install.sh \| bash`Needs Node.js 22.13 or newer. The installer checks the package's signature, then asks before adding FreeApply to each app it finds. |
| Claude Code, from this repository | `/plugin marketplace add FreeApply/freeapply`, then `/plugin install freeapply@freeapply` |
| Any other MCP app | Unpack `freeapply.mcpb` (it is a ZIP file) and add a stdio server that runs `node /path/to/freeapply/src/main.js`. |

To update, install the new version the same way. To uninstall, see https://www.mybotsai.com/install/#uninstall. Your
data in `~/.freeapply` stays until you delete that folder.

## First run
1. Restart your AI app and say **"Set up FreeApply"**. The dashboard opens.
2. Read and accept the Terms of Service and Privacy Policy there yourself (18+). Until you do, every agent tool except
   `freeapply_get_status` and `freeapply_open_dashboard` refuses to run, and the agent can never accept for you.
3. Fill in **Settings**: résumé (PDF, DOCX, TXT or MD), name and email, desired roles, minimum pay, locations, work
   authorization and the job sites you use. The agent applies nowhere until these are filled.
4. Sign in to your job sites in the browser your AI app uses, then say **"Find me jobs and apply"**.

Setup ends with that conversation applying on its own until you press Stop in the dashboard; it also checks your email
for replies every few hours and stars them, labels them, or both (your choice in Settings).

## Guarantees
- Facts about you come only from your résumé, your settings and what you tell the agent. It never invents experience.
- It never types passwords, creates accounts or solves CAPTCHAs. Those jobs are flagged for you.
- **Signed workflow.** The procedures, server instructions and hard limits ship in `agent/workflow.signed.json`,
  signed with our release key. Any edit fails verification and locks the tools until the official copy is restored.
  Pacing, duplicate checks, the pay floor and the truthfulness check are enforced in the tool code, not just asked of
  the AI.
- Your data stays on your computer, except what your data-sharing choices send. The dashboard accepts only local
  requests that carry its own header.

## Data sharing
| Choice | United States | Everywhere else, or with Global Privacy Control |
|---|---|---|
| Anonymous usage statistics | On by default, one-click opt-out | Opt-in |
| Job-market data (no name or contact details; sold only as totals covering 5+ installations) | On by default, one-click opt-out | Opt-in |
| Recruiter Talent Pool (contact details and résumé, sold to recruiters) | Opt-in | Opt-in |
| Product update emails | Opt-in | Opt-in |

The region comes from your profile country, otherwise your computer's language and time zone; unknown counts as
outside the US. In Settings → Data sharing you can preview exactly what is sent, sync now, and delete everything
already shared. Details: [Privacy Policy](https://www.mybotsai.com/legal/privacy/).

The dashboard shows one card labeled "Sponsored", chosen on your computer from a signed pack. No ad scripts, no
trackers, and no data is sent to show it.

## Dashboard
Overview, Applications, Replies, Issues and Settings, with the Terms, Privacy Policy, Disclosures and Recruiter Terms
linked in the footer. The **Needs you** tab collects what needs you, in plain words:
- **Questions**: what a form asked that your settings don't answer, each as a simple question you answer by typing,
  from a dropdown or by picking options. A question several jobs ask is shown once, and one answer goes to all of
  them; questions you already answered aren't asked again. The jobs then go back in the queue.
- **Accounts to make**: one card per sign-up page, however many jobs wait on that account, with its link and a
  **FreeApply Autofill** bookmarklet that fills your name, email, phone and location on sign-up pages. Passwords stay

readme.markdown:
# promoshot

**See it work:** [demo.md](demo.md) — technique prompts and open-ended
creative briefs, each given to a fresh agent with only the skill and the
MCP, its result beside the hand-built reference. The suite is in [demos/](demos/README.md).

  

The rendering engine behind [PromoShot](https://promoshot.app)
([App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/promoshot-app/id6770157576)),
and an open implementation of its project format. A `.promo` project is a
folder — `metadata.json` plus its media — and this workspace is everything
needed to validate, inspect, and render one to stills, image sequences, or
mp4 with mixed audio: no app attached, byte-for-byte the same compositor the
apps ship.

The design bet is that **the format is the interface**. An assistant, a
script, or a person writes `metadata.json`; the engine renders it the same
everywhere — the Mac and iOS apps (Metal + VideoToolbox), this repo's CLI,
or a headless Linux box with no GPU at all (wgpu on lavapipe, ffmpeg as a
subprocess). The format has three faces behind one truth: an authoring
subset with four validated recipes (`promo schema`), the full document
(`--full`), and a types-only JSON Schema generated from the parser's own
structs (`--types`) — and the parser the validator runs is the parser the
renderers use, so "validates" means "renders".

## Not the other PromoShot

This is the open engine (and App Store app) for **[PromoShot](https://promoshot.app)** by Alexander Garmash — a full **layer / keyframe / timeline** editor for screen recordings, video, and photos (Mac; iPhone and iPad open the same `.promo` projects).

It is **not** the similarly named App Store apps that turn screenshots into template videos (for example “PromoShot: Screenshot to Video”). If you want keyframes, masks, GPU compositing, and an open `.promo` format, you want this one: [promoshot.app](https://promoshot.app) · [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/promoshot-app/id6770157576).

## Product listing / PAD

Consumer apps: [promoshot.app](https://promoshot.app) · [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/promoshot-app/id6770157576). Software directories can ingest this PAD 4.0 file:

`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GarAlex/promoshot/main/promoshot.pad.xml`

## Crates

| Crate | What it owns |
|---|---|
| `promo-model` | The format: wire structs, migrations, palette roles, `schema.md` |
| `promo-timeline` | Timeline math: keyframes, trims, attachments, waits, validation |
| `promo-gpu` | wgpu compositing: quads, borders, letterbox, vectors, color conversion |
| `promo-text` | Caption shaping and effects (cosmic-text) |
| `promo-engine` | Preview/export orchestration, frame cache, memory governor, PCM mixer |
| `promo-media` | Decoder/encoder trait registry; ffmpeg-subprocess backend + conformance suite |
| `promo-editor` | The document's edit vocabulary: commands with undo, the wizard's arrangement, theme rules — what `promo_apply` and `promo_slideshow` are built on |
| `promo-cli` | `promo` — render a project from the command line |
| `promoshot-mcp` | MCP server over stdio, for agents |

## Build and verify

```
./check-all.sh          # fmt, clippy -D warnings, all tests, release build
```

Rendering video needs `ffmpeg` (and `ffprobe`) on PATH — frames are composited
on the GPU and piped to it raw; ffmpeg only decodes and encodes. On a headless
Linux machine, `mesa-vulkan-drivers` (lavapipe) is enough of a GPU.

### Headless Linux, no GPU

The Linux release tarball carries its own CPU renderer: a `lavapipe/` folder
(Mesa's lavapipe, its libraries and a Vulkan loader; licences in
`lavapipe/NOTICES.txt`) beside `promo`. Keep the folder next to the binary
and a machine with no Vulkan driver at all — a fresh container, or a
redeploy that dropped `mesa-vulkan-drivers` — still renders. `promo` picks,
in order: a real GPU; the system's lavapipe; the bundled lavapipe (saying so
once on stderr); SwiftShader, with a warning, since it is 10–50× slower than
lavapipe. With none of them it lists what it tried and the fix
(`sudo apt-get install -y mesa-vulkan-drivers libvulkan1`).
`PROMO_LAVAPIPE=<dir>` points at the folder elsewhere; `PROMO_LAVAPIPE=off`
never uses it. The binaries need glibc 2.39 (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13).
A machine with no fonts at all still renders: text falls back to a
built-in face (Tuffy) with a warning; install `fonts-dejavu-core` and
`fonts-liberation` for real ones.

What a CPU costs, measured on a 703-frame 1080×1920 reel with narration:

| Renderer | `promo video` |
|---|---|
| Mac GPU (Apple silicon, Metal) | 13.7 s |
| lavapipe, 8 cores | 18.9 s |
| lavapipe, 2 cores | 77 s |
| lavapipe, 1 core | 179 s |

(lavapipe in an amd64-emulated ubuntu:24.04 container; SwiftShader took
about half an hour on a comparable reel.)

`promo video` survives being killed. It encodes in segments (10 s of video
each; `--segment <s>`) into `<out>.promo-parts/` beside the output, and the
same command run again skips the finished segments and goes on from there,
saying how many it found. The segments are joined without re-encoding, the
soundtrack is mixed once for the whole range and muxed in at the join — no
edge in the sound, in sync to the sample — and the folder is removed on
success. The folder is keyed by a digest of the project's files and the
render settings, so an edited project starts over instead of reusing stale
segments. `--from/--to` take seconds (`12.5`) or frames (`375f`), to split
a long render into chunks.

promo validate <project> [--strict]     # "NOT OK" lists what will not render; --strict exits 1 on any finding
promo inspect  <project>                # canvas, layers, missing media, undefined colours
promo upsert-keyframe <project> --args '{"layer":"bg","time":2,"zoom":1.2}'

readme.markdown:
# Conference Partner — MCP server & REST API Academic **conference and journal** data for AI agents and scripts: CFP deadlines, CCF / CORE / QUALIS rankings, the **Conference Partner Index (CP-I)** — a 0–100 score we compute for every conference, including the majority that carry no external rank — acceptance-rate history, edition history, journal impact factors and special issues — served by [Conference Partner](https://www.myhuiban.com) (会伴), a conference tracker that has been maintained since 2013. Two surfaces over one dataset: | | Endpoint | For | |---|---|---| | **MCP** | `https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) | Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, any MCP client | | **REST** | `https://www.myhuiban.com/api/*` | scripts, backends, OpenAPI codegen | Both are backed by the same services and return **identical payloads** — the only difference is the protocol envelope. **Search, ranking lists and site statistics need no credentials at all.** Point a client at the URL and the first call works. ```bash curl "https://www.myhuiban.com/api/conferences?ccf_rank=A&field=ai&submission_date_start=2026-08-05" ``` --- ## Add it to your MCP client
Claude Code ```bash claude mcp add --transport http conference-partner https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp ```
Claude.ai / Claude Desktop (Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector) Remote MCP server URL: ``` https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp ``` To unlock the detail tools, add a static request header in the connector's advanced settings: `Authorization: Bearer hb_xxx` (see [Credentials](#credentials)).
Cursor — ~/.cursor/mcp.json or .cursor/mcp.json ```json { "mcpServers": { "conference-partner": { "url": "https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp" } } } ```
VS Code — .vscode/mcp.json ```json { "servers": { "conference-partner": { "type": "http", "url": "https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp" } } } ```
ChatGPT (Settings → Connectors → Create) MCP server URL `https://www.myhuiban.com/mcp`, authentication **No authentication** (or *API key* with your `hb_` key to enable the detail tools).
Ready-to-copy files for each client live in [`examples/mcp-config/`](examples/mcp-config/), and the per-client walkthrough — including how to attach a key — is in [`docs/mcp-clients.md`](docs/mcp-clients.md). Also listed on [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/server/sundou82/conference-partner), [Glama](https://glama.ai/mcp/connectors/com.myhuiban.www/conference-partner) and the [official MCP registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as `com.myhuiban.www/conference-partner`. --- ## Tools Eight read-only tools, each with a REST twin returning the same payload. | Tool | REST twin | Credentials | |---|---|---| | `search_conferences` | `GET /api/conferences` | — | | `search_journals` | `GET /api/journals` | — | | `list_conferences` | `GET /api/conferences/rankings/{ranking}` | — | | `list_journals` | `GET /api/journals/rankings/{ranking}` | — | | `get_statistics` | `GET /api/statistics` | — | | `get_conference` | `GET /api/conferences/{id}` | free account | | `get_journal` | `GET /api/journals/{id}` | free account | | `get_researcher` | `GET /api/researchers/{id}` | free account | Search accepts any combination of keyword, `ccf_rank` (A/B/C), `core_rank` (A\*/A/B/C), `qualis_rank`, `field` (research areas, CS and beyond), submission/conference date ranges and `updated_since` for incremental sync. Rank parameters take several comma-separated values matched as OR — `ccf_rank=A,B,C` is every CCF-rated venue. **Every parameter is optional** — filter-only queries such as "AI conferences with a deadline in the next 90 days" are the point. Ranking lists cover open CFPs, the three tier lists, the Conference Partner Index, popularity, lowest acceptance rate, trending, upcoming/past — and for journals, special-issue CFPs and highest impact factor. The CFP and date-ordered lists also take `field`. Every venue object carries `fields`, the research-field slugs it is tagged with, so loaded results can be narrowed further client-side. A rank field is `""` when the venue is not on that list, which for CCF is most conferences. ### Prompts The MCP server also ships **prompts** — ready-made tasks your client offers as one-click starting points, so you are not left staring at a list of tool names: | Prompt | What it does | |---|---| | `upcoming_deadlines` | deadlines you can still submit to, by field and tier | | `where_to_submit` | give it a paper topic, get ranked venues whose calls are open | | `venue_snapshot` | everything on record for one conference or journal | | `open_special_issues` | journals currently running a special-issue call | Full machine-readable definitions, refreshed from production by CI: [`spec/openapi.json`](spec/openapi.json) and [`spec/mcp-tools.json`](spec/mcp-tools.json). --- ## Credentials | Tier | How | Limit | |---|---|---| | **Anonymous** | send nothing | 50 requests/day per source IP | | **Free account** | `Authorization: Bearer hb_xxx` | 200 requests/day, shared across REST + MCP | | Paid | — | *planned, not available yet* | Create a key at [myhuiban.com/account/api-keys](https://www.myhuiban.com/account/api-keys) — it never expires and can be revoked individually, which is what you want for a client that only lets you pin a fixed request header. A JWT from `POST /api/login` works too and draws on the same pool. Every response carries `X-Quota-Limit` and `X-Quota-Remaining`. CORS is open, so browser JavaScript works. `401` = this endpoint needs a credential, or the one you sent is invalid. An unusable credential is **never** silently downgraded to the anonymous tier. `402` = account quota exhausted. `429` = anonymous per-IP quo …
