readme.markdown:
# Faxette plugins

Send a fax from Claude Code or Codex. The plugin adds Faxette's two MCP servers, one for each copy of Faxette, and a `send-a-fax` skill: your agent finds the official fax number, uploads your files and gives you a link to Faxette's status page, where you check the fax and pay to send it. You pay per fax, with no subscription. You don't need an account; if you have one, sign in when your app asks and your faxes stay in it.

Faxette faxes to the US, Canada, the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man.

## Install

Claude Code:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
claude plugin install faxette@faxette
```

Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
```

Then open `/plugins` in Codex, switch to the Faxette marketplace and install Faxette. Start a new session to use it.

Then ask, for example: "Please fax referral.pdf to Dr. Lee's office."

## Only the connectors

Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP clients can connect directly, without the skill. Each connector faxes to its own copy's countries:

| Connector | Faxes to |
| --- | --- |
| `https://mcp.faxette.com/mcp` | the US and Canada |
| `https://mcp.eu.faxette.com/mcp` | the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man |

Setup steps for each app are on [faxette.com/mcp](https://faxette.com/mcp).

## What's inside

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `plugins/faxette/skills/send-a-fax/SKILL.md` | How the agent finds the number, uploads files and hands over the status page |
| `plugins/faxette/.mcp.json` | The two MCP servers, for Claude Code |
| `plugins/faxette/mcp.json`, `plugin.json` | The same plugin in the Agent Plugins format, for Codex |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | The Claude Code marketplace |
| `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | The Codex marketplace |
| `registry/us/server.json`, `registry/eu/server.json` | Each server's entry in the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) |

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create_document` | Reserves an upload for one file (PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC, up to 20 MB) and returns a URL to PUT it to |
| `create_fax` | Creates the fax and returns its `status_url`, where the person checks it and pays |
| `get_fax_status` | Reads a fax from its `status_url`: status, pages, price, payment and attempts |
| `get_account` | Shows which Faxette account is signed in. Needs sign-in |
| `get_faxes` | Lists the account's faxes, 25 at a time, newest first, with a status filter. Needs sign-in |
| `get_fax` | One of the account's faxes, with its documents' file names and history. Needs sign-in |

Signing in is optional. The connector asks your app to sign you in the first time a tool needs it, through your copy of Faxette (`www.faxette.com` or `eu.faxette.com`). Disconnect an app any time in Settings → Connected apps.

Nothing is sent or charged from the chat. The person pays on the status page, which shows the fax number, documents and price first.

## Privacy and support

- Privacy policy: [faxette.com/legal/privacy](https://faxette.com/legal/privacy)
- Terms: [faxette.com/legal/terms](https://faxette.com/legal/terms)
- Support: [support@faxette.com](mailto:support@faxette.com)

## Publishing

Bump `version` in both `plugin.json` files when the plugin changes.

The servers are listed in the MCP Registry as `com.faxette/faxette` and `com.faxette/faxette-eu`. Bump `version` in both `registry/*/server.json` files with the server's, then publish each. The `com.faxette/*` names are proven with a DNS TXT record on `faxette.com` ([how](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/authentication.md#dns-authentication)):

```sh
mcp-publisher login dns --domain faxette.com --private-key <key>
(cd registry/us && mcp-publisher publish)
(cd registry/eu && mcp-publisher publish)
```

The key is the hex Ed25519 private key in the GooseGods Cloudflare Secrets Store, `faxette-MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY`. To replace it, make a new key and swap the `v=MCPv1` TXT record on `faxette.com` for the new public key:

```sh
openssl genpkey -algorithm Ed25519 -out key.pem
echo "v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=$(openssl pkey -in key.pem -pubout -outform DER | tail -c 32 | base64)"  # the TXT record
openssl pkey -in key.pem -outform DER | tail -c 32 | xxd -p -c 64                                  # the hex key for login
```

readme.markdown:
# Faxette plugins

Send a fax from Claude Code or Codex. The plugin adds Faxette's two MCP servers, one for each copy of Faxette, and a `send-a-fax` skill: your agent finds the official fax number, uploads your files and gives you a link to Faxette's status page, where you check the fax and pay to send it. You pay per fax, with no subscription. You don't need an account; if you have one, sign in when your app asks and your faxes stay in it.

Faxette faxes to the US, Canada, the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man.

## Install

Claude Code:

```sh
claude plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
claude plugin install faxette@faxette
```

Codex:

```sh
codex plugin marketplace add goosegods/faxette-plugins
```

Then open `/plugins` in Codex, switch to the Faxette marketplace and install Faxette. Start a new session to use it.

Then ask, for example: "Please fax referral.pdf to Dr. Lee's office."

## Only the connectors

Claude, ChatGPT and other MCP clients can connect directly, without the skill. Each connector faxes to its own copy's countries:

| Connector | Faxes to |
| --- | --- |
| `https://mcp.faxette.com/mcp` | the US and Canada |
| `https://mcp.eu.faxette.com/mcp` | the EU, the UK, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Monaco, Montenegro, Ukraine and the Isle of Man |

Setup steps for each app are on [faxette.com/mcp](https://faxette.com/mcp).

## What's inside

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `plugins/faxette/skills/send-a-fax/SKILL.md` | How the agent finds the number, uploads files and hands over the status page |
| `plugins/faxette/.mcp.json` | The two MCP servers, for Claude Code |
| `plugins/faxette/mcp.json`, `plugin.json` | The same plugin in the Agent Plugins format, for Codex |
| `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` | The Claude Code marketplace |
| `.agents/plugins/marketplace.json` | The Codex marketplace |
| `registry/us/server.json`, `registry/eu/server.json` | Each server's entry in the [MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) |

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `create_document` | Reserves an upload for one file (PDF, JPG, PNG, WEBP or HEIC, up to 20 MB) and returns a URL to PUT it to |
| `create_fax` | Creates the fax and returns its `status_url`, where the person checks it and pays |
| `get_fax_status` | Reads a fax from its `status_url`: status, pages, price, payment and attempts |
| `get_account` | Shows which Faxette account is signed in. Needs sign-in |
| `get_faxes` | Lists the account's faxes, 25 at a time, newest first, with a status filter. Needs sign-in |
| `get_fax` | One of the account's faxes, with its documents' file names and history. Needs sign-in |

Signing in is optional. The connector asks your app to sign you in the first time a tool needs it, through your copy of Faxette (`www.faxette.com` or `eu.faxette.com`). Disconnect an app any time in Settings → Connected apps.

Nothing is sent or charged from the chat. The person pays on the status page, which shows the fax number, documents and price first.

## Privacy and support

- Privacy policy: [faxette.com/legal/privacy](https://faxette.com/legal/privacy)
- Terms: [faxette.com/legal/terms](https://faxette.com/legal/terms)
- Support: [support@faxette.com](mailto:support@faxette.com)

## Publishing

Bump `version` in both `plugin.json` files when the plugin changes.

The servers are listed in the MCP Registry as `com.faxette/faxette` and `com.faxette/faxette-eu`. Bump `version` in both `registry/*/server.json` files with the server's, then publish each. The `com.faxette/*` names are proven with a DNS TXT record on `faxette.com` ([how](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/registry/authentication.md#dns-authentication)):

```sh
mcp-publisher login dns --domain faxette.com --private-key <key>
(cd registry/us && mcp-publisher publish)
(cd registry/eu && mcp-publisher publish)
```

The key is the hex Ed25519 private key in the GooseGods Cloudflare Secrets Store, `faxette-MCP_REGISTRY_PRIVATE_KEY`. To replace it, make a new key and swap the `v=MCPv1` TXT record on `faxette.com` for the new public key:

```sh
openssl genpkey -algorithm Ed25519 -out key.pem
echo "v=MCPv1; k=ed25519; p=$(openssl pkey -in key.pem -pubout -outform DER | tail -c 32 | base64)"  # the TXT record
openssl pkey -in key.pem -outform DER | tail -c 32 | xxd -p -c 64                                  # the hex key for login
```

## License

MIT

readme.markdown:
# QuasarUI MCP Server

Let your AI assistant find [QuasarUI](https://www.quasarui.com) Components for [Quasar Framework](https://quasar.dev) (Vue) and paste their source into your project.

Ask for "a pricing table with a monthly and yearly toggle" and your assistant searches the catalogue, picks a matching Component and pastes its code.

- **Without a key:** every Free Component. No account needed.
- **With an Access Key:** every Paid Component too, if your account holds All Access or Blocks Pro. [Create a key](https://www.quasarui.com/dashboard).

The server is hosted at `https://www.quasarui.com/mcp`. New Components appear there as soon as they are published; nothing here needs updating.

## Connect your client

Replace `YOUR_ACCESS_KEY` with your key, or leave the key out for Free Components only.

### Claude Code

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http quasarui https://www.quasarui.com/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_KEY"
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or `.cursor/mcp.json` in a project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "quasarui": {
      "url": "https://www.quasarui.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Claude Desktop and other stdio clients

Clients that only start local servers can use this package, which forwards to the hosted server:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "quasarui": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "quasarui-mcp"],
      "env": { "QUASARUI_ACCESS_KEY": "YOUR_ACCESS_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Docker

```sh
docker build -t quasarui-mcp .
docker run -i --rm -e QUASARUI_ACCESS_KEY=YOUR_ACCESS_KEY quasarui-mcp
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `list_blocks` | Lists every Block with its Component counts |
| `list_components` | Lists the Components in a Block, each marked free or paid |
| `search_components` | Finds Components by what they are, such as "login form" or "sidebar" |
| `get_component` | Returns a Component's source |
| `get_setup_guide` | Explains how to set up a project and paste a Component |

Without access, asking for a Paid Component returns its preview link and how to unlock it, never its code.

## Limits and errors

- Each IP address can make 60 requests a minute, and so can each Access Key. Past that the server answers 429 for a short while.
- A wrong, revoked or malformed key gets **401**. The server never falls back to Free Components for a bad key.

## License

The code in this repository is MIT. Components returned by the server are covered by the [QuasarUI license](https://www.quasarui.com/documentation/licensing).

readme.markdown:
# mifit

Read your own Mi Fitness (小米运动健康) data from the Xiaomi cloud: a small
Python library, a command-line tool and an MCP server for AI assistants.

The Mi Fitness app syncs your steps, heart rate, sleep and more to the Xiaomi
cloud, but Xiaomi offers no public API for individuals. mifit signs in to your
own account by QR code, reads that synced data and returns it as JSON or as
Python objects, so you can build on it.

> **Unofficial.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by or supported by Xiaomi.
> See [Disclaimer](https://github.com/Jenwein/mifit#disclaimer).

## What it reads today

| Domain | What you get | `records` type | Checked against the app |
|---|---|---|---|
| `steps` | steps and distance per day | `StepRecord` | yes |
| `heart_rate` | raw heart-rate samples | `HeartRatePoint` | yes |
| `heart_rate_daily` | heart rate per day: average, maximum, minimum, resting | `HeartRateDailySummary` | yes |
| `consumption` | calories per day: resting, active, intake, total | `ConsumptionRecord` | yes |
| `sleep` | sleep per day: totals, stage minutes, sessions with their stage timeline | `SleepRecord` → `SleepSession` → `SleepStage` | yes; the sleep score could not be checked and is in `raw` only |
| `workouts` | one entry per workout: start and end, sport, duration, distance, active and total calories, average and maximum heart rate, steps | `Workout` | yes |
| `workout_detail` | per workout (outdoor runs and rides): per-second samples (heart rate, cumulative distance and steps, cadence, pace or speed) and the GPS track | `WorkoutDetail` → `WorkoutSample` / `TrackPoint` | yes (one outdoor run, one ride); altitude is in `raw` only: the run's was a few metres off the app's |
| `spo2_daily` | blood oxygen (SpO2) per day: average, maximum, minimum | `Spo2DailySummary` | yes |
| `spo2` | raw SpO2 readings | `Spo2Point` | yes |
| `stress_daily` | stress level per day: average, highest, lowest, and minutes in each stress band (relaxed, mild, moderate, severe) | `StressDailySummary` | yes |
| `activity_daily` | activity per day, as on the app's 活力指标 page: activity count (活动次数), activity minutes (活动时长), active calories (卡路里) | `ActivityDailySummary` | yes |
| `weight` | weight entries: time, weight, BMI (body composition in `raw` only) | `WeightRecord` | yes; body composition could not be checked and is in `raw` only |
| `profile` (its own command: `mifit profile`) | height, weight, daily step, calorie and activity-time goals | `UserProfile` | yes |
| `raw` (CLI: `mifit raw`; Python: `client.raw`, `raw_window`, `daily_report`) | the rows of any fitness-data or daily-report key, as the service sends them | none: the service's rows, uninterpreted | not applicable: nothing is interpreted |

"Checked against the app" means the values were compared with what the Mi
Fitness app shows, on one real account (China region, UTC+8). More is
planned. Meanwhile, `mifit raw` (in Python `raw_window` and `daily_report`)
returns the rows of any other key of the fitness-data or (with `--daily`)
daily-report endpoint, uninterpreted.

What changed in each version, breaking changes included, is in
[CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/Jenwein/mifit/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md).

## Install

Requires Python 3.12 or later; `uv` installs one for you if needed.

```bash
uv tool install mifit     # recommended: its own environment, `mifit` on your PATH
pipx install mifit        # the same, with pipx
pip install mifit         # into the current environment, to use it as a library
```

Upgrade: `uv tool upgrade mifit` (or `pipx upgrade mifit`, `pip install -U mifit`).

## Log in

```bash
mifit login
```

A QR code is drawn in the terminal, with the login URL below it. Scan it with
the Xiaomi / Mi Fitness app on your phone (or open the URL) and approve the
sign-in. Your password never passes through mifit.

The session is saved to `~/.mifit/session.json` (on Windows
`%USERPROFILE%\.mifit\session.json`). It grants access to your Mi Fitness
account's health data (not only reading). It also holds your account's
passToken, which mifit uses to renew the session when it expires. The passToken
is account-level: it can obtain tokens for any Xiaomi service, so the file
grants access to your whole Xiaomi account, not just your Mi Fitness health
data, and it stays useful long after the session token itself has expired.
Treat it like a password, and do not share it or commit it. On Linux and macOS
the file is readable by you only; on Windows it relies on your user profile's
permissions.

If Xiaomi asks for an extra security confirmation, `mifit login` prints a URL:
open it, confirm, then run `mifit login` again.

## Use with an AI assistant (MCP)

`mifit mcp` is a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)
server: AI assistants such as Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor and VS Code
start it on your computer and read your Mi Fitness data when you ask them about
it ("how did I sleep last week?").

**What leaves your computer.** The results of the tools the assistant calls are
sent to the assistant's model provider, like the rest of the conversation. The
login stays in `~/.mifit` on this computer: the server runs locally on
stdin/stdout, opens no network port, never puts a credential in a result, and
only reads your health data (the login tools save the new session to
`~/.mifit`). GPS tracks are off: the server gives a workout's route only when it
was started with `--allow-gps` (in the Claude Desktop extension: when its
**Allow GPS tracks** switch is on) *and* the assistant asks for it, and a route
shows where you were, including where you live. (To serve assistants on other
machines instead, see [Remote access (HTTP)](https://github.com/Jenwein/mifit#remote-access-http):
that server does open a port.)

**Log in once**, in a terminal:

```bash
uvx mifit login
```

(or `mifit login` after `uv tool install mifit`). Without a terminal, ask the
assistant to log you in: it calls `login_start`, which returns the QR code to
scan with the Xi

# Noonlaunch MCP server

Launch your product on [Noonlaunch](https://noonlaunch.com) without leaving your editor, and let your agent browse the Noonlaunch directory, the weekly launch winners and a curated list of 333 places to launch a startup.

Noonlaunch is a product launch platform and directory. Makers launch products, the community votes, and the top 3 each week win a badge and a dofollow backlink.

- **Endpoint:** `https://noonlaunch.com/mcp`
- **Transport:** Streamable HTTP
- **Auth:** none. No API key and no account needed to connect.
- **Registry name:** `com.noonlaunch/mcp`
- **Docs:** https://noonlaunch.com/launch-with-ai

This repository holds the public listing files for the hosted server (`server.json`, logo and setup docs). The server itself runs at noonlaunch.com.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| `search-directory` | Search the product directory, ordered by community votes | Read |
| `get-product` | Full public details of one product by its slug | Read |
| `get-weekly-winners` | A week's launch board, with the top 3 marked as winners | Read |
| `list-launch-directories` | 333 startup launch directories, filterable by category, cost and domain authority | Read |
| `get-plans` | What launching costs and what each plan includes | Read |
| `check-product` | Whether a site can be submitted, plus its plans, categories and launch weeks | Read |
| `submit-product` | Submit a product. Nothing is published until the maker opens a private claim link | Write |
| `verify-badge` | Check the Noonlaunch badge is live on the site and publish a free launch | Write |
| `check-status` | Where a submission stands: claimed, paid, verified, published | Read |
| `report-badge-problem` | Ask a person to review a badge check that keeps failing | Write |

Every tool carries `readOnlyHint`, `destructiveHint`, `idempotentHint` and `openWorldHint` annotations. No tool deletes anything.

## How submitting works

1. Your agent asks for your live website URL (never localhost) and calls `check-product`.
2. It drafts the name, tagline and description, shows them to you, and asks which plan you want.
3. `submit-product` returns a private, single-use claim link. You open it and sign in with Google to confirm the listing. Nothing goes public before that.
4. Free launches: the agent adds the badge to your footer, you deploy, and `verify-badge` publishes the listing. Paid launches are published by the payment provider, and the agent can only report what `check-status` says.

## Connect

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http noonlaunch https://noonlaunch.com/mcp
```

### Claude (claude.ai and Claude Desktop)

Settings, Connectors, Add custom connector, then paste `https://noonlaunch.com/mcp`.

### Cursor

`~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "noonlaunch": {
      "url": "https://noonlaunch.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### VS Code

`.vscode/mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "noonlaunch": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://noonlaunch.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

```bash
codex mcp add noonlaunch --url https://noonlaunch.com/mcp
```

### Any other client

Point it at `https://noonlaunch.com/mcp` over Streamable HTTP. For clients that only speak stdio:

```bash
npx -y mcp-remote https://noonlaunch.com/mcp
```

## Example prompts

- "Launch this project on Noonlaunch."
- "Who won on Noonlaunch last week?"
- "Find free launch directories with a domain authority above 50."
- "How much does it cost to launch on Noonlaunch?"

## Limits

60 requests per minute per client.

## Privacy and terms

- Privacy policy: https://noonlaunch.com/privacy-policy
- Terms: https://noonlaunch.com/terms

## Support

Open an issue on this repository, or email support@noonlaunch.com.

## License

The files in this repository are MIT licensed. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).

# YouTube Transcript MCP Server

> Give Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code and any MCP client the ability to read **YouTube transcripts**. Hosted, nothing to install. Free API key: 10 requests a day.

A hosted [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server that exposes one tool, `get_youtube_transcript`, backed by [youtube-transcript.ai](https://youtube-transcript.ai). Paste a YouTube link mid-conversation and your AI reads the full transcript on demand.

**Connector URL:**

```
https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY
```

Replace `YOUR_KEY` with your API key. [Create a free key](https://youtube-transcript.ai/get-api-key) with a Google sign-in; it takes about a minute.

---

## Why

- **Free to start.** A free key covers 10 transcripts a day. Pro is 1,000 a day for $120 a year, on the same key.
- **Reliable.** A hardened fetch pipeline with proxy fallback returns transcripts even on videos that block typical scrapers.
- **Any language.** Pick a caption track by language code (`en`, `zh-CN`, `es`, `ja`, …) or let it choose the default.
- **Built for agents.** One tool, plain-text output with title and metadata. Multi-hour videos come back in parts, so nothing gets cut off.

## Authentication

Tool calls need an API key. There is no OAuth. Send the key in one of two ways:

| Where | Example |
|-------|---------|
| Header | `Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY` |
| URL | `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` |

The URL form is for clients that only accept a connector URL.

## Quick start

### Claude (web / desktop)

Settings → **Connectors** → **Add custom connector**

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Name  | `youtube-transcript.ai` |
| URL   | `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` |

Then ask: *“Summarize this video: https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ”*

### ChatGPT

In the custom connector / MCP server setup, add an MCP server with URL `https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY` (transport: **Streamable HTTP**), enable it for your chat, then paste a YouTube link.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user youtube-transcript \
  https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer YOUR_KEY"
```

### Cursor

Add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` inside one project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "youtube-transcript": {
      "url": "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Codex

Add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```toml
[mcp_servers.youtube-transcript]
url = "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp"
http_headers = { "Authorization" = "Bearer YOUR_KEY" }
```

### Clients that only launch local servers

For clients that start MCP servers from a config file and cannot take a remote URL, bridge with [`mcp-remote`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/mcp-remote):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "youtube-transcript": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote", "https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp?key=YOUR_KEY"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Let your agent do it

Paste [`https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp.md`](https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp.md) into a coding agent. It is a plain-text version of these instructions, written for an AI to follow.

## Tool reference

### `get_youtube_transcript`

Fetch the full text transcript of a YouTube video.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| `video`   | string | yes | YouTube URL (watch, `youtu.be`, shorts, embed) or a bare 11-character video ID |
| `lang`    | string | no  | Caption language code, e.g. `en`, `zh-CN`, `es`. Omit for the default track |
| `offset`  | integer | no | Where to continue a long transcript. Use the value given at the end of the previous part |

Returns plain text: the transcript with title, duration, and a list of available languages. Transcripts over 120,000 characters come back in parts; each part ends with a note giving the `offset` for the next call.

## Example prompts

- “Summarize the key points of `<link>` in 5 bullets.”
- “Pull the transcript of this video and translate it to Spanish.”
- “What does the speaker say about pricing in `<link>`? Quote the exact lines.”

## Programmatic use

The server speaks standard MCP over Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC). A zero-dependency example is in [`examples/quickstart.mjs`](examples/quickstart.mjs):

```bash
YT_TRANSCRIPT_KEY=YOUR_KEY node examples/quickstart.mjs https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ
```

Calling from your own code without MCP? There is a plain HTTP endpoint too: see the [YouTube Transcript API](https://youtube-transcript.ai/api).

## Limits

- Free: 10 requests a day. Pro: 1,000 a day for $120 a year. Upgrade from the [key page](https://youtube-transcript.ai/get-api-key).
- Every tool call counts as one request, including each part of a long transcript. The count resets at 00:00 UTC.
- The video needs captions, either written by the uploader or auto-generated by YouTube.

## Notes

- **Not affiliated** with YouTube or Google. Transcripts are fetched from publicly available captions.
- Listed in the official MCP Registry as `ai.youtube-transcript/youtube-transcript`.

## Links

- Web tool (no AI client needed): https://youtube-transcript.ai
- Connector landing page: https://youtube-transcript.ai/mcp
- HTTP API: https://youtube-transcript.ai/api

## License

MIT

# app-console-mcp

**Google Play Console, App Store Connect and AdMob from your terminal or from Claude — no browser.**

[Español](README.es.md)

Driving store consoles through a browser agent burns tokens on screenshots and page snapshots and breaks
whenever the UI changes. This project talks to the official APIs instead and answers in a few lines of plain
text. Every tool exists twice, with identical output:

- as an **MCP tool** for Claude Code, Claude Desktop or any MCP client, and
- as a **CLI command** (`appconsole ...`) for you, your scripts and CI.

It ships as three Claude Code plugins (Google Play, App Store Connect, AdMob), each with its MCP server and a
skill that teaches Claude the safe workflows. It also comes built into
[Alchemist Coder](https://github.com/Alekla0126/alchemist-coder), the open-source desktop app for Claude Code and
Codex: every agent there gets these tools for the services you have set up.

```text
$ appconsole play vitals com.example.app
com.example.app (data up to 2026-10-19):
crash: 0.31% 28-day user-perceived (ok, threshold 1.09%)
  newest versions (last 28 d): v42 0.12% (35% of users) · v41 0.44% (60% of users)
anr: 0.52% 28-day user-perceived (ABOVE THRESHOLD, threshold 0.47%)
  newest versions (last 28 d): v42 0.21% (35% of users) · v41 0.70% (60% of users)

$ appconsole admob report --days 7 --by format --currency USD
AdMob 2026-10-20 to 2026-10-26 by format: 128.40 USD (+9% vs previous 7 d: 117.80), 61210 impressions
  interstitial: 71.10 USD, 9340 impr, eCPM 7.61, match 88%, show 31%
  banner: 39.75 USD, 47880 impr, eCPM 0.83, match 95%, show 52%
```

## What it can do

| Google Play (`play`) | App Store Connect (`appstore`) | AdMob (`admob`) |
|---|---|---|
| `apps` list apps the key can see | `apps` list apps | `accounts` publisher accounts |
| `listing` / `update-listing` title, short, full description, new languages | `listing` / `update-listing` name, subtitle, keywords, description, promo text, what's new | `apps` apps and ad unit ids |
| `tracks` releases per track | `versions` versions and review state | `report` earnings, eCPM, match/show rate, CTR by app, ad unit, country, format, app/SDK/OS version, why ads are limited, ad source or mediation group, vs. previous period |
| `upload` .aab/.apk to any track (staged or draft) | `create-version` new editable version | `campaign-report` promotion campaigns: installs, cost, CPI |
| `promote` between tracks | `builds` processing state, export compliance | `ad-sources` networks and their adapters' settings |
| `rollout` change %, complete, halt, resume | `submit` attach build + submit to App Review | `mediation-groups` / `ad-unit-mappings` ✱ |
| `reviews` / `reply` | `release` release an approved manual-release version | `create-app` / `create-ad-unit` ✱ |
| `vitals` crash and ANR rates (Google's 28-day numbers) | `reviews` / `reply` | `map-ad-unit` / `create-mediation-group` / `update-mediation-group` ✱ |
| `products` subscriptions, base plans, prices | `sales` downloads, IAP units, proceeds per app | `ab-experiment` start or stop a mediation A/B test ✱ |
| `search-rank` public search position | `search-rank` public search position | |
| `images` / `upload-images` screenshots and graphics | `screenshots` / `upload-screenshots` per device and locale | |
| `users` / `grant` / `revoke` users, service accounts and app permissions | `products` subscriptions and in-app purchases | |
| `data-safety` send the Data safety form (CSV) | | |

✱ AdMob's limited access: Google has to enable your publisher id for these methods (ask your AdMob account manager or AdMob support) and the token needs the `admob.monetization` scope (`appconsole admob login --monetization`). Until then they explain what to ask for.

**Safe by default.** Every tool that changes something is a dry run unless you pass `confirm=true`
(`--confirm` in the CLI). Google Play dry runs build the change in a draft edit and let Google validate it
before discarding it, so you see real errors before anything is published. MCP tools carry
`readOnlyHint`/`destructiveHint` annotations so clients can auto-approve reads and ask before writes.

## Install

You need [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/) (it fetches Python and the dependencies).

### Claude Code plugins (recommended)

```text
/plugin marketplace add Alekla0126/app-console-mcp
/plugin install google-play@app-console
/plugin install app-store-connect@app-console
/plugin install admob@app-console
```

Install only the ones you use. Each plugin asks for its credentials (paths and ids; you can leave them empty and
use `appconsole config` instead), adds its MCP server and skill, and puts `appconsole` on the PATH of Claude's
Bash tool.

### Any MCP client (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Codex, VS Code…)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "google-play": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "git+https://github.com/Alekla0126/app-console-mcp", "appconsole", "mcp", "play"],
      "env": { "GOOGLE_PLAY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT": "/path/to/service-account.json" }
    },
    "app-store-connect": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "git+https://github.com/Alekla0126/app-console-mcp", "appconsole", "mcp", "appstore"]
    },
    "admob": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--from", "git+https://github.com/Alekla0126/app-console-mcp", "appconsole", "mcp", "admob"]
    }
  }
}
```

`appconsole mcp all` serves the three services as a single server, for clients that take only one.

Or with the Claude Code CLI:
`claude mcp add google-play -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/Alekla0126/app-console-mcp appconsole mcp play`

### CLI only

```bash
uv tool install git+https://github.com/Alekla0126/app-console-mcp
appconsole --help
appconsole play reviews com.example.app --unanswered-only
```

# LMCP — Context and Actions for Your AI

**Give your AI the context to get things done.** LMCP connects compatible assistants to your apps and accounts through the Model Context Protocol (MCP). Bring together relevant information from email, messages, calendars and files, then use tools to turn that context into useful action — with less searching and copying between apps.

Use it with **Claude, ChatGPT, Codex, Cursor** and other compatible MCP clients. Available integrations and connection methods vary by assistant, platform and permissions.

**[Download for Mac or Windows →](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases)** · **[Explore the product](https://www.local-mcp.com/en#explore)** · **[Setup guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)**

This repository contains release information, documentation and the npm wrapper. The core binary is proprietary; documentation and scripts have their own license — see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

## More than one app's view of your information

An email, a message and a document may each contain only part of the answer. With compatible tools and access you authorize, your assistant can find those pieces across apps and accounts and use them together.

| What you ask | How connected context helps |
|---|---|
| “Tell me everything I still owe the architect — I can't remember her name.” | Search relevant messages, email and files to identify the person and assemble outstanding requests with their sources. |
| “Help organize my day so I can meet my commitments.” | Combine calendar events, tasks and relevant messages to propose a realistic plan and make supported updates when authorized. |
| “Prepare replies to customer orders using the inventory and plan dispatch.” | Read accessible order and inventory information, draft replies and use supported scheduling tools. Review proposed actions before authorizing execution. |

These illustrate workflows an assistant can build from available tools, not guaranteed autonomous outcomes. Sources must be accessible; assistant capabilities and each tool's permissions still apply.

## Apps and tools

Explore email, calendars, contacts, messages, tasks, files, documents, browser automation and other integrations. Examples include Apple Mail, Outlook, Microsoft Teams, Slack, WhatsApp, Signal, Google Drive, OneDrive, Microsoft 365, Notes, Reminders, Microsoft To Do, OmniFocus, Notion and ServiceNow.

**Not every integration is available on both operating systems.** Apple-native tools require macOS; connected services may need their own sign-in or permissions. Some tools use locally cached or synced data rather than a complete cloud account.

For current tools, requirements and platform coverage, use the **[tool reference](https://www.local-mcp.com/tools)** and **[guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)** rather than a fixed count in this README.

## Install and connect

1. **[Download LMCP for your operating system](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases).** Follow the installer and onboarding steps.
2. Select your assistant and enable the compatible integrations you want to use.
3. Grant required permissions or sign in where needed, then follow the assistant-specific setup guide.

### Cursor plugin

This repository is also a Cursor plugin. It adds the `local-mcp` MCP server, a rule that tells Cursor's agent when to use LMCP, and skills for email, calendar, messages, files and Office.

LMCP must be installed first (step 1 above): the plugin starts the LMCP server on your computer and does not work without it.

Supports **macOS 13+** and **Windows 10+ (64-bit)**.

Choose one installation path:

- **Signed installer** for Mac (`.pkg`) or Windows: **[download page](https://www.local-mcp.com/download?ref=github-releases)**.
- **macOS terminal:** `curl -fsSL 'https://www.local-mcp.com/install?ref=github-releases' | bash`
- **Windows PowerShell:** `irm https://www.local-mcp.com/install-windows?ref=github-releases | iex` (per-user, no administrator rights or Node.js needed).
- **Claude Desktop extension:** one-click `.mcpb` at **[www.local-mcp.com/install/mcpb](https://www.local-mcp.com/install/mcpb)**.
- **npm (requires Node.js):** `npx -y local-mcp@latest setup` configures the compatible clients it detects.

Details for agents and each path: **[llms-install.md](llms-install.md)**. After installing, fully restart your AI client; MCP tools load at startup.

Local desktop/CLI clients and web assistants connect differently. The installer configures the compatible local clients it detects. Web assistants (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, Grok, Perplexity) connect through **`https://www.local-mcp.com/mcp`** as a custom connector with OAuth. They need the local app installed and Cloud Data Forwarding enabled in LMCP (off by default); with forwarding off, the connector exposes only `setup_install`. Follow the **[web AI guide](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides/web-ai)** and the **[current guides](https://www.local-mcp.com/guides)**.

An endpoint alone is not a verified connection: complete authorization and check that tools are available in your client.

# BLACK**V**EIL DNS

**Know where you stand.**

Source-available DNS & email security scanner for Claude, Cursor, VS Code, and MCP clients across Streamable HTTP, stdio, and legacy HTTP+SSE.

---

## Try it in 30 seconds

**Claude Desktop** (one-click install):

Download the [Blackveil DNS extension](https://github.com/MadaBurns/bv-claude-dns/releases/latest/download/bv-claude-dns.mcpb) and open it — the current 81-tool surface is available instantly. [Verify your download](https://blackveilsecurity.com/extensions/claude-dns#install).

**Claude Code** (one command):

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http blackveil-dns https://dns-mcp.blackveilsecurity.com/mcp
```

Then ask: `scan anthropic.com`

**Smithery** (one command):

```bash
smithery mcp add MadaBurns/bv-mcp
```

**Verify the endpoint is live:**

```bash
curl https://dns-mcp.blackveilsecurity.com/health
```

No install. No API key. One URL for hosted HTTP:

```
Endpoint   https://dns-mcp.blackveilsecurity.com/mcp
Transport  Streamable HTTP · JSON-RPC 2.0
Auth       None required
```

Transport support:

- `Streamable HTTP`: `POST /mcp`, `GET /mcp`, `DELETE /mcp`
- `Native stdio`: `blackveil-dns-mcp` CLI from the `blackveil-dns` npm package
- `Legacy HTTP+SSE`: `GET /mcp/sse` bootstrap stream plus `POST /mcp/messages?sessionId=...`

For Streamable HTTP, clients should retain the `Mcp-Session-Id` returned by `initialize` and send it on every subsequent request, including notifications. Send the negotiated version in `MCP-Protocol-Version`; unsupported values are rejected with HTTP `400`, while expired or terminated sessions return `404` and require a fresh `initialize`.

---

## What you get

- **81 MCP tools with 19 scoring categories** — SPF, DMARC, DKIM, DNSSEC, SSL/TLS, MTA-STS, NS, CAA, MX, BIMI, TLS-RPT, subdomain takeover, HTTP security headers, DANE, SVCB/HTTPS, DANE-HTTPS, subdomailing, reverse DNS (PTR/FCrDNS), and DNSKEY strength
- **Maturity staging** — Stage 0-4 classification (Unprotected to Hardened) with score-based capping to prevent inflated labels
- **Trust surface analysis** — detects shared SaaS senders in SPF, both cataloged platforms (Google, M365, SendGrid) and uncataloged hosts identifiable by their `spf` delegation label, then cross-references DMARC enforcement to determine real exposure
- **Guided remediation** — `generate` (artifact=`fix_plan`) produces provider-aware prioritized actions; its record artifacts (`spf_record`, `dmarc_record`, `dkim_config`, `mta_sts_policy`, `rollout_plan`) output ready-to-publish records; `validate_fix` confirms whether a fix was applied successfully
- **Supply chain mapping** — `map_supply_chain` correlates DNS signals to build a full third-party dependency graph with trust levels and risk signals
- **Attack path simulation** — `simulate_attack_paths` enumerates specific paths (spoofing, takeover, hijack) with severity, steps, and mitigations
- **Compliance mapping** — `map_compliance` maps scan findings to NIST 800-177, PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2, and CIS Controls
- **Self-tuning scoring** — adaptive weights adjust category importance based on patterns seen across scans via Durable Object telemetry
- **Per-tier analytics** — usage tracking by auth tier with operator API for tier summaries, key-level usage, and daily digests
- **Read-only** — checks never modify a target and need no authorization from it. Most are passive lookups over public Cloudflare DNS-over-HTTPS; `check_authoritative_dns_infra` and `check_root_server_set` query authoritative and root nameservers directly over TCP/53, and for authenticated callers `check_authoritative_dns_infra` also tests whether a domain's nameservers refuse a zone transfer (no zone data is retrieved)

# ViaFrei

### The German Real-Time Mobility Context Platform for AI

**ViaFrei gives AI assistants real-time awareness of Germany.** Trains and buses,
traffic and roadworks, fuel, charging, parking and weather. One MCP. No API key. No sign-up.

**Ask in plain words. Get the live answer, with its source.**

**[viafrei.de](https://viafrei.de/en)** · [Connect your assistant](https://viafrei.de/en/connect) · [For developers](https://viafrei.de/en/developers) · [For businesses](https://viafrei.de/en/business) · [All tools](#-everything-it-can-do) · [API reference](API.md)

---

```
claude mcp add --transport http viafrei https://mcp.viafrei.de/mcp
```

**Free. No account, no API key, no sign-up.** One line and your assistant knows
whether the A8 is jammed, whether your train, bus or tram is late, where the
nearest fast charger is (and whether it is free, where the operator publishes
that), which hydrogen station takes a lorry, whether the lift at your station
works and whether the road ahead is forecast to freeze — from official German open data, live, with the source named
in every answer. And every German motorway has a [live page of its own](#-motorway-pages)
on viafrei.de, with a map and a traffic light.

> **Beta.** ViaFrei is being stabilised: sources are still being added, and
> answers and coverage can change. The answers are written by an AI assistant
> from our data, and AI can make mistakes, so check anything important (a
> closure, a departure, a price) against the source each answer names.

> **New since server 2.4.3 (server 2.4.4 to 2.4.9): live times for buses, trams and
> the U-Bahn in fourteen more regions, a traffic light and a street map for every
> place, a site search that finds a shop or a house number, and station pages that
> load in place.**
>
> - **Live departures in fourteen more regions.** DELFI's fourteen regional SIRI ET
>   feeds (Berlin-Brandenburg, Bayern, Hessen, Rhein-Ruhr, Baden-Württemberg,
>   Bremen/Niedersachsen/Hamburg/Rostock-VVW, Oberelbe, Rhein-Neckar-Dreieck, Rhein-Sieg,
>   Sachsen-Anhalt, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Schleswig-Holstein, Saarland and
>   Mittelthüringen) now give `get_departures` and the departure cards on
>   viafrei.de a live figure for buses, trams and the U-Bahn as well as trains, and
>   VBN's Connect timetable and realtime answer in Niedersachsen and Bremen. One figure per
>   departure, the one that agrees with where the departure is going, and every
>   feed that carried it credited ([example](#-real-answers)).
> - **Traffic strategies.** Lower Saxony's traffic strategies (DVL-NI, since 2.4.4)
>   and the Autobahn GmbH's strategic routes for Bayern (shown since 2.4.7) join its
>   national strategic routing in `check_autobahn_traffic`, `check_road_status` and
>   on the road card, each called what its publisher calls it: a guidance to the
>   trade-fair car parks is never said as a detour.
> - **Road entries name their junctions in the direction of travel**, and a lorry
>   park whose publisher gives a placeholder for a name is not given that as its
>   name.
> - **A traffic light and a map for every place** on viafrei.de: the motorway
>   page's rule applied to the place's own cards, every reason linked to its row and
>   drawn on a map of the place, one light per place. The map marks parking,
>   charging, stations and the weather ring by kind, and each mark links to its row.
> - **Streets on the maps.** The place, station and motorway maps draw
>   OpenStreetMap's streets as thin lines under their marks, with the line
>   "Streets: © OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL 1.0" and our offer of the street
>   database beside it ([SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md#and-the-streets-on-viafreides-maps)).
> - **A search that finds what you type.** The place search on viafrei.de finds
>   districts, postcodes, streets, a street and house number typed without a town
>   ("Wilhelmshöher Allee 100") and points of interest by name. An address you pick
>   heads the page with the address, never with a shop at its door, and a point of
>   interest you pick is the place, under its own name.
> - **Station pages for every railway station**, 6,513 of them, including those
>   DB's directory does not list, with filters for the board (mode, departures or
>   arrivals, platform, destination, time, disruptions, step-free), every lift and
>   escalator listed, the place cards and the place traffic light for the
>   station's surroundings, and a home-page block of the stations most affected now.
>   A slow part of a station page loads in place; the page itself never fails for it.
> - **Police and Land traffic messages in your language** on viafrei.de's
>   translated pages, machine-translated on our own server and labelled as ours,
>   with the German original beside them. Baden-Württemberg's messages stay German
>   only, because its terms bind them to the traffic-warning service's rules.
> - **Your language, once.** A visitor who arrives on a German page is sent to the
>   same page in their browser's language, and a choice in the language menu ends
>   the switching for good. The [connect page](https://viafrei.de/en/connect) gives
>   every assistant its steps, links its official guide and says how each was
>   checked.
>
> No tool, prompt or resource was added, removed or renamed since 2.4.3. The 2.4.0
> to 2.4.3 releases brought the five-question `entry` on every road item, charging
> by operator and power band, truck-parking occupancy behind the user's acceptance,
> and the [station and exit pages](#-station-and-exit-pages); the
> [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md) has the whole list. Every source is listed, with what it
> feeds and what we hold back, in [SOURCES.md](SOURCES.md).

# mcpserver — agent-tools.cloud directory + MCP discovery

The server that powers [agent-tools.cloud](https://agent-tools.cloud) — an open
directory of **x402 paid services** with a free MCP discovery endpoint.
Also listed on [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/kangletian/agent-tools-x402-directory).

> **Note (2026-05-25):** the previously hosted paid Qwen3.6 relay and the paid
> vertical endpoints (signal / onchain / defi / portfolio) were retired after
> 30 days of zero external conversions. This repository now serves the
> directory site and the free MCP discovery server only.

## What this serves today

| Path | Auth | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /` (host = `agent-tools.cloud`) | free | Directory site (search / browse) |
| `GET /api/v1/search` | free | Faceted service search |
| `POST /api/v1/ask` | free, rate-limited | LLM-ranked recommendations grounded in directory candidates |
| `GET /api/v1/services/{slug}` | free | Service card with payment, call and quality metadata |
| `GET /api/v1/categories`, `/api/v1/stats` | free | Directory facets and aggregate stats |
| `POST /api/v1/submit` | free, rate-limited | Pending service submission with dedupe |
| `POST /mcp-discovery/` | free | **MCP streamable-http** discovery server |
| `POST /a2a` | free | **A2A JSON-RPC** agent (`message/send`): directory search + MCP safety scan |
| `GET /healthz` | free | Liveness |
| `GET /v1/models` | free | Upstream model listing (read-only) |
| `GET /.well-known/agent-tools.json` | free | Agent discovery manifest |
| `GET /.well-known/x402` | free | x402 v0.4 self-description (free-only) |
| `GET /.well-known/mcp.json` | free | MCP self-description |

The MCP discovery server is also published as a standalone PyPI package:
[`agent-tools-mcp`](https://pypi.org/project/agent-tools-mcp/)
([repo](https://github.com/JoursBleu/agent-tools-mcp)).

## MCP discovery tools

```
search(intent, top_k=5, category=None, max_price_usd=None, has_mcp=None)
ask_services(intent, top_k=5, category=None, max_price_usd=None, use_llm=True)
get(slug)
list_categories()
stats()
search_mcp_servers(intent, top_k=5, chain=None, require_healthy=False)
get_mcp_server(slug)
search_a2a_agents(intent, top_k=5, x402_only=False)
search_resources(intent, protocol=None, top_k=10)
scan_mcp_safety(endpoint_url, name="", description="", tools_text="")
register(url, name=None, description=None, mcp_url=None, category=None)
```

`search` accepts natural-language intent and ranks by FTS5 + popularity +
health. Each result carries a `match_reason` and a `confidence` score.
`ask_services` uses the same retrieval-first / LLM-rerank flow as `/api/v1/ask`.

`scan_mcp_safety` vets an MCP server (by endpoint URL) for malware /
prompt-injection lures before you connect: an already-indexed server returns our
latest stored verdict, an unknown one is probed live, scanned, and added to the
directory. The verdict comes from deterministic static rules (no code execution)
over the server's advertised name + description + tool docs. Rules cover
pipe-to-shell / base64-eval / PowerShell install cradles, bare-IP payload hosts,
prompt-injection phrasing, and MCP **tool-poisoning** coercion — "always call
this tool first", "before using any other tool you must…", hidden
`<IMPORTANT>` instructions, "list all API keys / include secrets in your
response", and coercion to read & forward `.key`/`.pem`/`.ssh`/`.env` files.
Source-code-oriented rules (SQL/command/code injection) are intentionally not
applied to natural-language descriptions to avoid false positives. Each live
call also runs a frontier-LLM second opinion as an advisory dimension.
It is also exposed as an A2A skill on `POST /a2a`. The hosted server carries the
full tool set above; the stdio `agent-tools-mcp` PyPI package ships the core
search tools only.

## Deploy

Production runs behind nginx (vhost: `agent-tools.cloud`).

```bash
cd <install-dir>
sudo git pull
sudo systemctl restart mcpserver
```

systemd units live in [`deploy/`](deploy/):

- `mcpserver.service` — the ASGI app (uvicorn, 127.0.0.1:9100)
- `agent-tools-crawl.{service,timer}` — 6h directory crawler
- `agent-tools-health.{service,timer}` — endpoint health checks

## Config

See [`.env.example`](.env.example). Required:

- `UPSTREAM_BASE_URL` / `UPSTREAM_API_KEY` — used by `/v1/models`
- `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_BASE_URL` / `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_API_KEY` / `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_MODEL` — LLM backend for `/api/v1/ask`
- `AGENT_TOOLS_SAFETY_BASE_URL` / `AGENT_TOOLS_SAFETY_API_KEY` / `AGENT_TOOLS_SAFETY_MODEL` — optional override for the `scan_mcp_safety` advisory LLM (falls back to the `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_*` backend)
- `AGENT_TOOLS_DB_PATH` — SQLite path for the directory
- `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` / `AGENT_TOOLS_ASK_RATE_LIMIT_PER_DAY` — public ask abuse limits
- `METRICS_BEARER_TOKEN` — optional remote access token for `/metrics`; without it metrics are local-only

## Smoke test

```bash
# Liveness
curl https://agent-tools.cloud/healthz

# Directory stats
curl https://agent-tools.cloud/api/v1/stats

# Intent-level service recommendation
curl -s -X POST https://agent-tools.cloud/api/v1/ask \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"find a weather API that accepts x402","limit":2}'

# Service card
curl https://agent-tools.cloud/api/v1/services/weather-hugen-tokyo-scan

# MCP discovery handshake
curl -s -X POST https://agent-tools.cloud/mcp-discovery/ \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -H 'accept: application/json, text/event-stream' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize",
       "params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},
                 "clientInfo":{"name":"smoke","version":"1"}}}'

# Retired paid path -> 404
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST \
  https://agent-tools.cloud/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"hi"}]}'
# => 404
```

# WaveSpeed MCP Server

  
    
    
  

An MCP server for the [WaveSpeed](https://wavespeed.ai) platform: run any model on the **live catalog** — image, video, audio, 3D — from Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, or any MCP client.

Built on the same design as the open-source [`@wavespeed/cli`](https://github.com/WaveSpeedAI/wavespeed-cli):

- **No hardcoded models for `run_model`.** The catalog comes from the live API (1h cache); new platform models work the day they ship.
- **One general verb, five shortcuts.** `run_model` executes anything; `get_model_schema` tells the agent what inputs a model actually accepts, so it reads before it writes. `generate_image`, `edit_image`, `generate_video`, `edit_video` and `extend_video` skip that: they use the same models as the [WaveSpeed /chat](https://wavespeed.ai/chat) page, pick the endpoint for what you give them and fit the request to its live schema.
- **Inputs are never mutated.** The one explicit transform is the `@path` marker — a `"@./photo.jpg"` value inside `input` uploads the file and substitutes its hosted URL. Bare paths are passed through untouched. The shortcut tools (`generate_image` etc.) are the exception: they pick the endpoint and fit the request to the model, and report what they changed in `notes`.
- **Quote before you spend.** `get_price` takes the same input as `run_model` and returns an estimate; the amount actually charged for a run is authoritative.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list_models` | Search the live catalog by text or modality type |
| `get_model_schema` | A model's real input schema (required, properties, defaults), with a link to the model's playground page |
| `run_model` | Submit + wait; rejects input keys the model doesn't accept; `@path` inputs upload automatically; returns output URLs |
| `generate_image` | Image from a prompt with the /chat image models (default Seedream 5 Pro); reference images use the model's edit endpoint |
| `edit_image` | Edit, restyle or combine existing images with the same models |
| `generate_video` | Video from a prompt, a first/last frame or reference images/videos/audio, with the /chat video models (default Seedance 2.5); the mode (text, image, reference) is picked from the inputs |
| `edit_video` | Edit an existing video, optionally with reference images/audio |
| `extend_video` | Continue an existing video with new footage |
| `get_price` | Cost estimate for the inputs you pass (no charge), with a link to the model's playground page |
| `get_balance` | Account credit balance, with the top-up link |
| `list_predictions` | Run history (default last 24h); filter by model, status, time range |
| `list_billings` | Itemized charges and refunds (needs a Billing-access key) |
| `get_usage` | Spend, request counts and per-model breakdown (default last 7 days; needs a Billing-access key) |
| `delete_predictions` | Delete finished runs from the history (up to 100; needs `confirm: true`, cannot be undone from here) |
| `upload_file` | Local file → hosted URL (24h content-hash dedupe) |
| `get_prediction` | Status/outputs of any run by id; optional `wait_seconds` to wait for it |

The five shortcut tools take `wait_seconds` like `run_model`, and `estimate_only: true` returns the price and the exact request that would run without submitting or charging anything. In their prompts, media is named `@image 1`, `@video 1`, `@audio 1` (in the order given); it is renamed to what each model expects. Models and defaults follow /chat: an unknown `model` is rejected, and a named model is never switched.

Some generations take minutes to hours. `run_model` submits the run and returns the prediction id right away (`done: false`); the assistant then calls `get_prediction` with that id and `wait_seconds` (max 1800) until `done` is `true`. The task keeps running server-side, so a dropped connection loses nothing. Pass `wait_seconds` to `run_model` to wait for a quick model in the same call. While waiting, both tools send MCP progress notifications that carry the prediction id.

## Setup

### Remote (nothing to install)

The same server is hosted at:

```text
https://api.wavespeed.ai/mcp
```

- **Claude on the web / ChatGPT:** add a custom connector with that address and approve the connection on the WaveSpeed page that opens. Approving creates a dedicated API key (named `MCP · <app>`) that you can delete on the [API Keys](https://wavespeed.ai/accesskey) page to disconnect.
- **Claude Code:** `claude mcp add --transport http wavespeed https://api.wavespeed.ai/mcp`
- **Cursor:**
  
    
      
      
    
  
- **VS Code:** `code --add-mcp '{"name":"wavespeed","type":"http","url":"https://api.wavespeed.ai/mcp"}'`
- **Any other client that sends request headers:** point it at the URL with `Authorization: Bearer <your API key>`.

The hosted server has the same tools, with one difference for files: it cannot read files on your computer, so pass public URLs, use `create_upload` from a tool that can send HTTP requests (it returns a temporary upload address and the `download_url` to use as an input), or, in ChatGPT, attach the file to the chat (the `upload_attachment` tool, which only ChatGPT can fill, imports it and returns a `download_url`). Full guide: [wavespeed.ai/docs/mcp](https://wavespeed.ai/docs/mcp).

### Local (npx)

`@latest` makes npx fetch the newest release on each start; without it, npx runs a globally installed `@wavespeed/mcp` if one exists, however old.

Auth resolves from `WAVESPEED_API_KEY`, or from the CLI's stored login (`wavespeed login`) — one login covers both tools. Keys: [wavespeed.ai/accesskey](https://wavespeed.ai/accesskey).

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add wavespeed -- npx -y @wavespeed/mcp@latest
```

**Claude Desktop / other clients** (`mcpServers` config):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wavespeed": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wavespeed/mcp@latest"],
      "env": { "WAVESPEED_API_KEY": "wsk_..." }
    }
  }
}
```

Accessible React components, blocks, templates, charts and themes for [shadcn/ui](https://ui.shadcn.com) and Tailwind CSS v4.

**Site:** https://ui.tealmac.com

This repository is for **bug reports, item requests and docs problems**. The components themselves are installed from the tealmac UI registry with the shadcn CLI, not from this repository.

## Install a free item

```bash
npx shadcn@latest add https://ui.tealmac.com/r/login-01.json
```

Or add the namespace once to `components.json`:

```json
{
  "registries": {
    "@tealmac": "https://ui.tealmac.com/r/{name}.json"
  }
}
```

then `npx shadcn@latest add @tealmac/login-01`.

## Pro

Pro items install from a private registry with your licence key. See [Set up Pro](https://ui.tealmac.com/docs/guides/pro) and [Pricing](https://ui.tealmac.com/pricing).

## For coding agents

tealmac UI has an MCP server, so your coding agent can search the catalogue and get the right install command: https://ui.tealmac.com/mcp-server

- [Bug report](../../issues/new?template=bug.yml): something is broken in an item or on the site.
- [Item request](../../issues/new?template=request.yml): a component, block or template you would like to see.
- [Docs problem](../../issues/new?template=docs.yml): something in the docs is wrong or unclear.

Licence keys, billing and anything private: email **hello@tealmac.com**. Please do not post licence keys in issues.

## Licence

Free items are free to use in personal and commercial projects. Pro items are covered by the [Pro licence](https://ui.tealmac.com/license/pro). See [License](https://ui.tealmac.com/license).

readme.markdown:
# archytan-mcp-gate

`archytan-mcp-gate` sits between an MCP host (Claude Code, Claude Desktop,
an IDE agent, your own agent) and an MCP tool server. Before any tool call
reaches the server, an [Archytan Lite](https://high-archy.tech/lite) gate
service has to authorize it. The MCP gate checks the signed receipt for that
decision and spends a single-use capability, and only then forwards the call.
A call the policy doesn't allow comes back to the agent as a tool error it
can read, and never reaches the server.

This repository is the MCP gate's source, under the Apache License 2.0. The
Archytan Lite gate service it talks to is a separate product, distributed as
a signed container image; its quickstart is in
[archytan-lite-community](https://github.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/archytan-lite-community).

## How it works

The host launches the MCP gate in place of the tool server, and the MCP gate
launches the server itself, so it becomes the only path between the agent
and its tools. For every `tools/call` it:

1. asks the Archytan Lite gate service to authorize the action the call maps
   to, on the resource the call names;
2. verifies the receipt the service returns: its fields must hash to the
   signed intent hash, the signature must be the service's key, and the
   receipt must describe exactly this call;
3. redeems the single-use capability that came with the ALLOW;
4. forwards the call to the tool server.

If any step fails, the call is refused and the server never sees it. The
agent never holds anything that could skip these steps: the MCP gate holds
the agent's credential, and the agent only ever speaks MCP.

## Requirements

- An Archytan Lite gate service with capabilities on
  (`ARCHYTAN_LITE_CAPABILITIES=on`). The tests run against version 2.7.0,
  the first whose policy can scope a role to named resources.
- A credential-bound caller for the agent, made with the service's
  `callergen`. The MCP gate never sends a role; the agent's role is whatever
  its credential holds.

## Install

Download the binary for your platform from this repository's
[releases](https://github.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/archytan-mcp-gate/releases).
`SHA256SUMS` covers every binary and is signed by the workflow that built
them, with [cosign](https://github.com/sigstore/cosign) keyless signing:

```sh
cosign verify-blob SHA256SUMS --bundle SHA256SUMS.cosign.bundle \
  --certificate-identity-regexp '^https://github.com/High-ArchyTech-Solutions/archytan-mcp-gate/\.github/workflows/release\.yml@refs/tags/v' \
  --certificate-oidc-issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com
sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing
```

Or build it yourself with Go:

```sh
go install github.com/high-archytech-solutions/archytan-mcp-gate/v2/cmd/archytan-mcp-gate@latest
```

Each release also attaches `archytan-mcp-gate.mcpb`, an
[MCP bundle](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/mcpb) for hosts that
install them, and lists it in the
[MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) as
`io.github.High-ArchyTech-Solutions/archytan-mcp-gate`. The host asks for
four things: an `mcp-gate.json` that names the tool server in its
`server` field (see [Configure](#configure)), the gate service's URL, the
agent's token file and the service's public key. The bundle carries the
builds for macOS and Linux on amd64 and arm64, and for Windows on amd64,
which Windows on Arm runs under emulation. `SHA256SUMS` covers it too.
The macOS builds aren't notarized by Apple, so macOS may refuse to run
one that arrived through a browser until you clear its quarantine
(`xattr -d com.apple.quarantine <file>`).

## Configure

Map each tool you want the agent to have to a policy action in
`mcp-gate.json`. `resource_id_arg` names the argument that identifies the
resource the call acts on:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "agent_uid": "agent-invoices",
  "tools": {
    "delete_invoice": { "action": "invoice.delete", "resource_type": "invoice", "resource_id_arg": "invoice_id" },
    "read_invoice":   { "action": "invoice.read",   "resource_type": "invoice", "resource_id_arg": "invoice_id" }
  }
}
```

Then point the host at the MCP gate instead of the tool server. The same
`mcpServers` entry works in Claude Desktop's `claude_desktop_config.json`
and a project's `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "invoices": {
      "command": "archytan-mcp-gate",
      "args": ["--config", "/etc/archytan/mcp-gate.json", "--", "node", "/opt/invoice-server/index.js"],
      "env": {
        "ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_URL": "https://gate.internal:8421",
        "ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_CALLER_TOKEN_PATH": "/etc/archytan/agent-invoices.token",
        "ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_PUBLIC_KEY_HEX": "<the gate service's receipt-signing public key>"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_URL` | Base URL of the Archytan Lite gate service. Plain `http` is accepted only to loopback, because every request carries the agent's credential. |
| `ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_CALLER_TOKEN_PATH` | File holding the agent's caller token. |
| `ARCHYTAN_MCP_GATE_PUBLIC_KEY_HEX` | The service's Ed25519 receipt-signing public key, in hex. Receipts signed by any other key are refused. |

The tool server can be named in `mcp-gate.json` instead of after `--`,
which suits a host or bundle that only lets you pass a config file:

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "agent_uid": "agent-invoices",
  "server": { "command": "node", "args": ["/opt/invoice-server/index.js"] },
  "tools": {
    "read_invoice": { "action": "invoice.read", "resource_type": "invoice", "resource_id_arg": "invoice_id" }
  }
}
```

The host's entry is then `"args": ["--config", "/etc/archytan/mcp-gate.json"]`.
The command runs exactly as written and inherits the MCP gate's
environment, the same as after `--`. Name the server in one place: with a
`server` in the config and a command after `--`, the MCP gate refuses to
start rather than pick one.

`mcp-gate.json` is read as strictly as host messages are. An unknown

> [!IMPORTANT] > **Active compatibility development.** Palo Alto Networks completed its Portkey acquisition on 2026‑05‑29 and now presents Portkey as the core of Prisma AIRS AI Gateway. The Portkey Admin API remains live, and its official OpenAPI and product changelog continued adding control-plane surfaces through October 2026; this project has therefore resumed API-coverage work. It targets the Portkey-compatible API (`x-portkey-api-key`), not Prisma AIRS/Strata Cloud Manager directly. Palo Alto now publishes a Prisma AIRS management specification, but it uses different authentication, multiple management bases, and a smaller domain set, so it is not a `PORTKEY_BASE_URL` swap. See the short [Prisma AIRS interoperability guide](./docs/PRISMA_AIRS_INTEROPERABILITY.md) for the supported side-by-side model and adapter criteria. # bowmark skill

<sub>**LM Studio** — GitHub strips a raw `lmstudio:` link, so this one is a paste, not a button. Copy it into your browser's address bar:</sub>

```
lmstudio://add_mcp?name=bowmark&config=eyJ1cmwiOiJodHRwczovL2FwaS5ib3dtYXJrLmFpL21jcC9iYWRnZS1sbXN0dWRpbyJ9
```

The skill for [Bowmark](https://bowmark.ai) — the web as callable functions. The agent reads a typed function library, writes a short script against it, and Bowmark runs it on the live sites.

```sh
npx skills add bowmark-ai/skill
```

Works on any host that supports the `SKILL.md` standard — **Claude Code, Codex** (which adopted the standard natively), Cursor, GitHub Copilot, OpenCode, and others.

The skill calls Bowmark's MCP server — wire that up at [bowmark.ai/#install](https://bowmark.ai/#install) or via [Smithery](https://smithery.ai/servers/bowmark-ai/bowmark).

**Want both in one step?** On Claude Code and Codex, install the plugin instead — it bundles this skill *and* auto-wires the MCP:

```sh
# Claude Code
claude plugin marketplace add bowmark-ai/plugin && claude plugin install bowmark@bowmark-ai
# Codex
codex plugin marketplace add bowmark-ai/plugin   # then `codex /plugins` to install
```

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `get_library` | Read the typed function library for a task or a site. Read-only, touches no site, and an unrecognized query returns the index rather than an error. |
| `run` | Execute a short async JavaScript script against the live sites and return `{ ok, result, logs, error, ms }`. |
| `report` | Tell Bowmark what it could not do, or which run came back wrong. Recorded as feedback; retries nothing. |

**No MCP client?** The same two calls are plain HTTP — `GET https://api.bowmark.ai/v1/library?query=…` and `POST https://api.bowmark.ai/v1/run`, both taking `Authorization: Bearer $BOWMARK_API_KEY`. The reference is [bowmark.ai/docs/api](https://bowmark.ai/docs/api); worked examples are at [bowmark.ai/docs/scripting#no-install-at-all](https://bowmark.ai/docs/scripting#no-install-at-all).

## OpenAI Apps (ChatGPT plugin) variant

The [ChatGPT Apps](https://platform.openai.com/plugins) submission takes a skill as a **ZIP or folder**, and its needs differ slightly from the general skill: the plugin always ships the MCP alongside the skill, and ChatGPT exposes the tools under bare names. So there's a tailored variant, **generated from this same canonical skill** — never hand-maintained:

- **Folder:** [`openai/bowmark/`](./openai/bowmark) — a content mirror of `bowmark/SKILL.md` with the trailing "Your API key" section and everything after it dropped (ChatGPT signs in by OAuth and cannot send a key), tool names rewritten to bare `get_library` / `run`, Claude-only frontmatter/tool-name references trimmed, and the three secret tools (`list_secrets`, `request_secret`, `get_secret_link`) replaced by the dashboard — the plugin's MCP is the ChatGPT directory connector, which does not offer them. That step refuses to build if the canonical wording moves out from under it. `build-openai.mjs` is the authority on what it cuts; this line described sections that have never existed in `bowmark/SKILL.md`, and a newcomer went looking for one.
- **ZIP:** [`openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip`](./openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip) — the same folder zipped, ready to drop straight into the ChatGPT "Skills" uploader. A **committed artifact** (not built in CI: the release runner has no `zip` binary), so it rides the mirror to `bowmark-ai/skill` at a stable raw URL like any other file.

Both are **generated** by [`build-openai.mjs`](./build-openai.mjs). Edit `bowmark/SKILL.md`, then regenerate and commit — never edit the `openai/` copies directly (CI's `check:openai` fails a PR whose text mirror is stale):

```sh
pnpm -F @bowmark/skill sync:openai        # regenerate openai/bowmark/SKILL.md
pnpm -F @bowmark/skill build:openai-zip    # rebuild openai/bowmark-openai-skill.zip (commit it)
```

readme.markdown:
# Wiro MCP Server

**Official [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) server for [Wiro AI](https://wiro.ai/)** — access all AI models on Wiro from Cursor, Claude, Windsurf, and any MCP-compatible AI assistant.

[Official MCP Server](https://wiro.ai/docs/wiro-mcp-server) · [Self-Hosted MCP](https://wiro.ai/docs/mcp-self-hosted) · [Models](https://wiro.ai/models) · [Dashboard](https://wiro.ai/panel) · [Docs](https://wiro.ai/docs)

## Quick Start

Local `npx` and library usage require Node.js 20 or later. The hosted MCP
endpoint does not require a local Node.js installation.

### 1. Get API Keys

Sign up at [wiro.ai](https://wiro.ai/) and create a project at [wiro.ai/panel/project/new](https://wiro.ai/panel/project/new) to get your API key and secret.

### 2. Add to Your AI Assistant

**Cursor** — open MCP settings (`Cmd+Shift+P` → "Open MCP settings") and add:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code:**

```bash
claude mcp add wiro -- npx -y @wiro-ai/wiro-mcp
```

Then set environment variables `WIRO_API_KEY` and `WIRO_API_SECRET`.

**Claude Desktop** — add to `claude_desktop_config.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Windsurf** — add to MCP settings:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "wiro": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@wiro-ai/wiro-mcp"],
      "env": {
        "WIRO_API_KEY": "your-api-key",
        "WIRO_API_SECRET": "your-api-secret"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**OpenClaw** — configure a remote server under `mcp.servers`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "wiro": {
        "url": "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1",
        "transport": "streamable-http",
        "connectionTimeoutMs": 10000,
        "headers": {
          "Authorization": "Bearer ${WIRO_MCP_AUTH}"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Set `WIRO_MCP_AUTH` in OpenClaw's environment, then verify with
`openclaw mcp doctor wiro --probe`. On older OpenClaw releases without that
probe command, use `openclaw mcp show wiro`, restart OpenClaw, and run
`/tools verbose`.

**Hermes** — add to `~/.hermes/config.yaml`:

```yaml
mcp_servers:
  wiro:
    url: "https://mcp.wiro.ai/v1"
    headers:
      Authorization: "Bearer ${WIRO_MCP_AUTH}"
    timeout: 60
    connect_timeout: 10
```

Store `WIRO_MCP_AUTH` in `~/.hermes/.env`, then run `/reload-mcp` and `/tools`.

### 3. Start Using

Ask your AI assistant:

- *"Generate a photorealistic image of a mountain lake at sunset"*
- *"What video generation models are available on Wiro?"*
- *"Show me the parameters for openai/sora-2"*
- *"Create a 5-second video with Kling V3 — a drone shot over mountains"*
- *"Check the status of my last task"*
- *"Show my latest productions and open the newest result"*

## Authentication

Wiro supports two authentication types (chosen when creating a project):

### Signature-Based (Recommended)

More secure. Requires both API key and API secret.

```
WIRO_API_KEY=your-api-key
WIRO_API_SECRET=your-api-secret
```

### API Key Only

Simpler. Only requires the API key. Omit `WIRO_API_SECRET` from your config.

```
WIRO_API_KEY=your-api-key
```

## Available Tools

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `search_models` | Search and browse AI models by keyword, category, or owner |
| `get_model_schema` | Get full parameter schema and pricing for any model |
| `recommend_model` | Describe what you want to build, get model recommendations by relevance |
| `explore` | Browse curated models organized by category — no parameters needed |
| `run_model` | Run any model — waits up to 45s by default, then returns a recoverable task token |
| `wait_for_task` | Continue waiting for an existing task without submitting or billing a duplicate run |
| `get_task` | Check task status immediately or wait up to 45s with `wait_seconds` |
| `list_tasks` | Browse authenticated task history across conversations, then continue with `get_task` |
| `get_task_price` | Get the cost of a completed task |
| `cancel_task` | Cancel a queued task |
| `kill_task` | Kill a running task |
| `upload_file` | Upload a file from URL for use as model input |
| `search_docs` | Search the Wiro documentation for guides and API references |

For long generations, `run_model` returns the existing task ID and token when its
wait budget expires. The assistant must continue with `wait_for_task`; retrying
`run_model` creates a separate billable task.

### LLM-friendly responses

All tools publish typed MCP input and output schemas. Successful calls return
`structuredContent` for reliable chaining, concise text `content` for clients
that only render text, and MCP resource links for generated media.
Model parameters remain catalog-driven: `json` and `json-array` fields are sent
as structured values in the same `run_model.params` object as all other inputs.
Use `get_model_schema` as the source of truth for continuation fields.
`previousTaskToken` is the single continuation reference. Send it with exactly
one new `prompt` or non-empty `messages` value for a stateful next turn, or with
`toolOutputs` for a tool-result continuation.

LLM task outputs preserve the public Task Detail segment names and casing:
`thinking`, `answer`, `function_call`, and `custom_tool_call`, including
`call_id`, `finishreason`, and optional normalized token `usage`.
Only validated fields are projected into structured MCP output. When segments
are present, `response` is derived from ordered `answer` segments instead of
raw debug transport; tasks without a typed projection retain their normal
`debugoutput` response.

Completed tool calls return a continuation template in the existing
`next
