readme.markdown:
# ElfDeckAI

**Let an AI play games on your Steam Deck.**

ElfDeckAI gives an AI assistant such as Claude a virtual controller,
keyboard and mouse on your Steam Deck, plus the ability to see the screen.
The AI looks at the game, decides what to do, and presses the buttons
itself. It works in both Gaming Mode and Desktop Mode, and on other Linux
machines too.

## Start here: Steam Deck (about 5 minutes)

You need a Steam Deck, and a PC on the same Wi-Fi with an AI app that
supports MCP, such as [Claude Desktop](https://claude.ai/download).

**1. Install on the Deck.** Switch the Deck to Desktop Mode (Steam button →
Power → Switch to Desktop), open **Konsole**, and paste:

```sh
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Garthnesss/ElfDeckAI/main/install-on-deck.sh | sh
```

At the end it prints the Deck's IP address. Keep it for step 3.

**2. Turn on SSH on the Deck** (once), so your PC can reach it. In the same
Konsole window:

```sh
passwd                            # choose a password for the Deck, if you haven't
sudo systemctl enable --now sshd
```

**3. Connect your PC.** On the PC, paste one line. It asks for the Deck's IP
address and its password (once), then sets everything up, including
Claude Desktop.

- **Windows** (in PowerShell):
  ```powershell
  irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Garthnesss/ElfDeckAI/main/setup-pc.ps1 | iex
  ```
- **Mac or Linux** (in Terminal):
  ```sh
  curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Garthnesss/ElfDeckAI/main/setup-pc.sh | sh
  ```

**4. Try it.** Restart Claude Desktop and ask: *"Take a screenshot of my
Steam Deck."* When you see your Deck's screen, start a game and ask the AI
to play.

**Tips**

- Turn-based games, RPGs, puzzles and menus work best. The AI needs a
  second or more per move, so fast action games are out of reach.
- In Gaming Mode, if a game ignores the AI's controller, ask the AI to make
  its controller **Player 1**. It knows how, using Steam's Reorder
  Controllers menu while the game runs.
- Something not working? Give [AI_SETUP_GUIDE.md](AI_SETUP_GUIDE.md) to
  your AI and ask it to help. It covers setup and troubleshooting step by
  step.

## How it works

Three small programs on the Deck create virtual input devices through the
Linux kernel's `/dev/uinput`, so games and Steam see them as real hardware:

- **ElfKey**: a virtual keyboard
- **ElfPad**: a virtual Xbox 360-class gamepad (buttons, analog triggers,
  two sticks, D-pad)
- **ElfMouse**: a virtual mouse, which can also click an exact point on
  the screen

A fourth program, an MCP server, exposes them, together with a screenshot
tool, as tools any MCP client can call. Your PC's AI app starts that server
on the Deck over SSH. Nothing depends on a particular game or emulator:
ElfDeckAI has played Pokémon FireRed in RetroArch on a physical Steam Deck,
from the intro through the first rival battle, with the agent seeing only
screenshots. See [notes/driving.md](notes/driving.md) for what was learned.

Everything is single-file Python using only the standard library, and the
Deck install needs no sudo.

## Other Linux machines

```sh
pip install elfdeckai

elfkey &
elfpad &
elfmouse &

echo "key x 150"     > /tmp/elfkey.fifo     # tap X for 150 ms
echo "press a"       > /tmp/elfpad.fifo     # tap A
echo "move 300 -100" > /tmp/elfmouse.fifo   # move the pointer
echo "click left"    > /tmp/elfmouse.fifo   # left click

grep -E "ElfKey|ElfPad|ElfMouse" /proc/bus/input/devices   # confirm the devices exist
```

Without pip, clone the repository and run `python3 elfkey.py` (and so on)
directly. Runtime state lives in `/tmp` and is cleared on reboot.

`/dev/uinput` is user-writable on the Steam Deck by default. On other
distributions, install the udev rule first (see [Installation](#installation)).

## MCP server

`elfdeckai-mcp` is a Model Context Protocol server (stdio transport) that
exposes 22 tools:

| Group | Tools |
|---|---|
| Keyboard | `key_tap`, `key_down`, `key_up`, `key_release` |
| Gamepad | `pad_press`, `pad_down`, `pad_up`, `pad_stick`, `pad_trigger`, `pad_center`, `pad_reset` |
| Mouse | `mouse_click_at`, `mouse_move_to`, `mouse_move`, `mouse_click`, `mouse_down`, `mouse_up`, `mouse_scroll`, `mouse_hscroll`, `mouse_release` |
| Vision | `screenshot` |
| Timing | `wait` |

`screenshot` captures the screen of the machine the server runs on and
returns a PNG, so an agent can work in a look, act, look again loop
without a separate video stream. It supports the Steam Deck in both Gaming
Mode (through gamescope) and Desktop Mode (KDE Plasma), wlroots compositors
and X11. Screens larger than
1280 pixels on their long side are scaled down before sending (set
`ELFDECKAI_SCREENSHOT_MAX` to change the limit, or `0` to turn it off), and
the result includes the image's size.

`mouse_click_at` and `mouse_move_to` take coordinates in the pixels of the
most recent screenshot, so an agent can click exactly what it sees, whatever
the screen's real resolution or the scaling applied. They assume a single
display.

Running on the same machine as the daemons:

```json
{"mcpServers": {"elfdeckai": {"command": "elfdeckai-mcp"}}}
```

Running on a Steam Deck from an AI client on your PC, over SSH (the
`setup-pc` scripts in [Start here](#start-here-steam-deck-about-5-minutes)
write this for you):

```json
{"mcpServers": {"elfdeckai": {
    "command": "ssh",
    "args": ["-i", "~/.ssh/elfdeckai_ed25519", "-o", "IdentitiesOnly=yes",
             "-o", "BatchMode=yes", "deck@DECK-IP-ADDRESS", ".local/bin/elfdeckai-mcp"]}}}
```

It logs in with an SSH key, because the MCP client cannot answer a password
prompt. Without pip, use
`"command": "python3", "args": ["/path/to/elfdeckai_mcp.py"]`.

Every tool call is validated against the tool's schema and the daemon's
own parser before anything is written to a FIFO. If a daemon is not
running, the call returns an error immediately instead of blocking.

| Command | Effect |

readme.markdown:
# ThreadMine MCP Server

> ThreadMine is a Java thread dump analyzer with AI — detects deadlocks, CPU spikes, pool exhaustion and virtual thread pinning. Free online, no signup.

Official [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for [ThreadMine](https://threadmine.dev). Paste a JVM thread dump into your AI assistant — Claude Code, Claude Desktop or Cursor — and get back the detected problems, a health score and a link to the full interactive report, without leaving the chat.

**No account needed.** Without an API key the server uses the same public endpoint as the [threadmine.dev](https://threadmine.dev) analyzer. With a key, analyses land in your ThreadMine workspace.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `analyze_thread_dump` | Uploads a thread dump (inline text or file path) and returns detected problems, health score (0-100) and the report link |
| `get_analysis` | Fetches a previous analysis by the id `analyze_thread_dump` returned. Read-only, consumes nothing |

## Setup

**Claude Code plugin** (MCP server plus a skill that tells Claude when to use it)

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add maschiojv/threadmine-mcp
claude plugin install threadmine@threadmine-plugins
```

**Claude Code, server only**

```bash
claude mcp add threadmine -- npx -y @threadmine/mcp
```

**Claude Desktop / Cursor** (`claude_desktop_config.json` / `.cursor/mcp.json`)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "threadmine": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@threadmine/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

## With or without an account

| | Without an API key | With `THREADMINE_API_KEY` |
|---|---|---|
| Limit | 5 analyses per hour, 20 per day, per IP | Your plan's quota ([pricing](https://threadmine.dev/en/pricing)) |
| Report | Public link (`threadmine.dev/resultado/...`), anyone with it can open it, expires after 7 days | Private, in your workspace |

To use your account, create an API key in the [web app](https://app.threadmine.dev) (**Settings → API Keys**) and set `THREADMINE_API_KEY` in the server's environment. For the plugin, export it in the shell that starts Claude Code; for the other setups, add it to the `env` block (`"env": { "THREADMINE_API_KEY": "tf_live_xxx" }`) or pass `-e THREADMINE_API_KEY=tf_live_xxx` to `claude mcp add`.

## Usage

Ask your assistant things like:

- *"Analyze this thread dump: `<paste>`"*
- *"Run the dump at /tmp/threaddump.txt through ThreadMine"*
- *"My Spring Boot app stopped answering, here's the jstack output"*
- *"What did analysis `<id>` find? Any deadlocks?"*

## Privacy

The dump is sent to the ThreadMine API over TLS. Thread dumps can carry hostnames, class and package names and SQL fragments. If your policy forbids sending production dumps to a third party, run them through [tm-anon](https://github.com/maschiojv/threadmine-anonymizer) first: it anonymizes the dump locally, keeps the mapping on your machine, and ThreadMine still analyzes the result.

## Notes

- `THREADMINE_API_URL` overrides the API endpoint (self-hosted / staging). `THREADMINE_SITE_URL` overrides the site used in anonymous report links.
- Requires Node.js ≥ 20.

## License

MIT

readme.markdown:
# CommerceBook for agents

Sell or buy on CommerceBook from an agent. CommerceBook (https://commercebook.ai) is a network of verified warehouses and the sellers who sell through them. The first useful call costs nothing:

- **To buy:** post a standing request with a ceiling. Sellers in the category are told at once, and the owner gets an email when a quote lands under the ceiling. Nothing is bought until a quote is accepted.
- **To sell:** post a standing offer, a product with its price and count. Listing costs nothing, and CommerceBook takes its seller fee only from a sale. Each new public request in a live product's category arrives by email.
- **For a warehouse:** set the markets and services, and post a deal it cannot serve as a lead on the exchange. Posting costs nothing.

```sh
npx -y @commercebook/mcp        # MCP server: the market and the requests with no key
npm install @commercebook/sdk   # TypeScript
pip install commercebook        # Python
```

Or connect an agent host to the remote MCP server at https://commercebook.ai/mcp (Streamable HTTP). No key is needed to read the market.

## The skills

Three skills in the Agent Skills format. Each is a folder with a SKILL.md that an agent runtime loads by its description.

| Skill | Loads when the principal asks to | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| sell-on-commercebook | find more places to sell, sell surplus inventory | [skills/sell-on-commercebook/SKILL.md](skills/sell-on-commercebook/SKILL.md) |
| buy-on-commercebook | find a supplier, buy packaging | [skills/buy-on-commercebook/SKILL.md](skills/buy-on-commercebook/SKILL.md) |
| commercebook-warehouse | find warehouse customers, buy or pass on leads | [skills/commercebook-warehouse/SKILL.md](skills/commercebook-warehouse/SKILL.md) |

Copy a skill folder into the agent's skills folder, for example `~/.claude/skills/` for Claude Code. Each SKILL.md is also served raw from GitHub at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/errc02/commercebook-agents/main/skills/<skill>/SKILL.md`.

## A buyer in five lines

```ts
import { CommerceBook } from '@commercebook/sdk';

const cb = new CommerceBook({ key: process.env.COMMERCEBOOK_API_KEY });
const found = await cb.searchProducts({ q: 'stretch film', max_price: 3000 });
const r = await cb.postRequest({ title: 'Stretch film, 18 inch, 80 gauge', category: 'packaging', qty: 40, ceiling_unit_cents: 2400 });
```

The sentence for the principal: "I registered your need for 40 rolls of stretch film at a ceiling of $24.00 a roll, at no cost. You get an email when a quote lands under it."

## A key

Reading the market needs no key. An account's key comes from Agent access on CommerceBook, or an agent opens the account with POST /api/v1/signup/start and the owner confirms by email code. Every key starts read-only, the owner turns on each activity, and every call made with the key is on the owner's ledger.

## What is in this repository

| Folder | Package | What it is |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [packages/mcp](packages/mcp) | `@commercebook/mcp` on npm | The MCP server, local (stdio) and the same tools as https://commercebook.ai/mcp |
| [packages/sdk](packages/sdk) | `@commercebook/sdk` on npm | The TypeScript client, typed from the OpenAPI document |
| [packages/python](packages/python) | `commercebook` on PyPI | The Python client, with TypedDicts from the OpenAPI document |
| [skills](skills) | | The three skills |
| [openapi.json](openapi.json) | | A copy of https://commercebook.ai/api/v1/openapi.json, the contract |

The npm packages are workspaces of this repository: `npm install` at the root links them, and `npm run build --workspaces` builds both.

## The briefings

The buyer, seller and warehouse briefings describe every call and the rules: https://commercebook.ai/docs/briefing/buyer.md, https://commercebook.ai/docs/briefing/seller.md and https://commercebook.ai/docs/briefing/warehouse.md. The policies: https://commercebook.ai/policies.

## Contributing and security

Contributions: see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Security reports go to support@commercebook.ai, see [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

## Licence

MIT, see [LICENSE](LICENSE).

readme.markdown:
# Layerre MCP Server

A [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for [Layerre](https://layerre.com).
Let your AI assistant turn Canva designs into reusable templates, edit layers, and render
PNG / JPEG / WebP / PDF images from data.

Docs: **[layerre.com/docs/mcp](https://layerre.com/docs/mcp/)**

## Features

- Import a Canva share link as an editable template
- Read and update template layers (text, images, positions, styling)
- Generate image/PDF variants with per-layer overrides, singly or in bulk
- Remote server with browser OAuth sign-in, or API key / local stdio

## Quick start

### Remote server (recommended)

Endpoint: `https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp` (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 + PKCE).

**Cursor** — `~/.cursor/mcp.json`

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "layerre": { "url": "https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp" } } }
```

**Claude Code**

```bash
claude mcp add --transport http layerre https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp
```

**VS Code** — `.vscode/mcp.json`

```json
{ "servers": { "layerre": { "type": "http", "url": "https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp" } } }
```

**Claude Desktop / Claude.ai** — Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector → `https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp`

**Windsurf** — `~/.codeium/windsurf/mcp_config.json`

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "layerre": { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp" } } }
```

Your client opens a browser window to sign in to Layerre and approve access.

### API key (headless / CI)

Create a key in the Layerre dashboard (Settings → API keys), then:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "layerre": {
      "url": "https://mcp.layerre.com/mcp",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer lyr_xxxxxxxx_xxxxxxxx" }
    }
  }
}
```

### Local (stdio)

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "layerre": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@layerre/mcp-server"],
      "env": { "LAYERRE_API_KEY": "lyr_xxxxxxxx_xxxxxxxx" }
    }
  }
}
```

## Tools

| Tool | Description | Type |
|------|-------------|------|
| `layerre_auth_status` | Check authentication status | read |
| `layerre_list_templates` | List templates (filter by tag, paginate) | read |
| `layerre_get_template` | Get a template with its layers | read |
| `layerre_list_template_tags` | List tags/folders with counts | read |
| `layerre_create_template` | Create a template from a Canva share URL | write |
| `layerre_update_template` | Update name, size, backgrounds, tags | write |
| `layerre_create_layer` | Add a text or image layer | write |
| `layerre_get_layer` | Get a layer | read |
| `layerre_update_layer` | Update a layer | write |
| `layerre_list_variants` | List generated variants | read |
| `layerre_get_variant` | Get a variant | read |
| `layerre_create_variant` | Render one image/PDF with overrides | write |
| `layerre_create_variants_bulk` | Render up to 25 variants in one call | write |

Example prompts:

- "Import https://www.canva.com/design/... as a Layerre template tagged `social`."
- "Generate a PNG of my 'Event Card' template with the title set to 'Launch Day'."

## Development

See [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md).

## Privacy & support

[Privacy policy](https://layerre.com/privacy) · [Terms](https://layerre.com/terms) · hello@layerre.com

## License

[MIT](./LICENSE)

readme.markdown:
# Mothership MCP server

[Mothership](https://www.mothership.com) is a freight marketplace for LTL, truckload and local freight. Its MCP server connects your AI assistant to your Mothership account, so you can get rates, track and cancel shipments, find freight classes and check your bills by asking in plain language.

The server is at `https://mcp.mothership.com` and speaks Streamable HTTP. You sign in with your Mothership account over OAuth 2.1, and the assistant sees only what your account can see. The [official MCP Registry](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io) lists it as `com.mothership/mothership`.

This repo also holds the Mothership plugin for Claude, ChatGPT, Codex and Cursor, which adds Mothership's skills to the server. See [Plugins](#plugins).

## What it can do

With the server connected, your assistant can:

- Quote LTL, truckload and local freight. It shows each carrier's price and delivery date, with a link to book the rate you pick in the Mothership dashboard. Every quote it gets is saved to your account.
- Track a shipment by its Mothership reference, PRO, BOL or pickup number, or your own reference: status, pickup and delivery windows, carrier, cargo, documents and the newest tracking updates.
- Find, list and count your shipments by date, status or carrier.
- Cancel a shipment. It shows the cancellation fee and refund first, and cancels only after you confirm.
- Find the NMFC item for what you ship, read an item's freight classes, and estimate a class from weight and dimensions.
- Check whether Mothership serves an address, and whether it's residential or limited access.
- Show your invoices, rebills, payment methods and billing details.
- Start freight claims, follow them, and accept or rebut a claim decision.
- Keep your address book, invite and manage teammates, and set up webhooks.
- Search Mothership's help articles and your support conversations.

In clients that support [MCP Apps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps), such as Claude and ChatGPT, quotes and shipments can show as cards.

## Connect

Any MCP client that supports remote servers with OAuth can connect to `https://mcp.mothership.com`. The first time it connects, it opens a Mothership sign-in page, and you approve the client's access. You need a Mothership account. If you don't have one, sign up at https://dashboard.mothership.com/signup.

Clients identify themselves with a Client ID Metadata Document, as Claude, ChatGPT and VS Code do. The server doesn't support dynamic client registration. Cursor signs in with a client ID that Mothership set up for it.

### Claude

In claude.ai or the Claude desktop app, add Mothership as a custom connector. On Free, Pro and Max plans:

1. Go to **Customize > Connectors**, select **+ Add**, then **Add custom connector**.
2. Enter `Mothership` as the name and `https://mcp.mothership.com` as the URL, and select **Continue**.
3. Keep the authentication settings Claude detects. Under **OAuth client**, leave **Use Claude's published identity** selected, since Mothership doesn't support **Register automatically**.
4. Select **Add**, then sign in with your Mothership account.

On Team and Enterprise plans, an Owner adds the connector from **Organization settings > Connectors** with **Add > Custom > Web**. Each member then connects it from **Customize > Connectors** and signs in with their own Mothership account. See [Anthropic's guide to custom connectors](https://support.claude.com/en/articles/11175166-getting-started-with-custom-connectors-using-remote-mcp).

### ChatGPT

1. Go to [Plugins](https://chatgpt.com/plugins), select **+**, then **Add custom MCP server**.
2. Enter a name and description. Under **Connection**, choose **Public endpoint** and enter `https://mcp.mothership.com`.
3. Choose OAuth for authentication, accept the risk warning, and select **Create as a plugin**.
4. Sign in with your Mothership account.

Your workspace's policies decide who can add a custom MCP server. ChatGPT keeps the tool list it found when you added the server, so when Mothership adds tools, open the server in Plugins and select **Refresh**. See [OpenAI's guide](https://developers.openai.com/apps-sdk/deploy/connect-chatgpt).

### VS Code

Open the Command Palette, run **MCP: Add Server**, choose **HTTP (HTTP or Server-Sent Events)**, enter `https://mcp.mothership.com`, and give the server the ID `mothership`. For a personal setup, choose **Global**, then **Copilot Global**. VS Code asks you to sign in with your Mothership account the first time the server starts. See [VS Code's MCP guide](https://code.visualstudio.com/docs/copilot/customization/mcp-servers).

### Cursor

Add Mothership to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for every project, or to `.cursor/mcp.json` in one project:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "Mothership": {
      "url": "https://mcp.mothership.com",
      "auth": { "CLIENT_ID": "cursor" }
    }
  }
}
```

`CLIENT_ID` names the OAuth client Mothership set up for Cursor, because the server has no dynamic client registration. Sign in with your Mothership account when Cursor asks. See [Cursor's MCP guide](https://cursor.com/docs/context/mcp).

### Other clients

Other clients can connect with the same URL if they support OAuth with a Client ID Metadata Document. A client that only supports dynamic client registration can't sign in.

## Plugins

The [`mothership`](plugins/mothership) plugin connects to the same server and adds Mothership's skills. Skills are instructions that teach the assistant how to get started, quote, track and cancel shipments, explain rebills, check locations and find freight classes. The assistant loads them like its own skills. Without the plugin, the server serves the same skills through its `skill-get` tool.

Claude Code:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add mothership/agent-plugins
claude plugin install mothership@mothership
```
